body.translated_text: Now we shall speak of the application in the ritual performance (<s>vitāna</s>) of this traditional text (<s>samāmnāya</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
He states the <s>vaitānika</s> (ritual-fire-related) [rites] beginning with the establishment of the sacred fires (<s>agnyādheya</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
But we shall first explain the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices (<s>darśapūrṇamāsau</s>), because the system (<s>tantra</s>) is taught there. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

At the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, when the oblation materials are near, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), having been invited, standing to the east-north of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), facing east, wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), having sipped water (<s>ācamya</s>), turning to the right, proceeds to the designated place (<s>vihāra</s>), passing to the east of the heap of discarded material (<s>utkara</s>) and to the west of the water-vessel (<s>praṇītāḥ</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Passing to the west of the fuel (<s>idhma</s>) when the water-vessel has not been brought forward. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Passing by the sacrificial pit (<s>cātvāla</s>) in [rites] that have a sacrificial pit. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
This is called the ford (<s>tīrtha</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
His regular movements are eastward. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And the bearing of the limbs [is eastward]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And [both apply] with regard to the sacred thread and purification. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And there is no departure from the designated place [except] if there is a ritual act [to be performed elsewhere]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
When a single limb is mentioned, one should understand [it to be] the right one. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
[This applies] when there is no [specific] directive. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In an injunction of ritual action, [the reference is to] the <s>Hotṛ</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'He gives' — [this refers to] the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'He offers,' 'he recites' — in expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>), [the reference is to] the <s>Brahman</s> (the supervising priest). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
[When only] a verse (<s>ṛc</s>) [is mentioned, it is understood] by the citation of a quarter (<s>pāda</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
A hymn (<s>sūkta</s>) [is understood from] the beginning of the hymn, [or] when a quarter is deficient. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
When [the quarter] is in excess, a <s>tṛca</s> (group of three verses) [is understood] everywhere. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Recitations (<s>japa</s>), accompanying formulas (<s>anumantraṇa</s>), blessings (<s>āpyāyana</s>), and praises (<s>upasthāna</s>) are [performed] in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And <s>mantras</s> that effect the ritual act [are also performed in a low voice]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
An exception [to a general rule] based on specific context (<s>prasaṅga</s>) is stronger [than the general rule]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having approached, placing the heel evenly at the northern hip of the <s>vedi</s> (altar) with the foot that is extended further forward, stepping on the sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>) with the front of the foot, holding both hands together, with the ring finger [extended] toward the sky, [held] at heart-level or at lap-level, gazing at the juncture of heaven and earth. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
This is the position of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Or a seated [position] — being thus constituted everywhere. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Something different [is done only] by [specific] directive. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
When directed, he recites [the following]: (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'Homage to the teacher, homage to the overseer, homage to the instructor. Who will recite this? He will recite this. May six broad [spaces] protect me from distress: heaven and earth, day and night, water and plants. May speech be well-established. May the sacrifice be auspicious. I take refuge in the metres. I [declare] myself — let him state his own name — in the past and future, in what is born and what is to be born, I partake. The impure [element] of speech — carry it away!' — Having drawn back the tips of the fingers — 'O <s>Jātavedas</s>, delight the animals in me' — let him rejoin [with the formula]. 'May heaven and earth be my armor, may <s>Agni</s> be [my] armor, may <s>Sūrya</s> be [my] armor, may the cross-beams be my armor. May I first attain [the power] of speech today.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having completed [the preliminary recitation], he recites (<s>anvāha</s>) the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>) (Commentary: He should recite along.)
Having made the syllable '<s>hiṃ</s>' — he recites '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar om</s>.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
This is the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (the prefatory '<s>hiṃ</s>' syllable). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
<s>Kautsa</s> [holds that] having recited '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>' alone, he makes the '<s>hiṃ</s>.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And he does not recite the prior recitation [in that case]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Now the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses [are]: '<s>pra vo vājā abhidyavaḥ</s>'; '<s>agna ā yāhi vītaye</s>'; '<s>gṛṇāna īḷenyo namasyaḥ</s>'; '<s>tiraḥ</s>'; '<s>agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe</s>'; '<s>samidhyamāno adhvare</s>'; '<s>samiddho agna āhuta</s>' — [this last one recited] twice. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
These should be recited in a single continuous monotone (<s>ekaśruti</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The single monotone (<s>ekaśrutya</s>) is the extreme proximity of the <s>udātta</s> (high), <s>anudātta</s> (low), and <s>svarita</s> (circumflex) [accents]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Making the <s>oṃkāra</s> — from the beginning of the [preceding] verse to the end — three <s>mātrās</s> long, ending with the sound '<s>m</s>' — he should connect [it] to the half-verse of the next [verse]. That is the continuous [recitation]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
This is the conclusion [of a verse]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The taking up of the next [verse] [ensures] non-confusion. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
At the completion [of the entire set], the conclusion is with the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>oṃ</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Four <s>mātrās</s> at the conclusion. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Its merging into the end [occurs]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Among the stops (<s>sparśas</s>), [the nasal merges into] the last [consonant] of its own class. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Among the semi-vowels (<s>antasthās</s>), [the nasal merges into] the respective nasal of each. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In [the case of] <s>repha</s> and the sibilants (<s>ūṣmans</s>), [the nasal becomes] <s>anusvāra</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Three times the first [verse] and the last, he recites with the half-repetition (<s>adhyardhakāra</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having recited one and a half [times], he should connect; then [he recites] the [remaining] two [verses]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Two [verses first] in the first [position], the last; then one and a half. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
These [become] fifteen through repetition. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

By this [procedure are governed] the <s>śastra</s> (recitation), <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), <s>nigada</s> (spoken formula), <s>anuvacana</s> (secondary recitation), <s>abhiṣṭavana</s> (praise), and <s>saṃstavana</s> (chant of praise). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

But elsewhere [there is] no half-repetition, no preliminary recitation before the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s>, and no repetition of the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> — in [rites with] few [verses], by default. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Not at the beginning of a section (<s>avaccheda</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s>-priests alone, only in the <s>śastras</s> (recitations). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

After the final <s>praṇava</s> of the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>, [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] concludes with the <s>nigada</s> (spoken formula): '<s>agne mahān asi brāhmaṇa bhārata</s>' ('O <s>Agni</s>, you are great, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>'). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
He selects the <s>ārṣeyas</s> (seer-lineage names) of the sacrificer, as many as there are. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The most remote [ancestor] first, in sequence. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
For [those in] priestly office (<s>paurohitya</s>) — the [lineages] of the king and the people. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Or the royal sages for [sacrificers who are] kings. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In case of doubt, all are [called] <s>Mānava</s> (descendants of <s>Manu</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having concluded with: 'Kindled by the gods, kindled by <s>Manu</s>, praised by the sages, lauded by the inspired ones, proclaimed by the poets, sharpened by <s>Brahman</s>, offered with ghee, the leader of sacrifices, the charioteer of rituals, the unhurried <s>Hotṛ</s>, the swift conveyer of oblations' — [he continues] up to the libation-formula: 'The ladle (<s>juhū</s>) — the vessel of the gods, the divine drinking-cup. O <s>Agni</s>, you encompass the gods like a felly [encompasses] a wheel. Bring the gods for the sacrificer!' — and having commenced [with this], he invokes each deity with the [appropriate vocative of the] second case, [saying] 'Bring!' at each directive, prolonging the initial [syllable]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
But the first deity [he invokes] with '<s>agna āvaha</s>' ('O <s>Agni</s>, bring!'). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>' — these are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (shares of the clarified butter). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'<s>Agni</s>, <s>Agnī</s>-<s>Somau</s>' — at the full-moon [sacrifice]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In place of <s>Agnī</s>-<s>Somau</s>, <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agnī</s> — at the new-moon [sacrifice], for one who does not perform the <s>samnaya</s> (combination rite). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
<s>Indra</s> or <s>Mahendra</s> — for one who performs the <s>samnaya</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Between the two oblation materials, [one invokes] <s>Viṣṇu</s> in a low voice — [according to] the <s>Aitareyins</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [offering is invoked] at the full-moon, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> at the new-moon — [according to] some. [According to] others, none at all. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Among the other [invocations made] in a low voice, '<s>āvaha</s>' ('bring!'), '<s>svāhā</s>' ('hail!'), '<s>ayāṭ</s>' ('he has gone'), '<s>priyā dhāmāni</s>' ('dear abodes'), '<s>idaṃ haviḥ</s>' ('this is the oblation'), '<s>maho jyāya</s>' ('for the greater [glory]') — [these are said] aloud. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Those others that have the same [formula-]character [and] are indirect — those [are said] in a low voice or aloud. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
What is direct [is said] in a low voice. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
At each prompting, an invocation [is made]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having addressed all [deities], [the offering is made] once for those with a single offering. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Likewise, in the other <s>nigamas</s> (formulas), one should praise as if [addressing] a single [deity]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
[One who has] the same deity [and] the same purpose. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
[If] uninterrupted, once in the formulas. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

After the dragged-out (<s>oḷha</s>) [verses], in the supplementary (<s>āvāpikā</s>) [verses]: 'Bring the gods who drink the clarified butter! Bring <s>Agni</s> for the <s>hotra</s> (invoking office)! Bring your own greatness! Bring, O <s>Jātavedas</s>! Sacrifice for good victory!' — having thus invoked, as situated, sitting with knees raised, north of the <s>vedi</s> (altar), having spread out grasses upon the ground, he should make [a space of] one span.

'<s>Aditi</s> is the mother of this [sacrifice]. Do not cut me off from the atmosphere. I, with <s>Agni</s> as the deity, with the <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Stoma</s>, with the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s>, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre, with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, with the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-call as the thunderbolt — whoever hates us and whom we hate, him I slay.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

He should accompany with a <s>mantra</s> the one about to call out [the response] (<s>āśrāvayiṣyantam</s>): 'Call out! Announce the sacrifice to the gods! Announce me among men — for fame, for glory, for the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.' [And] to the one selecting [the <s>Hotṛ</s>]: 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, this one selects you — <s>Agni</s> for the <s>hotra</s> — together with [his] father <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. May heaven and earth protect me. <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Hotṛ</s>; I am the human [<s>Hotṛ</s>].'

Having heard 'human [<s>Hotṛ</s>]' from the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he should stand up [with the verse]: 'With life-span, with my own life-span, with the sap of plants, with the powers of <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god), I have arisen — following the immortals.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'Sixty and ninety snares, O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, are spread between <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Hotṛ</s>. They ensnare the simple one; [only] the exceedingly wise one passes through' — [he recites this] upon rising. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'I follow the path of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) as the <s>Hotṛ</s>' — having stepped forward, he should take hold of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> at the shoulder with the hand on the nearer side. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
[He should take hold of] the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler priest) at the hip area, with the left hand. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'We take hold of <s>Indra</s> for the office of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, as the priest placed in front — by whom the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, the gods, ascended to the highest heaven, to the sky.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

With sweeping-grasses (<s>sammārga</s> grasses), he should wipe his face three times inward [with the formula]: 'You are a wiping-away (<s>sammārga</s>). Wipe me auspiciously with offspring and cattle.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Once with the <s>mantra</s>, twice silently — everywhere thus when the ritual act is repeated. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having touched water, he should address the <s>Hotṛ</s>-seat with [the formula]: 'Arise, O <s>Daidhiṣavya</s>, from here! Sit in this seat of his — [you] who are less skilled than we.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

With the thumb and the little finger, he should push a grass [stalk] from the <s>Hotṛ</s>-seat westward to the south [with the formula]: 'Cast aside is <s>Parāvasu</s>.' 'I sit in the seat of him who is near' — he should sit down with the right thigh placed above [the left]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
These [acts of] pushing aside and sitting down [are performed] at all seats, by all [priests], at the first sitting-down on each day, even at the same [seat]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Twice — [according to] <s>Gautama</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
At the eating of the <s>brahmodana</s> (priestly rice porridge), at the establishment of the fires (<s>agnyādheya</s>) — [these belong to] the <s>Brahman</s> (priest). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
At the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], upon returning from the <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> [<s>stotra</s>]. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>Hotṛ</s> crawls forward. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
At the taking up of the ladle (<s>srugādāpana</s>) in the animal sacrifice. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Not at the <s>patnīsāmyājika</s> (the wife's accompanying rite). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Not anywhere other than [the seat] of the <s>Hotṛ</s> — [according to] <s>Kautsa</s>. (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having sat down: 'O divine sacrificial grass, may I sit upon you comfortably.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'Sit closer, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, be seated on the sacred grass' — having touched the grass with [his forehead to] his knees, from that point onward he should recite: (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'Homage to the lord of the earth, homage to the lord of the world, homage to the lord of beings, homage to existence. I take refuge in <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath). I take refuge in <s>apāna</s> (outbreath). I take refuge in <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath). I take refuge in speech. I take refuge in sight. I take refuge in hearing. I take refuge in mind. I take refuge in the self.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'I take refuge in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [metre]. I take refuge in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. I take refuge in the <s>Jagatī</s>. I take refuge in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. I take refuge in the metres. May <s>Sūrya</s> protect us from heaven. Homage to the great ones, homage to the small ones.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'All gods, command us! Do not let me be harmed here. The <s>Hotṛ</s>, seated, most worthy of sacrifice — may I first attain [the power] of speech today.' — Having completed [this], when the fuel is ablaze, he should have the ladles taken up with the spoken formula (<s>nigada</s>). (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'<s>Agni</s> is the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Let [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>] know the <s>hotra</s> (invoking office) of <s>Agni</s>. Let [him] know the guidance (<s>prāvitra</s>). It is well [done], O sacrificer. [You who say] "The one who [appointed] <s>Agni</s>..."' — having concluded [thus], he should recite in a low voice: 'You have chosen the <s>Hotṛ</s>.' (New/Full Moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Now he should conclude [the recitation]. 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, fill the ladle with ghee-containing [offering]. O <s>Ghṛtavatī</s> (ghee-rich one), O divine pair, O all-desirable one, we invoke <s>Iḷā</s>. I praise the gods, I bow to others worthy of homage, I sacrifice to those worthy of sacrifice.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
When this <s>nigada</s> (recitation) is completed, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> makes the call (<s>āśrāvaṇa</s>). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> should make the response (<s>pratyāśrāvaṇa</s>), standing at the place of the <s>utkara</s> (refuse heap), having taken up the <s>sphya</s> (wooden sword), <s>idhma</s> (firewood), and binding cords — facing south, according to the <s>Śāṭyāyanaka</s> [school]. He says '<s>astu śrauṣaṭ</s>' prolonging the 'au' syllable. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
They perform the <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
These are five. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Being directed once for each, he offers. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>āgūr</s> (invitation formula) and the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) come first, except for the <s>anuyāja</s> (after-offering). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'<s>ye yajāmahe</s>' is the <s>āgūr</s> (invitation formula). The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call) is final in all cases. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
It should be louder and stronger than the <s>yājyā</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Of both [<s>āgūr</s> and <s>yājyā</s>], one should prolong the initial syllables. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And the final syllable of the <s>yājyā</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Separating the junction syllables, one inserts an 'a' vowel, unless it is a two-word [compound] or ends in a consonant. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
A <s>visarjanīya</s> not preceded by a short vowel is changed to a <s>repha</s> (r-sound). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And the other one [i.e., a <s>visarjanīya</s> preceded by a short vowel] also becomes a <s>repha</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
A non-<s>repha</s> [<s>visarjanīya</s>] is elided. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The first [stop consonant] takes its own third [aspirated voiced counterpart]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Always before the letter 'ma'. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'<s>ye yajāmahe</s>, <s>samidhaḥ</s>, <s>samido agna</s>, <s>ājyasya vyantu</s>, <s>vaoṣaṭ</s>' — this is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Thus is the first [<s>prayāja</s>]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having uttered the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, '<s>vāg ojaḥ saha ojo mayi prāṇāpānau</s>,' he recites the <s>anumantraṇa</s> (accompanying formula) each time. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> should be recited during daytime. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Likewise the <s>anumantraṇa</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
This is the paradigm for the <s>yājyā</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

The second [<s>prayāja</s>] is '<s>Tanūnapāt</s>, <s>Agna</s>, may he come to the <s>ājya</s>,' except for the [schools of] <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Śunaka</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vadhryaśva</s>, and the <s>Rājanya</s> families. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
For them [it is] '<s>Narāśaṃsa</s>, <s>Agna</s>, may he come to the <s>ājya</s>.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The third is '<s>Iḍa</s>, <s>Agna</s>, may they come to the <s>ājya</s>.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

The fourth is '<s>Barhis</s>, <s>Agna</s>, may it come to the <s>ājya</s>.' The <s>āgūr</s> in the fifth: '<s>svāhā</s> to such-and-such, <s>svāhā</s> to such-and-such,' following the order of invocation of the deities as directed; for uninvoked [deities]: '<s>svāhā</s>, may the <s>ājya</s>-drinking gods, pleased, come to <s>Agni</s>'s <s>ājya</s>.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Up to that point [he recites] in a low voice. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And after the <s>śamyuvāka</s> (praise of the pressing-stone), [he recites] in a raised voice. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In a middle voice [he recites] the <s>havīṃṣi</s> (oblation formulas) up to the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering-to-the-well-offered). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In the highest voice, the remainder. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'<s>Agni</s> shall smite the foes' is the <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the first <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion). 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, are the lord of the good' is [the <s>anuvākyā</s>] for the second. 'May <s>Agni</s>, pleased, come to the <s>ājya</s>' is the <s>yājyā</s> for the first. 'May <s>Soma</s>, pleased, come to the <s>ājya</s> oblation' is [the <s>yājyā</s>] for the second. He offers both with the <s>āgūr</s> as the directive. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
All [offerings] have <s>anuvākyā</s>s (invitatory verses) and are without separate <s>praiṣa</s> (directives); the <s>anvāyātyā</s> (follow-up verse) is separate from them. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
And for the <s>Soma</s>-related ones, those between the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> and the <s>patnīsamyājas</s> (offerings of the wife). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
These two are the foe-destroying (<s>vārtraghnau</s>) [formulas] on the full-moon day. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The differentiation of the <s>anuvākyā</s> is by distinguishing marks and by difference in name; hence the inquiry [into the correct verse]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
When [the verses] are fixed, the <s>yājyā</s>s [are also fixed]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

On the new-moon day, the increasing (<s>vṛdhanvantau</s>) [formulas are used]: '<s>Agni</s> with the ancient hymn,' 'O <s>Soma</s>, with songs we [praise] you.' Up to that point is the restraint of speech. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

And between the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s>, and during <s>nigada</s> (recitation), <s>anuvacana</s> (repetition), <s>abhiṣṭavana</s> (praise-chanting), <s>śastra</s> (recitation), and <s>japa</s> (murmuring) — from the beginning to the end. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Except for what is [required] for the accomplishment of the sacrifice. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
If he stumbles, he should mutter 'May the gods protect us from this.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Or alternatively, another <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> [verse]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

The deities have been stated. Their <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> [verses are]: '<s>Agni</s> is the head of heaven, of the sacrifice,' 'This <s>Agni</s> of a thousand [powers],' '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode across this,' 'The god thrice [strode across] this earth,' '<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, with [shared] wealth,' 'You two [have] these heavenly lights.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, come with aid,' 'The inspired one seeking measure,' '<s>Indra</s>, [bring] wealth to the exalted one,' 'You have conquered many foes, O much-invoked,' 'Great <s>Indra</s> who by might has become,' 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, are great by <s>Brahman</s> (prayer).' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

If the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [offering is done with] the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voiced offering): '<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, who today for you two,' '<s>Mātariśvan</s> brought one from heaven.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Now for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>: 'Please the gods, O youngest desired one' is the <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'<s>Ye yajāmahe</s>, <s>Agni</s> <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>ayāḷ agni</s>,' having said [this] with the sixth [case] declension, indicating the deity, he should continue with '<s>priyā dhāmāny ayāḷ</s>.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Likewise the subsequent [formulas with] '<s>ayāḷ ayāḷ</s>,' but placed before them. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having enumerated up to the <s>ājya</s>-drinkers: 'May he worship the dear abodes of the <s>ājya</s>-drinking gods, may he worship the dear abodes of <s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>, may he secure his own greatness. May the sacrifice bring [offerings], may <s>Jātavedas</s> enjoy the oblation. O <s>Agni</s>, whatever today, O <s>Hotṛ</s> of the people's sacrifice' — he offers without pause. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Or in the original manner. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having anointed the two upper joints of the index finger, he wipes [the ghee] on the two lips inward. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'By the lord of speech, of your offering, for nourishment, for the <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath), I taste' — [applying] on the upper lip; 'By the lord of mind, of your offering, for vigor, for the <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), I taste' — on the lower lip. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having touched water, receiving the <s>Iḍā</s> (offering portion) with joined hands, placing it in the left hand, placing the hand with fingers [extended] northward behind it, he should have the subsidiary <s>Iḍā</s> portion cut. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Between the thumb and the fingers, he himself as the second should take [the portion]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having received it back, grasping it with the thumb, drawing it back. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Making the fingers into a non-fist, grasping the <s>Iḍā</s> from the right, he invokes [it] in a measure equal to the mouth, or equal to the breath. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'<s>Iḍā</s> is invoked — together with heaven, with the <s>Bṛhat</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], with <s>Āditya</s> — may <s>Iḍā</s> call us — together with heaven, with the <s>Bṛhat</s>, with <s>Āditya</s>. <s>Iḍā</s> is invoked — together with the atmosphere, with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], with <s>Vāyu</s> — may <s>Iḍā</s> call us — together with the atmosphere, with the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, with <s>Vāyu</s>. <s>Iḍā</s> is invoked—' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'together with the earth, with the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], with <s>Agni</s> — may <s>Iḍā</s> call us — together with the earth, with the <s>Rathantara</s>, with <s>Agni</s>. The cows are invoked together with the mixed [milk] — may the cows call me together with the mixed [milk].' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'The milch-cow is invoked together with the bull — may the milch-cow together with the bull call me. The cow with ghee-filled steps is invoked — may the cow with ghee-filled steps call me. The seven divine <s>Hotṛ</s>s are invoked — may the seven divine <s>Hotṛ</s>s call me.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'The friendly portion is invoked — may the friendly portion call me. <s>Iḍā</s> the rain is invoked — may <s>Iḍā</s> the rain call me.' This [part is recited] in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>). Then loudly: '<s>Iḍā</s> is invoked, invoked is <s>Iḍā</s> — may <s>Iḍā</s> call us. <s>Iḍā</s> is invoked.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'The daughter of <s>Manu</s>, with ghee-filled steps, [belonging to] <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, made by <s>Brahman</s> and the gods — invoked! The divine <s>Adhvaryu</s>s — invoked! The human [priests] — invoked!' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'Those who attend upon this sacrifice and the lord of the sacrifice — invoked! The two ancient ones, <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth), of true order, divine, born of the gods — invoked! This sacrificer is invoked for the further divine sacrifice — invoked for more oblation-making. May the gods enjoy this oblation of mine.' At that [point he says] 'invoked.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having invoked, he should eat the subsidiary <s>Iḍā</s> [with the formula]: 'O <s>Iḍā</s>, enjoy our portion, nourish the cows, invigorate the horses, you command the increase of wealth — bestow that upon us, give that to us — we have eaten your portion.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'All-souled, all-bodied, all-heroic, all-peopled' — or '<s>sarvapuruṣāḥ</s>' (with all men). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having performed the <s>mārjana</s> (purification), they proceed with the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Placing the <s>paristaraṇa</s> (strewing grass) between the joined hands, he pours away the rinsing water — that is the <s>mārjana</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>anuyājas</s> begin with [an offering] to the gods. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
They have endings with the word '<s>vīta</s>' (entered). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
They are three. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Being directed once for each, he offers. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'May the divine <s>Barhis</s> come for wealth-winning, for wealth-giving. May the divine <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> come for wealth-winning, for wealth-giving. The divine <s>Agni</s> <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, generous, gentle, wise, of true thought, the sacrificing <s>Hotṛ</s>, better <s>Hotṛ</s> than the <s>Hotṛ</s>. O <s>Agni</s>, the gods whom you have worshipped, whom you have satisfied — lead forth their <s>hotra</s> to the divine assembly in heaven, to the sacrifice among the gods. And O <s>Agni</s> <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, may you be the <s>Hotṛ</s> for wealth-winning, for wealth-giving — reverence to <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), speak forth!' Or without pause. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having been directed for the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn of praise): 'This has been well done for <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth). We have performed the <s>sūktavāka</s> and the <s>namovāka</s> (words of homage). May we prosper in the <s>sūktavāka</s>. O <s>Agni</s>, you are the <s>sūktavāk</s> (speaker of good hymns).' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'<s>Upaśruti</s> (divine hearing) of heaven and earth, gracious — may your [blessing] and yours be upon this sacrificer in this sacrifice, O <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>. Bestowing prosperity, swift in giving, fearless, unassailable, of wide pasture, having made [all] free from fear.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

'O rain-giving <s>Dyāvā</s> (Heaven), with flowing waters, beneficent, auspicious, full of vigor, full of milk, of good conduct and of sweet conduct.' Having concluded at 'of these two, it was found,' indicating the deity with the first (nominative) case, he should continue with 'this oblation was enjoyed, was magnified, was made into great glory.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Likewise the subsequent [formulas]. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'<s>Akrātām</s>, <s>akrata</s>' — as appropriate to the meaning. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The [procedure for the] <s>upāṃśu</s> (low-voiced offering) has been stated. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having followed through to the <s>āvāpika</s> (supplementary offering) end: 'The <s>ājya</s>-drinking gods enjoyed the <s>ājya</s>, were magnified, were made into great glory. By the <s>Agnihotra</s>, this oblation was enjoyed, was magnified, was made into great glory.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

In this <s>hotrā</s> (priestly office) may he prosper, in the divine assembly — this sacrificer, so-and-so, so-and-so — indicating his two names in a low voice, in the presence of the teacher — he desires long life, he desires good progeny, he desires increase of wealth. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
He desires [victory] over kinsmen, he desires the next divine sacrifice, he desires more oblation-making, he desires the heavenly abode, he desires all that is dear. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Whatever he desires by this oblation, may that be fulfilled in this [sacrifice], may the gods grant him that. <s>Agni</s> the god intercedes with the gods for him; we humans [intercede] with <s>Agni</s>. (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
'Both what is sacrificed and what is gained — may both <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth) protect us from distress. Your path is this — homage to the gods.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having been directed for the <s>śamyuvāka</s>: he says '<s>tat śamyor āvṛṇīmahe</s>' (we choose that of the pressing-stones) — [this is recited] with an <s>anuvākyā</s> but without <s>praṇava</s> (oṃ). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>Adhvaryu</s> hands him the <s>Veda</s> (bundle of sacred grass). (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
He should receive it [saying]: 'You are the <s>Veda</s>, may I know through the <s>Veda</s>.' (New-moon: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having risen with [the verse] "<s>ud āyuṣa</s>" ("Rise up with life"), and sitting down west of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire), they offer with <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) [the oblations to] <s>Soma</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the wives of the gods, and <s>Agni</s> the householder. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

"<s>āpyāyasva sametu te</s>" ("Swell up, let [the milks] come together for you"), "<s>sam te payāṃsi samuyantu vājāḥ</s>" ("let the milks and vigors unite for you"), "<s>iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam</s>" ("here [we invoke] <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the foremost"), "<s>tan nas turīyam adhapoṣayitnu</s>" ("that fourth [milk] nourishing us from below"), "<s>devānāṃ patnīr uśatīr avantu naḥ</s>" ("may the willing wives of the gods help us") — these two [verses]; "<s>agnir hotā gṛhapatir sa rājā</s>" ("<s>Agni</s> is the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the householder, the king"), "<s>havyavāḷ agnir ajaraḥ pitā naḥ</s>" ("<s>Agni</s> the oblation-bearer, ageless, is our father") — these are the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s> (wife-oblation) [verses]. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Now, one who desires offspring should offer [oblations] to <s>Rākā</s>, <s>Sinīvālī</s>, and <s>Kuhū</s>, before [the oblation to] the householder [<s>Agni</s>]. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

"<s>Rākām aham</s>" ("<s>Rākā</s> I [invoke]"), "<s>Sinīvālī</s>," "<s>Kuhūm aham</s>" ("<s>Kuhū</s> I [invoke]") — two [verses] each for the offering verse (<s>yājyā</s>) and the invitatory verse (<s>anuvākyā</s>). (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

"<s>Kuhūm ahaṃ suvṛtam vidma</s>" ("We know <s>Kuhū</s>, the well-turned"), "<s>apasam asmin yajñe suhavāṃ johavīmi</s>" ("the active one, easy to invoke, I repeatedly call upon in this sacrifice"), "<s>sā no dadātu śravaṇaṃ pitṝṇām</s>" ("may she grant us the fame of the ancestors"), "<s>tasya ete devi haviṣā vidhema</s>" ("to her, O goddess, may we offer with this oblation"), "<s>Kuhūr devānām amṛtasya patnī</s>" ("<s>Kuhū</s>, the wife of the immortality of the gods"), "<s>havyā no asya haviṣaḥ śṛṇotu</s>" ("may she, worthy of invocation, hear [the call] of our oblation"). (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

"<s>saṃdāśuṣe kiratu bhūri vāmam</s>" ("may she scatter abundant treasure for the generous one"), "<s>rāyas poṣaṃ yajamāne dadhātu</s>" ("may she bestow increase of wealth upon the sacrificer"). He should make her pour <s>ājya</s> onto the palm of the hand. Having invoked <s>Iḷā</s>, she should eat all of it. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The <s>śamyuvāka</s> (utterance with the <s>śamyā</s> club) may or may not be [performed]. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having given the bundle of grass (<s>veda</s>) to the wife, he should have her recite — the <s>Hotṛ</s> or the <s>Adhvaryu</s>: "You are the <s>veda</s> (knowledge), you are acquisition (<s>vitti</s>), may I acquire. You are the deed (<s>karma</s>), you are the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), you are the rite (<s>kriyā</s>). You are the connector (<s>saṃsani</s>), you are the obtainer (<s>sanitṛ</s>), may I obtain. May the <s>veda</s> grant [me] a vigorous [son], rich in ghee, a dwelling, increase of wealth, a thousandfold." (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
"He whom many live upon, who is the controller of people — may I obtain that offspring, may I obtain [it] — for the sake of desire, you [I invoke]." Thus. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
She should touch with the tip of the bundle of grass (<s>veda</s>) the region of the navel — if she desires offspring. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Then he should untie her girdle (<s>yoktra</s>) [saying]: "I release you from the bond of <s>Varuṇa</s>." (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Placing that [girdle] as a doubled rope west of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> toward the east, he places over it blades of the <s>veda</s> grass with their tips pointing north. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
In front, a full vessel, closely joined with the blades of <s>veda</s> grass. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having touched [it], he should have her recite: "You are fullness; may you be fullness for me. You are complete fullness; may you be complete fullness for me. You are being; may you be being for me. You are all; may you be all for me. You are imperishability; may you not perish for me." (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Then, from the full vessel, sprinkling water in each direction while having her recite: "In the eastern direction, may the gods and <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) purify me. In the southern direction, may the months and ancestors purify me. In the western direction, may the households and cattle purify me.

In the northern direction, may the waters, herbs, and forest trees purify me. In the upward direction, may the sacrifice, the year, and <s>Prajāpati</s> purify me. May they purify me." Or [simply] "may they purify me." (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Then, having placed her upturned cupped hands beneath the girdle, and lowering the full vessel toward his own left side, he should have her recite: "May I not pour away my offspring, O you who lie with us. I pour you [waters] into the ocean; drink your own draught." (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having grasped the blades of <s>veda</s> grass at the tips, without shaking them, strewing them continuously, he goes from the <s>Gārhapatya</s> to the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) by the left [southern side], [reciting] "<s>tantum tanvan rajaso bhānum anvihi</s>" ("stretching the thread, follow the light of the atmosphere"). (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

Having placed the remainder [of the <s>veda</s> grass], and standing west of and to the north of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he should offer with the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) from the pot all expiatory oblations, with <s>mantras</s> ending in <s>svāhā</s>, unless <s>svāhā</s> is [already] recited in the <s>mantra</s>. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Whatever he offers without being commissioned — [the same rule applies] elsewhere also. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
The same applies to the unmanifest <s>homa</s> (oblation), the adding of fuel (<s>abhyādhāna</s>), and the attendant ceremonies (<s>upasthāna</s>). (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

"<s>Ayāś ca agne anabhiśastīś ca</s>" ("O <s>Agni</s>, [grant us] freedom from distress and freedom from blame"), "<s>satyam it tvam ayā asi</s>" ("truly you are without distress"), "<s>ayāsā vayasā kṛtaḥ</s>" ("made without distress, with vigor"), "<s>ayāsan havyam ūhiṣe</s>" ("you bear the oblation without distress"), "<s>yā no dhehi bheṣajaṃ svāhā</s>" ("grant us the remedy, <s>svāhā</s>"). (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

With the two [verses beginning] "<s>ato devā avantu naḥ</s>" ("from there may the gods help us"), and with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances): "<s>bhūḥ svāhā</s>," "<s>bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>," "<s>svaḥ svāhā</s>," "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>." (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Having offered, he sits down with the concluding recitation (<s>saṃsthājapa</s>), goes out by the passage (<s>tīrtha</s>), and is then unrestricted. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)

"<s>Oṃ</s>, and to me be melody (<s>svara</s>), and to you, O sacrifice, be the subsidiary offering (<s>upa</s>), and obeisance (<s>namas</s>). Whatever of yours is deficient, to that, obeisance to you; whatever of yours is excessive, to that, obeisance to you" — this is the concluding recitation. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Thus [ends the section] for the <s>Hotṛ</s>. (New-moon ritual: <s>Hotṛ</s>)
Now [the duties] of the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
The sipping of water (<s>ācamana</s>), the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), and purification rites are [the same] as for the <s>Hotṛ</s>. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
He is always to the south of all ritual actions, whether of the stationary [fires] or of those that move. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
In whichever direction the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) and the <s>vedi</s> (altar) would extend — that alone is east in that context. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
In ritual actions without <s>mantras</s>, there is an option between standing and sitting. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
He should stand during oblations that have [the call] "<s>vaṣaṭ</s>." (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
He should sit at other times. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Having circumambulated the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire to the east, joining the tips of all fingers and thumbs, he should sit down to the south on <s>kuśa</s> grasses. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Having sat down, he should recite: "<s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]; he shall sit at the seat of <s>Brahman</s>. O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, protect the sacrifice." (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
This is the <s>Brahman</s> recitation (<s>brahmajapa</s>) in all sacrificial systems where there is a fire and where sitting down [is prescribed]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
He gives permission [to proceed] once seated. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

Having heard "O <s>Brahman</s>, I shall bring forward the waters," and having recited "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar bṛhaspatiprasūta</s>" ("<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>, impelled by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>"), he gives permission with "<s>oṃ praṇaya</s>" ("<s>oṃ</s>, bring forward") — everywhere. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
But the commands [vary] according to the ritual act. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Beginning with <s>praṇava</s> (<s>oṃ</s>), [they are spoken] aloud. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Or [aloud] from after the <s>praṇava</s> onward. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
From that point onward, he remains with speech restrained, until the taking up of the offering-material (<s>haviṣkṛtodvādana</s>). (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Until the wiping (<s>āmarjana</s>) in the animal sacrifice. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
In the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, [the silence extends] from the <s>gharma</s> and the like, and from the <s>atipraiṣa</s> and the like, up to the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> [call]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
From the morning litany (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>) and the like, up to [the offering of] the <s>Antaryāma</s> [cup]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Of the <s>Harivant</s> [offerings], at each pressing, up to the <s>Iḷā</s> [invocation]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
During the <s>stotras</s> (chants), from the giving of permission (<s>atisarjana</s>) and the like, up to the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> [call]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Up to the <s>udṛc</s> (overflowing) [cup] during the <s>Pavamāna</s> [chants]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
And whatever is accompanied by a <s>mantra</s>. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
The remainder is [the same] as for the <s>Hotṛ</s>. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
And [also the rules for] emergencies (<s>āpatti</s>). (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
But where the fire is brought forward, even in a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, from that [point] onward, speech restraint [applies]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
And going to the south, he recites the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) "<s>āśuḥ śiśāna</s>" ("the swift, the sharpened"). (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Having completed [it], the sitting down and the rest are as stated [above]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
But during the <s>Soma</s> pressing, there is no <s>brahmajapa</s> (recitation by the <s>Brahman</s> priest). (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
At other times, with speech released, speaking little, the mind fixed on the sacrifice. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)
Upon noticing a reversal, an interpolation, or an omission in a <s>mantra</s>, ritual action, or declaration, he should offer an oblation while bending the knee. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

If [the error is] in a <s>Ṛc</s> [verse], [he offers with] "<s>bhūḥ</s>" into the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire]. If in a <s>Yajus</s> [formula], "<s>bhuvaḥ</s>" into the southern [<s>Dakṣiṇa</s>] fire — [or into] the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> during <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices]. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

If [the error is] in a <s>Sāman</s> [chant], "<s>svaḥ</s>" into the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. For everything [combined], or when unknown, "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>" into the <s>Āhavanīya</s> alone. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

Before the [other] priests, he should press back with the handle of the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) a coal that has fallen outside the fire-enclosure, [reciting]: "May my austerity not be burnt, may my sacrifice not be burnt, may the lord of the sacrifice not be burnt. Obeisance to you who approach, obeisance to <s>Rudra</s> who depart. Obeisance [to you] where you sit down." (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

"Do not harm this one, do not harm that one" — [he recites] in each direction: the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the sacrificer in the east; the <s>Brahman</s> and the sacrificer in the south; the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the wife, and the sacrificers in the west; the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> and the sacrificers in the north. (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

Then he should cast [the coal] back, [reciting]: "I have seized the sacrifice from the lap of <s>Nirṛti</s> (destruction). I, the knowing one, hand it over to the gods. O you of good offspring, for a hundred [years] have [the gods] not harmed us. O gods, grant us here your shelter." (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

He should offer over it: "<s>sahasraśṛṅgo vṛṣabho jātavedāḥ</s>" ("The thousand-horned bull, <s>Jātavedas</s>"), "<s>stomapṛṣṭho ghṛtavān supratīkaḥ</s>" ("with chants on his back, rich in ghee, of beautiful form"), "<s>mā no hiṃsīd dhiṃsito dadhāmi</s>" ("may he not harm us; I place back the displaced one"), "<s>na tvā jahāmi gopoṣaṃ ca no vīrapoṣaṃ ca yaccha svāhā</s>" ("I do not abandon you; grant us prosperity in cattle and in heroes, <s>svāhā</s>"). (<s>Brahman</s>: general)

When the <s>prāśitra</s> (fore-portion) is being brought, he looks at it [reciting]: "With the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, I look upon you." [Then]: "By the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I receive you." Having received it in his cupped hands: "I seat you at the navel of the earth, in the lap of <s>Aditi</s>." (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)

Having placed [it] on <s>kuśa</s> grasses facing east, he should eat it without biting, with the thumb and little finger, [reciting]: "With the mouth of <s>Agni</s> I eat you, with the mouth of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>." (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)

Having sipped water, or he should sip [reciting]: "With truth I anoint you. May the deities who are in the waters pacify this. Do not harm my sight, hearing, and vital breaths." "I place you in the belly of <s>Indra</s>" — [saying this] he should touch his navel. Having washed the <s>prāśitraharaṇa</s> (vessel for the fore-portion), he pours water toward himself three times with it. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)
Having wiped [his hands], he should place the <s>Brahman</s>'s portion in this [vessel]. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)
The sacrificer's portion [he places] behind, on <s>kuśa</s> grasses. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)

He should look upon the supplementary offering (<s>anvāhārya</s>) [reciting]: "You are the share of <s>Prajāpati</s>; you are full of vigor, full of nourishment, imperishable. Do not look upon me [with evil eye] — in this world and in the other." (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)

"Protect my in-breath and out-breath; for the sake of desire, I [invoke] you" — thus, without touching [it], having smelled it, having grasped the remainder with the thumb and little finger, he should place [it] in the <s>Brahman</s>'s portion. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)

Having heard "O <s>Brahman</s>, we shall go forth," [he recites]: "<s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the <s>Brahman</s>; he has sat at the seat of <s>Brahman</s>. O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you have guarded the sacrifice. Guard the sacrifice, guard the lord of the sacrifice. Guard me." (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)

Having recited "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar bṛhaspatiprasūta</s>," he gives permission for the offering of the <s>samidh</s> (fuel-stick) with "<s>oṃ pratiṣṭha</s>" ("<s>oṃ</s>, proceed"). When the rite is concluded, he should offer all expiatory oblations last among the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests). The others should place their hands [on him]. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)
Or [they should touch] the <s>Hotṛ</s>. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)
Of these two [the <s>Hotṛ</s> and <s>Brahman</s>], the regular (<s>nitya</s>) oblation [procedure is as described]. (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)
All [priests] conclude with the concluding recitation (<s>saṃsthājapa</s>). (New-moon ritual: <s>Brahman</s>)
The <s>Iṣṭi</s> (oblation rite), <s>Paśu</s> (animal sacrifice), and <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] are taught according to the full-moon model. (General rules)
With those [procedures], one should sacrifice on the new-moon day or the full-moon day. (General rules)
And a <s>rājanya</s> (member of the warrior class) should also offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>. (General rules)
At other times, he should offer food to an ascetic <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (General rules)
One who follows truth and righteousness, who has pressed <s>Soma</s>, should always offer oblations. (General rules)
When there are many [ritual acts], the sequence of the instructions for many [acts] applies. (General rules)
But the offering verse (<s>yājyā</s>) and the invitatory verse (<s>anuvākyā</s>) are two each. (General rules)
When no specific instruction is given, the regular [rule applies]. (General rules)
The establishment of the sacred fires (<s>agnyādheya</s>). (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
On the [<s>nakṣatras</s>] <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, the <s>Phalgunīs</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, or the latter <s>Proṣṭhapadās</s>. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
On any one of these. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should establish [the fires] in spring, at a <s>parvan</s> (junction day). (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
A <s>kṣatriya</s> and a <s>vaiśya</s> are associated [respectively] with summer, the rains, and autumn. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
One may establish [the fires] in any season whatsoever. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
One who is about to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> should not inquire about the season or the <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism). (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
He should fetch the fire-churning sticks (<s>araṇi</s>) from a <s>Śamī</s> tree growing upon an <s>Aśvattha</s> tree, without looking back. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

'O <s>Aśvattha</s>, you who have mounted the <s>Śamī</s> tree, you who are together with her — I fetch you with the sacred prayer, with sacrifices, with signs' — the <s>Agnyādheya</s> [concludes] with the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> (full oblation). (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
If, however, the offerings would become thin [i.e., insufficient]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
In the first [<s>iṣṭi</s>], [the deities are] <s>Agni</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Pavamāna</s> (<s>Agni</s> the Purifier). (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
'O <s>Agni</s>, you purify lives; O <s>Agni</s>, purify, you of good purification' [are the <s>mantras</s>]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

'He who carries the oblation, the immortal <s>Agni</s>, the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker), the <s>purohita</s> (priest)' — when 'the <s>samyājyā</s> (accompanying offerings) of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation to <s>Agni</s>)' is stated, one should understand them as belonging to the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
Wherever a deity is introduced, [it causes] the removal of the regular [offerings]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
Those [offerings] that are between the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions) — those [remain] in their place. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
This is the rule for [offerings of] the same class. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

In the second [<s>iṣṭi</s>], [the two deities] are the two Augmenters. [The <s>mantras</s> are:] '<s>Agni</s> the purifier; <s>Agni</s> the bright; O purifying one, brightly shining for us; O <s>Agni</s>, with purifying splendor; <s>Agni</s>, of most pure vows; forth, O <s>Agni</s>, your bright [flames].' (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

'He the mighty, overcoming all assailants; I praise <s>Agni</s> the <s>purohita</s>' — [these are] the <s>samyājyā</s>. In the second [<s>iṣṭi</s>], one inserts into the kindling verses (<s>sāmidhenī</s>), before the penultimate, the two [verses beginning] 'broad-shining, immortal.' (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

When 'nourishing (<s>dhāyya</s>)' is stated, one should understand these [verses]; [they are] the nourishing ones: '<s>Agni</s> with wealth, attaining riches; prosperity-giving; disease-removing.' '<s>Agnīṣomau</s>, <s>Indrāgnī</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — these are optional [deities]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
<s>Aditi</s>. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

'And you, O <s>Aditi</s>, the great; the great mother of the virtuous; the wife of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), we invoke for protection. The one of mighty sovereignty, unaging, broad, of good shelter, <s>Aditi</s> of good guidance.' (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

'Being kindled, O <s>Agni</s>; this O <s>Agni</s>' — [these are] the <s>samyājyā</s>. When 'in the <s>Virāj</s> meter' is stated, one should understand these — [thus] three [<s>iṣṭis</s>]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
The first and last [<s>iṣṭis</s>] should indeed be [in <s>Virāj</s>]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
Or [only] the first. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
In that case, the nourishing [verses] and the <s>Virāj</s> [verses] would indeed be [combined]. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
'In the mother transformation, [the system] based on <s>Virāj</s>' — one should understand this. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
For twelve nights after the establishment [of fires], the fires should be kept burning continuously. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)
But indefinitely for one who has lost his prosperity. (<s>Agnyādheya</s>)

At the release [ceremony], in the afternoon, having kindled the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire), having brought the southern fire (<s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>) — brought from a <s>Vaiśya</s> family or from a wealthy person's [fire], some say from one of the same origin, or one that is being maintained, or having kindled it with the fire-churning sticks — one should raise the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), blazing, from the <s>Gārhapatya</s>. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
'O divine [fire], I raise you from the gods for glory' — with this [<s>mantra</s>] he should raise [it]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

'Being raised up, raise me from sin — what I have done unknowingly and what knowingly; whatever sin has been committed during the day — from all that, being raised up, protect me' — with this he should carry [the fire] forward. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

'I offer an immortal oblation in the immortal [fire]; [I offer] <s>Agni</s> in the earth, in the womb of immortality. By that may I conquer endless desire; <s>Prajāpati</s> first conquered this. <s>Agni</s> into <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — with this he should deposit [the fire], facing the sun. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Similarly in the morning, [he performs] until dawn, indeed facing [the sun]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
But he should carry [the fire] forward [reciting] 'whatever of the night was...' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
From this point onward, one who has established the fires [observes] the vow-practice until the oblation. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
And one who offers before sunrise [observes it] until sunrise. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The oblation [is performed] after sunset. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Sipping of water (<s>ācamana</s>) is always [required]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having recited 'By <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) and <s>Satya</s> (truth) I sprinkle you,' he should sprinkle — three times thrice, each one [separately], taking water again and again. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
There is an option regarding the sequence. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

But the southern [fire] is known to be first: 'This southern [fire] is indeed the father of the fires; the <s>Gārhapatya</s> is the son; the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the grandson' — therefore one should sprinkle in this order. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
From the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, he should carry an uninterrupted stream of water [reciting] 'Stretching the thread, endowed with light from the atmosphere' — to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Sitting down west of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, he should push the embers northward [reciting]: 'You are makers of good oblations; you will make the oblation good.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
On those [embers] he should place the <s>Agnihotra</s> [pot] on the fire [saying]: 'Placed on the fire, placed on the fire, placed on the fire, indeed.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

'In the abode of <s>Iḷā</s>, rich in ghee; O <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of beings), enjoy this oblation, moving and unmoving. May the nourishment of those seven domestic animals of all forms be mine' — or [this alternative <s>mantra</s>]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
One should not place curds on the fire — some say one should place [them]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The regular oblation is with milk. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Gruel, cooked rice, curds, clarified butter [are] for one desiring village, food, vigor [of the senses], and radiance [respectively]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
What is placed on the fire should be allowed to blaze up. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Without placing curds [on the fire, recite]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, do not take away my radiance.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Sprinkling [the milk] with the offering spoon (<s>sruva</s>), or not — [reciting]: 'You are peace; you are immortality.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
There should be no interchanging of these two [alternatives]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
He should carry [it] around [the fire] with a blazing [brand], three times with intervals [reciting]: 'Warded off are the <s>rakṣas</s> (demons); warded off are the enemies.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Pulling [the milk] until it swells, he should set it aside northward [reciting]: 'For heaven — for you; for the atmosphere — for you; for the earth — for you' — as he places [the portions]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having released the embers [reciting] 'You are makers of good oblations; you made the oblation good,' he should heat the ladle (<s>sruk</s>) and the offering spoon (<s>sruva</s>) [reciting]: 'Burned are the <s>rakṣas</s>; burned are the enemies; scorched are the <s>rakṣas</s>; scorched are the enemies.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having placed the <s>sruva</s> to the north of the pot, he should give the signal [saying] 'Om, I shall lift up.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

The one who has established the fires, having sipped water, having crossed beyond the altar (<s>vedi</s>) to the further side, sitting down to the south, hearing that, should give the signal 'Om, lift up.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having given the signal, [reciting] '<s>bhūḥ</s> <s>iḷā</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s> <s>iḷā</s>, <s>svaḥ</s> <s>iḷā</s>, <s>vṛdha</s> <s>iḷā</s>' — he should lift up a spoonful (<s>sruvapūra</s>). (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The most fire-suitable, the most full — for him who desires the eldest-born prosperity of his sons. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
For whichever of his sons is dear to him, he should lift up a full [spoonful]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having touched the pot and placed the fuel-stick and the ladle upon the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, having placed [the oblation] near the <s>Āhavanīya</s> on <s>kuśa</s> grass, measured to the length of a breath, and having bent his knees, he should place the fuel-stick [reciting]: 'I place upon you the silvery, fire-luminous, nocturnal brick. <s>Svāhā</s>!' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having placed the fuel-stick, [reciting] 'You are lightning; flash away my sin' — having sipped water [reciting] 'Faith in <s>Agni</s>' — he should offer into the blazing [fire] at the measure of two fingers [saying]: '<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>. Om. <s>Agni</s> is light; light is <s>Agni</s>. <s>Svāhā</s>!' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having offered the first oblation, having placed [the ladle] on the <s>kuśa</s> grass, he should look at the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [saying]: 'Grant me cattle.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Then the second [oblation], silently, more [in quantity], unmixed, to the east-north or to the north. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
One should meditate on <s>Prajāpati</s> mentally during silent oblations, everywhere. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having left the greater portion in the ladle, shaking [it] three times, wiping [it] off at the root of the <s>kuśa</s> grass, he wipes [saying]: 'For the cattle — for you.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

To the south of those [<s>kuśa</s> grasses], he makes [the gesture with] fingers turned upward, wearing the sacred thread on the right shoulder (<s>prācīnāvītin</s>), silently — or [saying] '<s>Svadhā</s> to the ancestors.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having poured down water. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
'You are rain; rain away my sin' — having sipped water [reciting] 'Faith in the waters.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The one who has established the fires should pronounce the benediction. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having stated the establishment [formula], [reciting] 'By that <s>Ṛṣi</s>, by that <s>Brahman</s> (sacred formula), by that deity, as did the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, be firmly seated' — [this is for] the fuel-stick. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
'Those of his milking and yielding' — [this is for] the first oblation. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having worshipped, he should await the second [oblation], looking on [and reciting]: '<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>. May I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in nourishment through nourishment.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
And with [verses addressed to] <s>Agni</s>. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
With the three [verses beginning] 'O <s>Agni</s>, you purify lives.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Year after year. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
With gruel or milk, he should offer by himself at the <s>parvan</s> (junction day). (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
At the other time, [through] one of the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>). (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Or a resident student. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having touched water, turning northward, he should partake [of the remainder]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Or having offered at the two other [fires]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
'For life I partake of you' — the first [portion]. 'For the eating of food — you' — the second. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having silently placed a fuel-stick, [he offers] '<s>Agni</s> the lord of the household, <s>svāhā</s>!' in the <s>Gārhapatya</s>. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The second [oblation] is always [done]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having silently placed a fuel-stick, [he offers] '<s>Agni</s> the lord of rest, <s>svāhā</s>!' in the southern [fire]. Or '<s>Agni</s> the eater of food, lord of food, <s>svāhā</s>!' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The second [oblation] is always [done]. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Then, having washed her [the pot] with <s>kuśa</s> grass, he should pour out four full [libations] to the east and north [saying]: 'To the seasons, <s>svāhā</s>! To the directions, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Seven Sages, <s>svāhā</s>! To the other people, <s>svāhā</s>!' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

A fifth [libation] on the <s>kuśa</s> ground [saying]: 'I offer the immortal on the earth to <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' A sixth behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [saying]: 'I offer the breath into the immortal; I offer the immortal into the breath. <s>Svāhā</s>!' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Having heated [it], he should deposit it within the sacrificial enclosure (<s>antarvedi</s>). (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
He should give [the remainder] to the attendant. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Going around in front of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he should place three fuel-sticks, three at a time, standing with face turned northward. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The first with a <s>mantra</s>. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
In the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [reciting] 'Shine forth'; in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [reciting] 'He has shone'; in the southern [fire reciting] 'He has shone forth.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
The sprinkling has been described. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
With those two [comes] the sweeping around. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
But the earlier [sweeping] is before the sprinkling. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Thus [also] in the morning. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
Near sunrise, when it has dawned, or after sunrise. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

'By truth and cosmic order I sprinkle you' — the sprinkling. 'Om, I shall lift up' — the giving of the signal. 'I place upon you the golden, sun-luminous, diurnal brick. <s>Svāhā</s>!' — the placing of the fuel-stick. '<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>. Om. <s>Sūrya</s> is light; light is <s>Sūrya</s>. <s>Svāhā</s>!' — the oblation and the wiping. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)
One who is about to depart, having kindled the fires, having sipped water, having gone past [the fires], stands in worship. (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

He should praise the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [saying]: 'Protect my cattle.' The <s>Gārhapatya</s> [saying]: 'Lead [me]; protect my offspring.' The southern [fire saying]: 'O <s>Atharvan</s>, protect my food.' Looking at the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [saying]: 'O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, protect these my houses for me — undestroyed, unharmed. May <s>Pūṣan</s> guard them until our return.' (<s>Agnihotra</s>)

Having returned as prescribed, circumambulating, he attends upon the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire): 'My name, O <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of beings), father and mother have bestowed upon me, O <s>Agni</s>; may you bear it back to me again when I return; I shall bear your name first' — (agnihotra)
He should set forth without looking back, reciting the hymn 'Do not bow down.' — (agnihotra)
He should release his voice at a distance from the fires. — (agnihotra)
'May the path of the father always be easy to travel' — having descended from the path. — (agnihotra)

If one who has not attended upon the fires should go on a journey: 'Being here myself, I bear you who are there, O <s>Agni</s>, with heart, speech, and mind. Do not abandon me who am away; I attend upon you with the light of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — having attended upon the fires in each direction. — (agnihotra)
'We have gone off the path' — upon returning. — (agnihotra)

With fuel in hand, maintaining silence, having heard the fires crackling, he should approach and look at the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire): 'May those who bring [offerings] at all times, with an untroubled mind — O <s>Agni</s>, may we not come to harm as your neighbors. Homage to you, the bountiful; homage to you at the approach. O <s>Agni</s>, purify yourself for our bodies; join us with wealth.' — (agnihotra)

Having placed fuel on the fires, he attends upon the <s>āhavanīya</s>: 'My name and yours, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, let us wear like two garments, moving about. May they sustain you for strength and for life, as each of us, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, [has] a body.' — (agnihotra)
Thereupon he should add fuel. — (agnihotra)

In the <s>āhavanīya</s>: 'O <s>Agni</s>, all-knowing, most wealth-bestowing to us — O <s>Agni</s>, sovereign, seize for yourself splendor and overcoming power, <s>svāhā</s>!' In the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire): 'This <s>Agni</s>, the lord of the house, the household fire, most wealth-bestowing to offspring — O <s>Agni</s>, lord of the house, seize for yourself splendor and overcoming power, <s>svāhā</s>!' In the southern [fire]: 'This <s>Agni</s>, rich in soil, wealthy, increaser of nourishment — (agnihotra)

O <s>Agni</s>, rich in soil, seize for yourself splendor and overcoming power, <s>svāhā</s>!' He should look at the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>: 'O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, may you two guard these homes of mine — unperished, uncarried off — may <s>Pūṣan</s> protect them until our return again.' — (agnihotra)
Having returned as prescribed, having swept [the ground], sitting down north of the <s>vihāra</s> (fire-hall), he should release his voice [saying]: '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>.' — (agnihotra)

If absent for more than ten nights, he should offer <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) taken four times: 'May the mind delight in the light; may the <s>ājya</s> [restore] my interrupted sacrifice — may it join together this [sacrifice]. The dawns that were desired and those that were not — I join them together with this oblation of ghee, <s>svāhā</s>!' — (agnihotra)
And on [the day of] non-offering of the <s>agnihotra</s>. — (agnihotra)
Some [say] a counter-offering [is required for each missed day]. — (agnihotra)

He should look at the houses — even one who has not established the fires [should say]: 'O houses, do not fear; I come in the best manner for your welfare; and may you prosper among us, and may your lord of cattle not be harmed.' He should enter [saying]: 'I enter the houses, auspicious-minded, hero-producing, full of heroes — bearing nourishment, sprinkling ghee — may I dwell in them, of auspicious mind.' Looking around thrice [saying]: 'Auspicious, benign, may there be peace, peace.' — (agnihotra)
Even if something known [has happened that is] unpleasant, they should not announce it on that day. — (agnihotra)
It is prescribed: 'Fearlessness to you, fearlessness to these — let there be!' Thus he should attend [upon the fires] when setting out, upon returning, or day by day. — (agnihotra)
On the new-moon day, in the afternoon, [is performed] the <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (oblation of rice-balls to the ancestors). — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

He should carry one firebrand from the southern fire toward the south-east [saying]: 'Those who, assuming forms, being <s>asuras</s> (demons), wander about with the <s>svadhā</s> (oblation to ancestors) — those who carry away beyond and within — may <s>Agni</s> drive them away from this world.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
All rites [are performed facing] that direction. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Having set up [the fire] and strewn [grass] on both sides, south of the southern fire — [arranged] eastward, northward, westward, or northward, one by one — he should set out the utensils: the rice-pot, winnowing basket, wooden sword, mortar, pestle, ladle, the fixed [vessel], black antelope skin, fuel cut in one stroke, stirring stick, and water vessel. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Having ascended the platform to the south of the fire, he should immerse the rice-pot full of rice grains. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
He should set aside the husked [grains]. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Having made the mortar [rest] on the black antelope skin, the wife should pound the rest, without separating [the grains]. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Having pounded [them], washing once, he should cook [them] on the southern fire. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

In front of the <s>atipraṇīta</s> (carried-forward fire), he should draw a line with the wooden sword [saying]: 'Driven away are the <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>rakṣas</s> (evil spirits), and those who sit on the <s>vedi</s> (altar).' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Having sprinkled that [line], having strewn [it] with [grass] cut in one stroke, he should set [the offerings] down. Having anointed with ghee the rice cooked in the pot, [he should set out] the <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter), melted butter — either unprocessed fresh butter or processed — placing the <s>ājya</s> in the fixed vessel, to the south. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
[He should also set out] collyrium, ointment, cushion, and pillow. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Wearing the sacred thread on the right [shoulder] (<s>prācīnāvītī</s>), having set up the fuel, taking [the offering] with the stirring stick, he should offer with the proper portion: 'To <s>Soma</s> accompanied by the ancestors, <s>svadhā</s>, homage! To <s>Agni</s>, the carrier of offerings to the departed, <s>svadhā</s>, homage!' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Or with the utterance of '<s>svāhā</s>,' [offering] to <s>Agni</s> first, wearing the sacred thread on the left [shoulder] (<s>yajñopavītī</s>). — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Having presented the stirring stick, wearing the sacred thread on the right [shoulder], he should convey water three times along the line [saying]: 'May the fathers be purified! May the grandfathers be purified! May the great-grandfathers be purified!' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

On that [line] he should place the rice-balls, with the palm turned downward, for the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather [saying]: 'This is for you, O so-and-so, and for those who follow you here.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
For each of those — for those among them who are deceased — thus [says] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>. He should honor the others directly, because of the purpose [of the rite]. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
He should place [rice-balls] for all [of them] — thus [says] <s>Tailvali</s>, because [the offering] is a quality of the ritual action. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Even to the end of their lives, he should place [rice-balls] only for the three deceased — thus [says] <s>Gautama</s>, for the ritual action is motivated by its purpose. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
The method differs for the living and the dead. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Not for others, because of the lack of authority. Not directly. He should not place [rice-balls] for the living. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Nor for those [whose deaths are] concealed among the living. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
He should offer oblations for the living. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
The offering to all is [made when] all are living. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
One who does not know the names [should say]: 'Father, grandfather, great-grandfather.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
He should address the placed [rice-balls] with a benediction: 'Here, O ancestors, rejoice! Help yourselves each to your share!' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Turning to the left, turning northward, holding his breath as best he can, sitting still, having turned back around [he recites]: 'The ancestors have rejoiced; they have helped themselves each to their share.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
He should eat the <s>prāṇabhakṣa</s> (life-portion) of the rice offering. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
The disposal is always [performed]. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
'So-and-so, anoint yourself; so-and-so, apply collyrium' — [he applies] ointment and collyrium to the rice-balls. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

He should give a garment, or a fringe, or a tuft of wool — after fifty years [of age, using] his own hair [saying]: 'This is your garment, O ancestors; do not yoke us to anything other than this, O ancestors.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Then he should attend upon them: 'Homage to you, O ancestors, for nourishment! Homage to you, O ancestors, for sap! Homage to you, O ancestors, for vigor! Homage to you, O ancestors, for the non-terrifying! Homage to you, O ancestors, for life! Homage to you, O ancestors, for savor! <s>Svadhā</s> to you, O ancestors! Homage to you, O ancestors! Homage! These [offerings] are yours, O ancestors; these are ours. May we who are alive, being here, be alive!' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
And with the three [verses beginning] 'Homage, we invoke.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

Then he should send them away: 'Depart, O ancestors, <s>Soma</s>-loving, by the deep paths of the ancients. Having given, bestow upon us good wealth, and grant us riches with all heroes.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Having returned to the fire: 'O <s>Agni</s>, [I praise] you today like a horse with songs of praise.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)

[At] the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire): 'Whatever of the atmosphere, earth, or heaven, whatever of mother or father we may have harmed — may <s>Agni</s> the <s>Gārhapatya</s> release me from that sin; may he make me sinless.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
'Grant me a hero, O ancestors' — [requesting] the middle one of the rice-balls. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
He should feed the wife [saying]: 'O ancestors, place in the womb an embryo, a boy adorned with a lotus garland, so that he may be free from defect.' — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
The other two [rice-balls should be placed] in water. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Or in the <s>atipraṇīta</s> (carried-forward fire). — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Or as the fire-priest [desires], one desiring food — that one should eat [them]. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Or one afflicted by a great illness should eat [them]; one attains one or the other destination. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Thus for one who has not established the fires, in the regular [rite]. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
Having cooked [the rice] and carried [the fire] forward, he should offer oblations. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
The disposal of the utensils is twofold. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
The second [thing] placed in the surplus is grass. — (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
One who is about to undertake the new-moon and full-moon [sacrifices performs] the <s>anvārambhaṇīyā</s> (initiatory offering). — (anvārambhaṇīyā)
[The deities are] <s>Agni</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Sarasvān</s>, <s>Agni</s> the giver. — (anvārambhaṇīyā)

'O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, may you two increase us in unison, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>-descendants; come with splendors and prizes. O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, your great abode is dear; do you two enjoy the hidden ghee of the one who sends [offerings]. In every house, the praise going to you — may the tongue pour forth ghee for you two. <s>Sarasvatī</s> the purifying, the reed-rich, the maiden of wondrous life — the divine, beautiful eagle-like bird of <s>Sarasvat</s>, the great, the soma-pressing of <s>Savitṛ</s> — may he bring us blessings!' — (anvārambhaṇīyā)
If after the establishment [of fires] one becomes ill, or if affairs go wrong, [there is] the re-establishment offering. — (punarādheya)
In that [offering], one should sacrifice the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) and <s>anuyājas</s> (subsequent offerings) with divisions. — (punarādheya)

'O <s>Agni</s>, may the fuel-sticks for <s>Agni</s> go with <s>ājya</s>! May <s>Tanūnapāt</s> go for <s>Agni</s> with <s>ājya</s>! May the <s>Iḍā</s>-[offerings] go with <s>Agni</s> for <s>Agni</s> with <s>ājya</s>! May <s>Agni</s> on the sacred grass go for <s>Agni</s> with <s>ājya</s>!' — (punarādheya)
'Serve <s>Agni</s> with fuel-sticks; come, I shall speak to you' — these two [verses] are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions) for <s>Agni</s>. — (punarādheya)
They are called 'the one possessing intelligence' and 'the one possessing the moon-drop.' — (punarādheya)
Thus the procedure [continues]. — (punarādheya)
And the offering [continues likewise]. — (punarādheya)
The regular [rite comes] first, [according to] those who follow the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. — (punarādheya)
'O <s>Agni</s>, purify the life-spans' — this is the latter [verse]. — (punarādheya)
But in the regular [rite], the word '<s>havis</s>' (oblation) is in the latter [verse]. — (punarādheya)

The oblation is for <s>Agni</s>: 'O <s>Agni</s>, indeed, of the rite, of the auspicious — with these your praises today, by these our songs — O <s>Agni</s>, like a horse today with songs of praise' — [these are] the concluding offerings. — (punarādheya)

'May the divine sacred grass go for <s>Agni</s> at the winning of wealth, at the wealth-giving; may the divine <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> go for <s>Agni</s> at the winning of wealth, at the wealth-giving.' — (punarādheya)
The <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering) [is performed] with rice, <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet), and barley.
One should not eat the [new] grain without having offered the <s>agnihotra</s>.
When one is satisfied with the year's [harvest], then one should sacrifice with the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>.

Or [as] the gods say: 'He is now satisfied with the year's [harvest]; let him sacrifice with the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>.' One should indeed milk the <s>agnihotrī</s> (agnihotra cow), or having milked her, one should offer with her milk.
Or the rite [may be performed] with barley.
But [it is] an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) for a king.
And some [say it is] for all.
In the <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) offering, [there is] a <s>caru</s> (oblation) for <s>Soma</s>.
