'O <s>Soma</s>, those life-giving [powers] of yours, those abodes of yours in heaven and on earth' — having recited the constant <s>japa</s> (murmured prayer) of the intermediate <s>iḷā</s>, placing [it] in the left hand, one should touch [the grain] with the other [hand, saying]: 'I take this offering for <s>Prajāpati</s>, for my prosperity, for my glory, for my food.'

'The auspicious food — the gods have won the better [portion] with you; by your help may we partake of you. Enter us like a father, O life-giving one; be auspicious to us here, be well-being for the biped, well-being for the quadruped.' Having tasted and sipped water, one should touch the navel [saying]: '<s>Amo</s> (that one), you are <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath); that is truth I speak; you are the home; you have entered all. Removing old age and disease from [my] body, abide in me; may we not be harmed, O <s>Indra</s>.'
By this [procedure], the partakers [consume] the ritual shares — everywhere at the first eating [of new grain].
Now for rice and barley, the <s>dhāyyā</s> (introductory) [verses are] in the <s>Virāj</s> [meter].

<s>Agni</s>-<s>Indra</s> or <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-gods), <s>Soma</s> — if <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) is [included] there, <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth) [are the deities].

'Indeed, those who kindle <s>Agni</s>, skilled in work, beautiful in splendor, devoted to the gods.' 'All gods, come — whatever [gods] are on the earth, mighty, free from guile.' 'Great heaven and earth, our primordial parents, with newest [hymns].'
Now [follow] the desire offerings (<s>kāmya iṣṭayaḥ</s>).
In the offering for one desiring long life, [there are two deities who are] possessors of life.
'O <s>Agni</s>, with bright perception.' 'O <s>Soma</s>, for great fortune.' <s>Agni</s> is the giver of long life, <s>Indra</s> is the protector.

'May life-span be placed for you from all sides; this <s>Agni</s> is the most excellent. May your <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) come back to you; I drive away disease from you. O <s>Agni</s>, giver of life, delighting in the oblation, ghee-faced, ghee-born — having drunk ghee and the sweet, beautiful [milk] of cows, protect this [person] like a father [protects] a son.'

'<s>Indra</s> the protector, <s>Indra</s> the helper — in this contest, O mighty one, do not [forsake us]. Protect us, O <s>Agni</s>, with unceasing protections. O <s>Agni</s>, carry us across, O newest one' — [these are] the concluding offering [verses].
In the offering for well-being, [there are two deities who are] protectors.
'O <s>Agni</s>, protect us from distress; O <s>Soma</s>, [protect us] from all sides.'

'<s>Agni</s> [grants] well-being.' 'Well-being to us from heaven, O <s>Agni</s>, from earth.' 'Far from us [be] enmity, far [be] distress' — the previously mentioned [verses are] the concluding offerings.
In the offering for one desiring a son, <s>Agni</s> [grants] offspring.

'To whom you [are born], O <s>Jātavedas</s>, [born] of good deeds; [he] who in his heart, the active one, thinking [of you].' '<s>Agni</s>, the most widely famous' — [these] two [are] the concluding offerings.
The latter [verses are addressed] to <s>Agni</s> [alone].
The regular [offerings] have [the verse] 'head-possessing' (<s>agnir mūrdhā bhuvo yajñasya</s>).
'For you, O best of the <s>Aṅgirases</s> — may we obtain that desire of yours, O <s>Agni</s>' — [this is] for [fulfilling] a desire.
The latter [verses] belong to the <s>Vaimṛdhya</s> (enemy-destroying) [offering].

'Destroy our enemies, O <s>Indra</s>.' 'Like a fearsome wild beast, roaming abroad, dwelling in the mountains.' 'Immediate fall, staggering, downfall, rear collapse — bring forth the <s>pranākāphāna</s>; spreading apart the thighs as if about to fly.' 'Destroy our enemies, O <s>Indra</s>.' 'Stamping like a horse's hoof, lead us to good praise.'
[The offering is] for <s>Indra</s> the giver or <s>Indra</s> the re-giver.

'Whatever riches you destroy for us in anger, O <s>Indra</s>, restore those to us with this oblation. May <s>Indra</s>, the bountiful lord, give us back riches; the powerful one, rich in wealth, generous — may he turn his mind toward us when invoked; may <s>Indra</s>, propitiated with the oblation, be gracious to us.'
[The offering is] for the directions or for the guardians of the directions.

'To the guardians of the directions, the four immortal overseers of beings — to them may we make offerings with oblations. May I unite all directions with sweetness; may the waters and plants all be free from disease. May this sacrificer overcome enmities; may all cattle remain uncaptured.'
The <s>loka-iṣṭi</s> (offering for [the attainment of] worlds).
Earth, atmosphere, and heaven are the deities.

'The great mother Earth, I invoke the atmosphere. The vast heaven for protection.' 'Earth bears everything; the atmosphere spreads wide; the great heaven yields milk.' 'The great Earth is my armor, the atmosphere [is] for my well-being, heaven [is] my shelter and great fame' — three [verses for each] of the three [deities].
The first [verse] of the first [deity], the last [verse] of the middle [deity].
The <s>Mitravindā</s> [offering is] a <s>Mahāvairājī</s> (great Virāj offering).
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> — [these are] the individual offerings.

'<s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s> who [gives] a thousand, may <s>Pūṣan</s> protect us with cattle, may <s>Sarasvatī</s> [protect us]; may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> anoint the sacrifice with form.'

Addressing [them] in reverse order, one should sacrifice [saying]: 'We who sacrifice to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agni</s> — <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> bestowing forms, <s>Sarasvatī</s> [bestowing] fortune, <s>Pūṣan</s>, may <s>Savitṛ</s> give to us, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> giving, <s>Indra</s> [giving] a thousand, <s>Mitra</s> the giver, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agni</s>.'
There are eight <s>Vairāja</s>-based [offerings].
Of these, the first six have a single oblation [each].
One performing a hostile rite should sacrifice with the <s>snuṣā-śvaśurīya</s> (daughter-in-law and father-in-law) [offering].

'<s>Indra</s> the hero has crossed over the realms; the daughter-in-law is my rival — I am the father-in-law. I conquer enemies, exulting; I win the prize in the contest for prizes.' '<s>Indra</s> the hero, foremost, maker of all, accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, with well-born troops — my daughter-in-law, having entered the father-in-law's [domain], let the rival attend upon [my] speech with [her] mind.'
'Welcomed, O generous <s>Agni</s>, make strong, for great good fortune' — [these are] the concluding offerings.
For those who disagree, for the purpose of agreement, [there is] the <s>Saṃjñānī</s> (concord) [offering].
<s>Agni</s> with the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s> — [these are] the individual offerings.

'May <s>Agni</s> first protect us with the <s>Vasus</s>; may <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rudras</s> guard us by himself. May <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s> make [it] according to season; may <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s> grant us shelter.' 'May <s>Agni</s> with the <s>Vasus</s> protect us; may <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rudra</s>-bodied ones [protect us]; may <s>Indra</s>, invoked for gifts, with the <s>Maruts</s> [protect us]; may <s>Varuṇa</s>, the all-knowing, with the <s>Ādityas</s> [protect us].'
Those desiring division [of foes should perform] an <s>Aindrāmārutī</s> (Indra-Marut) [offering].
'The <s>Maruts</s>, in whose dwelling' — 'for the mighty <s>Māruta</s> [host], self-radiant.'

Having recited the <s>Aindrī</s> (Indra-verse), one should sacrifice with the <s>Mārutī</s> (Marut-verse); having recited the <s>Mārutī</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Aindrī</s>; <s>Indra</s> first in the invocations, or the <s>Maruts</s>.
Or <s>Indra</s> [first]; from the principal offering onward, the <s>Maruts</s>.
Those desiring success in the natural way [should perform] the <s>Saṃjñānī</s> (concord offering) as well.
Those being overpowered [should perform] an <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatyā</s> (Indra-Bṛhaspati) [offering].
'Come to us, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; for this one, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>' — even if they should invoke [them] for <s>Indra</s> [alone].
In the <s>Pavitra-iṣṭi</s> (purificatory offering) —

body.text: apām.idma.nyayanam.samudrasya.niveśanam./.anyante.asmat.tapantu.hetayaḥ.pāvako.asmabhyam.śivo.bhava./.namas.te.harase.śociṣe.namas.te.astv.arciṣe./.anyante.asmat.tapantu.hetayaḥ.pāvako.asmabhyam.śivo.bhava.iti.pāvakavatyo.dhāyye./ (Kāmya.iṣṭayah) (2 and the rest are not found in BI ed.)
body.translated_text: 'We know the kindling-place of the waters, the resting-place of the ocean. May the missiles that hurt others [and not us]; be auspicious to us, O purifying one. Homage to your heat, to your flame — may the missiles that hurt others [and not us]; be auspicious to us, O purifying one' — the <s>dhāyyā</s> (introductory) [verses] contain [the word] 'purifying'.
The <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) contain [the word] 'purifying'.
'<s>Agni</s> drives away the <s>rakṣas</s> (demons).'
'He who with a purifying stream.'
The <s>ṛc</s> (verse) [is] the offering verse.
'That purifier of yours which flows in the flame, in the vessels.'
'Purifier' — these [are the verses].

<s>Agni</s> <s>Pavamāna</s> (the purifying fire), <s>Sarasvatī</s> the beloved, <s>Agni</s> <s>Pāvaka</s> (the bright purifier), <s>Savitṛ</s> the true impeller, <s>Agni</s> <s>Śuci</s> (the pure one), <s>Vāyu</s> with his teams, <s>Agni</s> <s>Vratapati</s> (lord of vows), <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>, <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>.
'And to us, among dear and not-dear [people], these [women] offering, from you, with salutations.'
'<s>Vāyu</s> going foremost, delighting in sacrifice.' 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, bright one, I come to you.'
'I have praised <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>.' 'This <s>Dadhikrāvan</s> [has surpassed] the five peoples with his might.'
'Welcomed, O generous <s>Agni</s>, make strong, for great good fortune' — [these are] the concluding offerings.
This [purificatory offering is] for one who has been away for a year.
Or for one desiring purification.

On this, the following sacrificial verse (<s>yajña-gāthā</s>) is sung: 'Employing the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s>, the <s>Vrātapatī</s>, and the <s>Pavitra-iṣṭi</s> offerings — the one who increases truth purifies ten generations.'
The offering for one desiring rain is the <s>Kārīrī</s>.
In that [offering], 'For this sacrifice, I praise <s>Agni</s>, the self-sustained, with salutations' — [this is] the <s>dhāyyā</s> (introductory verse).
Whatever [offerings] in the rain-desiring sacrifice have [verses] mentioning water, [use those with] the two water-containing [verses].
'In the waters, O <s>Agni</s>, is your seat.' '<s>Soma</s> has spoken to me in the waters.'
<s>Agni</s> [seeking] his abode, the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Sūrya</s> [are the deities].
And three additional <s>piṇḍya</s> [verses follow].

'Golden-haired, extending across the atmosphere' — two [verses]. 'You, those immovable [things].' 'In your abode, all the world is established.' Or: 'Like a lowing cow, the lightning flashes; even the mountain, the greatly grown one, trembles. They send forth the ray with might. Driving with the strongest ones, you go along the thread.' 'Stir up from the ocean, O <s>Maruts</s>.' 'Forth, O <s>Maruts</s>, of mighty power, seeking rain.' 'O men, generous ones, [give] to the worshiper.' 'Lightning flashing, O men, with thunderbolts of stone.' 'The dark covering — the tawny ones, the fair-winged.' 'With teams, like village-conquerors, as men.'

'O <s>Agni</s>, drive away the hostile ones.' 'The planets know.' 'O <s>Agni</s>, when <s>Devāpi</s>, blazing, [praised you]' — [these are] the concluding offerings. Having recited the <s>ṛc</s> verses, some sacrifice with <s>yajus</s> formulas.

When [the sacrifice] is completed, one should worship all the directions [reciting] 'Speak forth to the mighty one with these hymns' — with the four [verses], verse by verse, or with [the entire] hymn.
From here onward [follow] the <s>iṣṭi</s>-<s>ayanas</s> (seasonal offerings).
[These are] annual [offerings].
Their performance [is] on the full-moon day of <s>Phālgunī</s> or of <s>Caitra</s>. — (ayana offerings)
<s>Turāyaṇa</s> [rite]. — (ayana offerings)
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> — separate offerings for each pressing (<s>savana</s>), day after day. — (ayana offerings)
Or a single [offering] with three oblations. — (ayana offerings)
In the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice, one should offer two [rites] on the full-moon days and two on the new-moon days. — (ayana offerings)
The first two are regular, as for one who does not follow [the special rites], on the new-moon day. — (ayana offerings)
Of the latter two, the <s>Aindra</s> (offering to <s>Indra</s>) [is performed] on the full-moon day as the second. — (ayana offerings)
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> (offering to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>) [is performed] on the new-moon day. — (ayana offerings)
'O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, what is most expansive for us, O bountiful ones, not transgressing' — [this is recited] below the <s>Prājāpatya</s> <s>iḍā</s>. — (ayana offerings)

'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you [encompasses] these; yours are these worlds, the intermediate directions, and the cardinal directions, the remote places, the lowlands, and the highlands. O <s>Prajāpati</s>, creator of all, living and prosperous — accept this our offering, O god.' Thus [is] the <s>ayana</s> of heaven and earth. — (ayana offerings)
With the full-moon [rite], from the new-moon [day]; with the new-moon [rite], up to the full-moon [day]. — (ayana offerings)
In [rites] not [explicitly] taught [in tradition], the modification of the procedure [is derived] from the purpose. — (general rules)
Or the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) [should perform] as he remembers. — (general rules)
But the <s>Vairāja</s> [meter is used] in the fire-churning. — (general rules)
But some [say it should be in] the <s>dhāyya</s> [chant]. — (general rules)
The <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) are characterized by the deity. — (general rules)

The <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) is characterized by having the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter], containing 'āvatī,' containing 'hūta' (invoked), containing 'upokta' (praised), [and] the preceding characteristic. — (general rules)

The <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) is characterized by having the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter], containing 'vīta,' containing 'juṣṭa' (enjoyed), [and] the following characteristic. Or even of another meter. — (general rules)
But the <s>yājyā</s> should not be shorter [than the <s>anuvākyā</s>]. — (general rules)
Not [in] <s>Uṣṇih</s> [meter], not [in] <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter]. — (general rules)
But one should avoid [verses] containing [words meaning] 'emaciated,' 'lost,' 'slain,' or 'burnt.' — (general rules)
But when the deity is clearly indicated, just so [the verse is selected]. — (general rules)
Or by characteristic when [the deity is] not clearly indicated. — (general rules)
If one cannot find [an appropriate verse] at all, [one uses a verse] addressed to all [deities]. — (general rules)
If one cannot find [any], [one uses verses] addressed to <s>Agni</s>. — (general rules)
Or with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances: <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>). — (general rules)
Having addressed the deity, one should recite and offer. — (general rules)
Or with two <s>naṃrā</s> (humble/submissive) [verses]. — (general rules)

'Hear this invocation of ours; you whom we invoke with songs — come and sit upon this <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) of ours. The <s>barhis</s> is spread out in order; sit down upon this, O implored one, come to us here today. With an unangered mind, enjoy this; consume the offering presented and offered' — these are the <s>naṃrā</s> [verses]. — (general rules)
[Verses] addressed to <s>Agni</s> [are used] when [the deity is] unspecified. — (general rules)
One who is about to perform the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites, on the day before, [performs] the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>-<s>Pārjanya</s> [offering]. — (general rules)

'<s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>Agni</s> has generated for us the newest thought, growing strong with power. Placed on high in heaven, placed on earth, <s>Agni</s> — sing forth for <s>Parjanya</s>; the winds blow forth, the lightnings flash' — from the <s>agnyādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) onward, the endings are whispered for the <s>havis</s> (oblation). — (general rules)
[Likewise] the <s>Saumikī</s> (Soma-related) [verses]. — (general rules)
[Likewise] the <s>Prāyaścittikī</s> (expiatory) [verses]. — (general rules)
The <s>anvāyātyā</s> (accompanying) offerings are single-dish (<s>ekakapāla</s>). — (general rules)
Everywhere, except the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (offering to <s>Varuṇa</s>). — (general rules)
The <s>Sāvitra</s> (offering to <s>Savitṛ</s>) [is performed] in the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal rites). — (general rules)
And some [include] the principal oblations [as well]. — (general rules)
The <s>Pitṛyā</s> (ancestral) and <s>Upasad</s> (approach offerings) share the same ritual procedure (<s>tantra</s>). — (general rules)
And the <s>Paunarādheyikī</s> (re-establishment offering) [is performed] before the last <s>anuyāja</s> (after-offering). — (general rules)
Or [these are performed] sharing the procedure with the <s>Sumandra</s> [offering]. — (general rules)
The <s>āguḥ</s> (response), <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>), and <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation) are [recited] aloud everywhere. — (general rules)
Likewise in the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering), the first-fruits [oblation]. — (general rules)
But for the <s>āhārya</s> (secondary fire), the <s>praṇava</s> of the <s>puronuvākhyā</s> (introductory litany) is connected with the breath [i.e., recited softly]. — (general rules)
Likewise the <s>āguḥ</s> (response) and <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation) of the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse). — (general rules)
The <s>svaras</s> (accents) of the principal rite [that are normally] whispered are [recited] loudly. — (general rules)
[Those that are normally] loud in the principal rites [are recited] softly [when whispered]. — (general rules)

In the morning, when instructed at the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (offering to all gods), [the <s>hotṛ</s>] recites the fire-churning [verses] after [the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses]; after the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses, having stood at a footstep's distance from the [altar] place, having uttered the <s>hiṃkāra</s>. — (vaiśvadeva)

'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, great heaven and earth for us; you, O <s>Agni</s>, from the lotus' — having left a half-verse of three [verses], he should pause until the <s>sampraiṣa</s> (direction). — (vaiśvadeva)
Elsewhere also [one pauses] at the end of a verse; but when this [the fire] is being born, at this very end. — (vaiśvadeva)
'O <s>Agni</s>, you destroy the enemy' — this hymn should be inserted, again and again from [its] birth. — (vaiśvadeva)
Having heard [that the fire is] born, with the immediately following <s>praṇava</s>, one should continue the remainder. — (vaiśvadeva)
With the remainder [one should complete] the next [verse]. — (vaiśvadeva)

'And let the creatures speak; this one with hand [holds] the wooden implement' — at the half-verse one should pause. 'Forth to the divine god for invocations' — these two [verses]: '<s>Agni</s> is kindled by <s>Agni</s>; you indeed, O <s>Agni</s>, by <s>Agni</s>; they won him of good wisdom; with sacrifice they sacrificed the sacrifice, the gods' — one should place the enclosing sticks [while reciting these]. — (vaiśvadeva)
One should know that the last [verse] everywhere is the enclosing verse (<s>paridhānīyā</s>). — (vaiśvadeva)

In the <s>dhāyya</s> [chant], the <s>Virāj</s> [meters]; nine <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings); before the last [prayāja], four should be inserted: 'O <s>Agni</s>, may the doors of the ghee open; O <s>Uṣas</s> and <s>Naktā</s> (Dawn and Night), may they enjoy <s>Agni</s>'s ghee; O divine <s>hotṛs</s>, may they enjoy <s>Agni</s>'s ghee; O three goddesses, may they enjoy <s>Agni</s>'s ghee.' — (vaiśvadeva)
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, the self-powerful ones, <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>, <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth). — (vaiśvadeva)

'To the all-divine true lord; beautiful [blessing] today, O <s>Savitṛ</s>, and beautiful tomorrow; O <s>Pūṣan</s>, in your ordinance, we; your one form is bright, your other form is worthy of sacrifice; here and here, O self-powerful ones; sing forth the wondrous hymn to the swift one' — thus [are the verses]. — (vaiśvadeva)

Nine <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings); six beyond the first: 'May the divine doors open for wealth-winning, for wealth-bestowing. May the divine <s>Uṣas</s> and <s>Naktā</s> enjoy for wealth-winning, for wealth-bestowing. May the divine <s>Joṣṭrī</s> (the delighting one) enjoy for wealth-winning, for wealth-bestowing. May the divine <s>Ūrjāhutī</s> (invigorating offerings) enjoy for wealth-winning, for wealth-bestowing. May the divine <s>Hotṛs</s> enjoy for wealth-winning, for wealth-bestowing. May the three divine goddesses enjoy for wealth-winning, for wealth-bestowing.' — (vaiśvadeva)

After the <s>sūktavāka</s> or <s>śaṃyuvāka</s> of the after-offerings, without summoning [with] the <s>vājin</s> (swift one) [formula], the instruction [is given] for the <s>vājin</s> offerings. — (vaiśvadeva)

'May the swift ones be auspicious for us at the invocations; at contest after contest, protect us, O swift ones' — with upward <s>jñu</s> (knee), without lowering, [he recites] the offering verse. — (vaiśvadeva)

'O <s>Agni</s>, consume' — this is the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response exclamation) for the <s>vājin</s> [offering]; or 'O <s>Agni</s>, consume the <s>vājin</s>.' Wherever in a single <s>sampraiṣa</s> (direction) there are two <s>vaṣaṭkāras</s> together, there one should respond twice. — (vaiśvadeva)
And there is no <s>āguḥ</s> (response) at the second one. — (vaiśvadeva)
Having received the <s>vājin</s> portion like the <s>iḍā</s> (refreshment portion), one should wish for the <s>upahava</s> (invitation). — (vaiśvadeva)
'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, invite; O <s>Brahman</s>, invite; O <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, invite.' — (vaiśvadeva)

'Whatever seed of mine is scattered, whatever goes forth from me, whatever is born again — may that enter me auspiciously, may that make me vigorous. Of that <s>vājin</s> (swift offering) partaken, of that which has been invited, being invited, I partake' — thus one should partake of the <s>prāṇabhakṣa</s> (breath-partaking). — (vaiśvadeva)
Likewise the <s>adhvaryu</s>, the <s>brahman</s>, and the <s>āgnīdhra</s> [partake]. — (vaiśvadeva)
The <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) [partakes] visibly, and so do the other consecrated ones (<s>dīkṣitas</s>). — (vaiśvadeva)
Having sacrificed with the full-moon [rite], one should undertake the observances of the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites. — (vaiśvadeva)
One should let the hair [on the head] grow back. — (vaiśvadeva)
One should have the beard shaved. One should sleep on the ground. One should avoid honey, meat, salt, women, and ointments. — (vaiśvadeva)
One should approach one's wife during her season. — (vaiśvadeva)
Shaving [is prescribed] at all the <s>parvan</s> (juncture days). — (vaiśvadeva)
Or at the first and last [parvan days]. — (vaiśvadeva)
On the fifth full-moon day, [one performs] the <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s> (offerings to <s>Varuṇa</s> with barley). — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
Having sat down behind the <s>vedi</s> (altar) of the <s>Darśapaurṇamāsika</s> (new- and full-moon rites), when instructed, [the <s>hotṛ</s>] begins the fire-carrying [verses]. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)

'Forth to the divine [fire] with divine thought' — three [verses]; but for the <s>iḍā</s>, 'O waters, O divine one, O <s>Agni</s>, with all [gods], O one of beautiful appearance, with the gods' — at the half-verse one should pause. Seated, he recites the first [verse] in a whisper with <s>praṇava</s>. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
There, in transitioning from one station to another, having concluded with <s>praṇava</s> and having paused for breath, he begins the next [verse]. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
It is known that [the recitation] is connected with the breath. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
Following the fire forward, the subsequent [verses are recited]. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)

'This great power for the wise one at the assembly; this one was established here first by the ordainers' — but these two [are recited] at the beginning for a <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior) and <s>Vaiśya</s> (commoner). — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
Having stationed oneself behind the northern <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
But on the northern <s>vedi</s> in <s>Soma</s> sacrifices. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)

When the fire has been placed, [reciting] 'Sit, O <s>hotṛ</s>, in your own seat, knowing; the <s>hotṛ</s> knowing [sits] in the <s>hotṛ</s>'s seat' — having placed the two enclosing [sticks] with these two [verses], sitting down in that very seat, one should release the voice [saying] '<s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>.' — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
Elsewhere too, wherever [the <s>hotṛ</s>] follows while reciting. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
Standing during the <s>sampraiṣas</s> (directions), the voice-release is likewise. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
From the fire-churning onward, [the procedure is] the same as in the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> [offering]. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
But in the place of the oblations from the sixth onward: <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Ka</s> (Who? / <s>Prajāpati</s>). — (varuṇa-praghāsa)

'O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, come with help; he shatters <s>Vṛtra</s> and wins the prize; O <s>Maruts</s>, in whose abode; like spokes of a wheel, this one; hear this [prayer] of mine, O <s>Varuṇa</s>; I approach you with prayer, O worshipful one; who is our <s>Citra</s> (wondrous one); <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (golden embryo) came into being' — the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> [is] third [in reciting] to the <s>vājin</s> [offering] to <s>Agni</s>. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
When [the rite] is concluded, they proceed to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath). — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
There the <s>avabhṛtha</s> offering is partly done and partly not done. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
We shall explain that further on. At [the interval of] two months, [there is] an animal [sacrifice] for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>. — (varuṇa-praghāsa)
Likewise after that, the <s>Sākamedhas</s> (communal offerings). — (sāka-medha)
On the day before, three offerings for each pressing (<s>savana</s>). — (sāka-medha)

In the first [offering], <s>Agni Anīkavān</s> (having a face/front): 'We invoke <s>Agni</s> of shining face for aid with songs. May he carry us past [our] enemies.' In the next [offering], the two with 'growing': '<s>Maruts</s> <s>Sāṃtapanāḥ</s> (the scorching ones); this oblation [is] for the <s>Sāṃtapanāḥ</s>; you, O <s>Maruts</s>, who [hurt] the malicious one' — the latter [verse] for the <s>Maruts Gṛhamedhas</s> (householder Maruts), from the ghee-portion shares onward, up to the <s>iḍā</s>. — (sāka-medha)
'O <s>Gṛhamedhas</s>, come; from the depths they arise; great ones' — thus [are the verses]. — (sāka-medha)
The two <s>Puṣṭimant</s> (nourishing) <s>Virāj</s> [meters] at the concluding offering (<s>saṃyājya</s>), without the <s>nigada</s> (verbal direction). — (sāka-medha)
Elsewhere too, when there is no summoning. — (sāka-medha)
But [the <s>nigada</s> is used] at the summoning, in the ancestral [rite], and in the animal [sacrifice]. — (sāka-medha)
And on this night, much food [should be distributed] along with excellent heroes. — (sāka-medha)
At that [ceremony's] non-performance, they should offer the <s>paurṇadarvī</s> (full-ladle offering). — (sākamedha)
When a bull bellows. — (sākamedha)
Or when there is thunder. — (sākamedha)
Some indeed cause the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler) to sound, calling it the son of <s>Brahman</s>. — (sākamedha)

If they should prompt the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker), his <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) are: 'O full ladle, fly away; well-filled, come back again. Like a merchant let us trade — nourishment and vigor, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (hundred-powered one). Give to me, I give to you; place [it] in me, I place [it] in you. Like the gatherer of waters — the mother gives, giving and giving.' — (sākamedha)
The latter [verse is addressed] to the <s>Maruts</s>, the playful ones. — (sākamedha)
'And let the creatures say: "This doer [of deeds] has not been seized"' — the two [verses] about the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> spoken indirectly. — (sākamedha)
'Your playful host, O <s>Maruts</s>, [is] like swift horses; the <s>Maruts</s> who are self-moving.' — (sākamedha)

'Being gratified, O bountiful <s>Agni</s>, [bring] the host for great good fortune' — thus the <s>saṃyājyā</s> (concluding offering verse). Except for the <s>vājina</s> (prize-contest) and <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), the <s>māhendrī</s> (verses to <s>Mahendra</s>) are stated along with the <s>varuṇapraghāsas</s>. — (sākamedha)
But for the seventh and subsequent oblations, in place [of those deities stands] <s>Indra</s> the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, or <s>Indra Mahendra</s>, or <s>Viśvakarman</s>. — (sākamedha)

'Come to us, O <s>Indra</s>, slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>; [this offering] has been given for your great <s>Indriya</s> (might); O <s>Viśvakarman</s>, growing by the oblation; [we know] those supreme abodes of yours and those nearest' — thus. — (sākamedha)
Having carried <s>Agni</s> forward past the southern fire, the <s>pitryā</s> (ancestral rites) [are performed]. — (pitryā)
That [rite] ends with the <s>śaṃyuvāka</s> (tranquility formula). — (pitryā)

With suppressed recitation — the <s>hotṛ</s> [acts] without [the usual] <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call), <s>anumantraṇa</s> (accompanying mantras), and <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (exclamatory utterance), except [what is required]. — (pitryā)
In that [rite], five ritual acts [are performed] as the southern [rites]. — (pitryā)
The other [rites follow] in accordance with the regular order. — (pitryā)
'Willingly we establish you' — this [verse] repeated thrice without intermission constitutes the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses). — (pitryā)
With the final <s>praṇava</s> (sacred syllable 'Om') of those, the instruction is: 'Bring the gods and the ancestors to the sacrificer.' — (pitryā)
In place of '<s>Agni</s>, bring for the <s>hotra</s> (oblation), bring your own greatness,' one should invoke '<s>Agni</s> the bearer of offerings to the ancestors.' — (pitryā)
And in the last <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering), one should introduce him before the <s>ājyapas</s> (ghee-drinkers). — (pitryā)
And in the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn recitation), in place of '<s>Agni</s> through the <s>hotra</s>.' — (pitryā)
Here there is no <s>prādeśa</s> (pointing out). — (pitryā)
No <s>mārjana</s> (purification). — (pitryā)
No name-designation in the <s>sūktavāka</s>. — (pitryā)
Having been observed, one should sit down — or when told 'Sit down, O <s>hotṛ</s>.' — (pitryā)
With life-sustaining [mantras], wearing [the sacred thread] over the left shoulder, they perform the rites with oblations, with the sacred thread arranged to the left. — (pitryā)

The <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler) [stands] to the south, the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) to the north. Two <s>anuvākyās</s> (invitatory verses) each. The <s>anavāna</s> (uninterrupted recitation) [is] one and a half [verses]. — (pitryā)
'Om <s>svadhā</s>' is the call. 'Let there be <s>svadhā</s>' is the response. 'Along with <s>svadhā</s>, <s>svadhā</s>' is the directive. — (pitryā)
Those who say 'Ye <s>svadhā</s>' or 'Ye <s>svadhā</s>, great one.' '<s>Svadhā</s> namaḥ' is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation). — (pitryā)
The prolonged vowels (<s>pluta</s>) are obligatory. — (pitryā)
The ancestors with <s>Soma</s>, or <s>Soma</s> accompanied by the ancestors; the ancestors seated on the sacred grass; the ancestors consumed by fire; <s>Yama</s>. — (pitryā)

'Let the lower ones rise up and the higher ones; you, O ancestors possessed of <s>Soma</s>, first invoked; O ancestors of the <s>Soma</s> [offering], you, O <s>Soma</s>, discerned with wisdom; <s>Soma</s> [gave] the cow, <s>Soma</s> the swift horse; you, O <s>Soma</s>, in accord with the ancestors; O ancestors seated on the sacred grass, [come] here for protection; I have found the ancestors of good offering; homage be to the ancestors today; O ancestors consumed by <s>Agni</s>'s fire, come here; and those ancestors who are here and those who are not here; those burnt by fire and those not burnt by fire; O <s>Yama</s>, sit upon this seat of sacred grass' — two [more verses]: 'The one who has departed along the great slopes.' — (pitryā)
If [addressed] to <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>), the middle <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse). — (pitryā)
'Those who thirsted [reaching] toward the gods, crying out; from you, O <s>Agni</s>, the sages, from you the hymns; the wife being produced with a thousand [offspring]' — thus. — (pitryā)
<s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings) [is] the bearer of offerings to the ancestors. — (pitryā)
From here onward, [it follows] the standard procedure. — (pitryā)
And in the performance of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, after the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions), other mantras are omitted. — (pitryā)
And one <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) each. — (pitryā)
'That <s>Agni</s> who carries the flesh-offering; you, O <s>Agni</s>, invoked <s>Jātavedas</s>' — these are the <s>saṃyājyā</s> (concluding offering verses). — (pitryā)

During the <s>bhakṣas</s> (partaking), having partaken of the <s>prāṇabhakṣas</s> (life-breath partakings), they should offer upon the sacred grass. When the [rite] has concluded — or before the two <s>anuyājas</s> (supplementary offerings) — turning southward, they attend upon the southern fire. — (pitryā)
Without turning back, in the procedure of not carrying [the fire] forward. — (pitryā)

'Most unwavering, generating dark [forms], for he of burning [splendor] is the wide path to the spacious one. He rose up [as] the support, the first of honey, when he projected his own body into [another] body.' — (pitryā)
But the other two [priests] indeed turn back. — (pitryā)
[They attend upon] the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) with a <s>paṅkti</s> (five-lined verse): 'You of beautiful appearance.' — (pitryā)
[They attend upon] the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire) with [the verse] 'I consider that <s>Agni</s>' — with a single <s>ṛc</s> (verse), not with a whole hymn. — (pitryā)
Then they approach him, murmuring 'Do not, O <s>Agni</s>, [harm] us' and 'Not [you].' — (pitryā)
Having completed [the rite] to the east of the <s>gārhapatya</s> with the hymn, turning leftward, they make the <s>tryambaka</s> (three-eyed <s>Rudra</s>) offerings. — (pitryā)
There the <s>adhvaryus</s> (officiating priests) study the ritual procedure. — (pitryā)
Having returned, they proceed with the <s>ādityā</s> (solar rite). — (pitryā)
The two <s>dhāyyā</s> (meditative chants) are <s>virāj</s> (sovereign meter) [verses] conferring nourishment. — (pitryā)
On the fifth full-moon day, [one performs] the <s>Śunāsīrīya</s> (rite to <s>Śuna</s> and <s>Sīra</s>). — (śunāsīrīya)
Or earlier, as circumstances permit. — (śunāsīrīya)

Except for the <s>vājina</s> (prize-contest), [the procedure is] the same as the <s>vaiśvadevī</s> (rite to the All-Gods). But in place of the sixth and subsequent oblations, [the deities are] <s>Vāyu</s> with his teams, or <s>Vāyu</s>, or <s>Śunāsīrau</s> (Ploughshare and Plough), or <s>Indra</s> with <s>Śunāsīra</s>, or <s>Indra</s> with <s>Śuna</s>; <s>Sūrya</s> [is] the last. — (śunāsīrīya)

'Come, O <s>Vāyu</s>, be pleased; approach us with your blessings; you go to the generous one. You, O god, with mind — for the sovereign one; what offering has been brought to you; O <s>Śunāsīrau</s>, be pleased with this speech; may the ploughshares furrow auspiciously for us; O <s>Indra</s>, we invoke <s>Śunāsīra</s> in this half [-month].' — (śunāsīrīya)

'May he help us in [winning] prizes. Desiring horses, desiring cattle, seeking prizes — we invoke the auspicious, bountiful <s>Indra</s>. Desiring horses, desiring cattle, seeking prizes — the swift one, visible to all. The brilliant face of the gods has risen' — these are the <s>yājyās</s> (offering verses) and <s>anuvākyās</s> (invitatory verses). — (śunāsīrīya)
Having concluded [the seasonal rites], one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>; if unable, with an animal [sacrifice]. — (śunāsīrīya)
Or the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites again, the <s>cāturmāsya</s> rites again. — (śunāsīrīya)
In the animal sacrifice: — (paśubandha)
An <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) [is performed] on both sides, or on one side. — (paśubandha)
Or [an iṣṭi] dedicated to <s>Agni</s>. — (paśubandha)
Or [an iṣṭi] dedicated to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>. — (paśubandha)
Or both. — (paśubandha)
One of them [is performed] beforehand. — (paśubandha)
The carrying forward of <s>Agni</s> has been stated. — (paśubandha)

Having sat down behind the <s>vedi</s> (altar) of the animal-sacrifice rite, when directed, for the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post) being anointed: 'They anoint you in the sacrifice, being devoted to the gods' — with the last utterance one should stop at the half-verse. — (paśubandha)

'Rise up, O lord of the forest; being raised with the kindled [fire], in front — upward be your aids' — two [verses]. 'Born for the good fortune of days' — one should stop at the half-verse. 'A youth, well-clothed, has come around' — with this one should encircle [the post]. — (paśubandha)

Where in a single ritual there are many [posts] with animals, having encircled the last one, one should recite praise without the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (exclamatory utterance): 'Those which you men, devoted to the gods, have fashioned' — with six [verses]. — (paśubandha)
Or with five. Some [say] without repetition. — (paśubandha)

The fire-churning has been stated; likewise the <s>dhāyyā</s> (meditative chants); the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) [are performed] whether made or unmade. In the invocation, <s>Vanaspati</s> (Lord of the Forest) [comes] immediately after the animal's deity. — (paśubandha)
Having swept with the sweeping-implements, one should offer the <s>pravṛtāhutis</s> (preliminary oblations). — (paśubandha)

'May I be pleasing to Speech; may I be more pleasing to the Lord of Speech. O divine <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), whatever is the sweetest of speech — place me in that. To <s>Sarasvatī</s>, to Speech, <s>svāhā</s>. Having taken again, the five-fold offering: <s>svāhā</s> to Speech, <s>svāhā</s> to the Lord of Speech, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Sarasvat</s>, to the great powers, to the combined powers, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (paśubandha)
Some [say it is addressed] to <s>Soma</s> alone. — (paśubandha)

Having led the <s>praśāstṛ</s> (director) by the ford, one should hand him the staff with the right and left hands [saying]: 'With the two arms of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, as director I hand [you] the direction.' — (paśubandha)
Likewise the other [priest] with the same two [hands] joined: 'With the two arms of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, as director I receive the direction. May I be unbent and unshaken.' — (paśubandha)

Having received [the staff], he should pass beyond the <s>hotṛ</s> to the north, carrying the staff on the right side, and should not touch himself or another with it — until the directive utterance. — (paśubandha)
Other implements of sacrifice that have been employed should not be moved about casually. — (paśubandha)
Standing bent to the south of the <s>hotṛ</s>'s seat, having rested the staff on the <s>vedi</s> (altar), he should pronounce the directives and the instruction. — (paśubandha)
And the <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), when there is a directive, [is recited] before the directive. — (paśubandha)
The <s>paryagni</s> (circumambulation with fire), <s>stoka</s> (drop-offering), <s>manotā</s> (mind-directed rite), and the hymns [recited] while [the animal] is being led up. — (paśubandha)
Being seated with <s>Soma</s>, [one performs] the rest. — (paśubandha)
There are eleven <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings). — (paśubandha)
Their directives [are as follows]. — (paśubandha)
The first directive-hymn. The second has been stated. — (paśubandha)
Directed by the <s>adhvaryu</s>, the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s> (priest of <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>) directs the <s>hotṛ</s> with the directives. — (paśubandha)
The <s>hotṛ</s> sacrifices with the <s>āprī</s> (propitiatory) [hymns] that bear the marks of the directives. — (paśubandha)
'<s>Agni</s> is kindled' — [this is the āprī hymn] of the <s>Śunakas</s>. 'Accept our kindling' — of the <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s>. 'Kindled today' — of all [other schools]. — (paśubandha)
Or according to the [family] seer. — (paśubandha)
But in [the sacrifice] to <s>Prajāpati</s>, [the āprī hymn] of <s>Jāmadagni</s> [is used] for all. — (paśubandha)
When directed at the ten hymns, the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites for the <s>paryagni</s> (circumambulation) the <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse hymn): '<s>Agni</s> the <s>hotṛ</s>, not...' — (paśubandha)

For the <s>adhrigu</s> (the leading of the animal), having been directed and sub-directed — or when told 'O <s>hotṛ</s>' — having uttered the directive '<s>Agni</s> has gone forth, has won the prize,' he deposits the staff within the <s>vedi</s>. — (paśubandha)
The <s>hotṛ</s> [performing] the <s>adhrigu</s>, carrying the limbs, [assigns] the deity to the animal as appropriate. — (paśubandha)
[This applies] in [the sacrifice of] a male [animal] or a pair. — (paśubandha)
[The deities are] the two lords of the sacrificial animal (<s>medhāpatī</s>). — (paśubandha)
There is an option regarding the [cutting of the] <s>medhā</s> (marrow/essence). — (paśubandha)
As appropriate, after the <s>adhrigu</s>, the other [rites] except for the paired [animals]. — (paśubandha)
In all the <s>yajus</s>-recitations that are pronounced aloud. — (paśubandha)
In the standard [rite], in the recitations that have full meaning. — (paśubandha)
But the words of the mantras are indeed the standard ones. — (paśubandha)
Even in substitutions. — (paśubandha)
The navel, analogy, fat, and oblation — these are to be adapted [in the mantras]. — (paśubandha)

O divine <s>śamitṛs</s> (slaughterers), begin! And you human ones, bring [the animal] near. Desiring the sacrificial essence from the consecrated [animal], [obtain] the sacrificial essence for the lords of the sacrifice. Bring forth <s>Agni</s> for him, spread the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass); let the mother acknowledge him, let the father acknowledge, let the brother born of the same womb, let the companion of the same herd [acknowledge]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Place his feet facing northward; send his eye to the sun, his breath to the wind, his vital air to the atmosphere, his hearing to the directions, his body to the earth. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

Let one cut his skin in one piece; before the navel, let one cut out the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) with the cutting tool; keep the heat contained within. Make his chest like a hawk, the forelegs [removed] with the cutting tool, the upper forelegs with the <s>śalā</s> (pin), the two shoulder-blades by the <s>kaśyapa</s> method, the hips at the joint, the thighs [as] <s>sreka</s> (strips), the shanks leaf-shaped, the kneecaps — twenty-six are his ribs; having attended to them, let one remove [them]. Make his every limb complete, not deficient.

Dig a pit for the refuse near the cow-pen on the ground. Mix the blood with the <s>rakṣas</s> (demons, i.e., to ward off demons). Do not disturb his vital sap, thinking it to be nourishment, lest the destroyer destroy among your offspring and descendants, O <s>śamitṛs</s>. O guileless ones, slaughter well, well-slaughtering slaughter, slaughter O guileless ones, sinless! — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'Mix the blood with the <s>rakṣas</s>' and 'O <s>śamitṛs</s>, sinless' — [these are recited] in a low voice. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'In one piece' and 'twenty-six' — [these are recited] twice each when there are many [animals]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'Before' and 'within' — thus some [say]. Having recited the <s>adhṛgu</s> formula three times beginning with 'O guileless ones': 'O <s>śamitṛs</s>, whatever meritorious deed you perform here, may that [come] to us; whatever ill-done, may that [go] elsewhere' — having muttered [this], he turns around turning to the right. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
And the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest does likewise]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
The <s>Brahman</s> [priest] and the sacrificer [turn] to the left. They should turn back when the animal has been suffocated. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

When the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) is being cooked, the one who is directed recites in response to the <s>stokas</s> (drops): 'May [<s>Agni</s>] enjoy the widely extending one, this one' and 'This our sacrifice.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>) (<s>stokīya</s>: <s>stoka sūkta</s> ṚV 3.21)
The sprinkling has been described, [along with] the <s>svāhākṛtis</s> (svāhā invocations). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'Let the <s>hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s>, svāhā! Of the ghee, svāhā! Of the fat' — thus the directive [verse]; the last <s>āprī</s> [verse serves as] the ghee [verse]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
The <s>vapā</s> (omentum), the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake), and the <s>havis</s> (oblation) — these are the offerings of the animal [sacrifice]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
These [are offered] separately to various deities. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
And the <s>manotā</s> [verse]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>) ('For you, O <s>Agni</s>, first [were established as] <s>manotā</s>',
The <s>manotā</s> [verse] should not be repeated — thus some [say]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Their directive [verses] have corresponding characteristics. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
In those [directives], in place of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, whichever deity belongs to the [particular] animal [is substituted]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
For a goat — a bull; for a cow — a ram; for a sheep — a horse; [the term] 'horse' [is used] in the injunction, with explicit designation of the impelling [deity]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Similarly with the <s>vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest), <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings), <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn recitation), and directive [verses]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

However, in a <s>Prājāpatya</s> (offering to <s>Prajāpati</s>) combined with <s>agniciti</s> (fire-altar building), a <s>Vāyavya</s> (offering to <s>Vāyu</s>) cake [is offered] alongside the animal. Some [say] in a <s>Vāyavya</s> [sacrifice], a <s>Prājāpatya</s> [cake] — thereby the animal's deity is enhanced, say the teachers, because the cake is the principal [offering]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
In the prescriptions for the cake, the oblations — like the cake — except ghee, [for] those with which the offering coincides. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'More worthy of the sacrifice' — in the designation of the animal. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'Took,' 'ate,' 'made,' 'enjoyed,' 'grasped,' 'increased' — [these are the verbal forms] of the deities. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

When the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) has been offered, [the priests] together with the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] cleanse themselves at the <s>cātvāla</s> (pit), the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> having laid down the staff. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'O waters, carry this away; may the waters and plants be friendly to us, may they be hostile to him who hates us and whom we hate.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
This much is the purification in the animal [sacrifice]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Having exited by the proper path, one should sit until the cooking of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Having performed with that [offering], they should proceed with the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
But if there are supplementary [offerings], they should proceed with those first. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
But their [application] does not extend to the prescriptions [of the supplementary offerings]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Nor [does it extend] to others that arise after the invocation. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
After the <s>iḷā</s> (offering of refreshment). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Having been directed for the <s>manotā</s>, he recites 'For you, O <s>Agni</s>, first.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
They proceed with the oblation. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
In that directive [verse], 'whichever of the two — <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> indeed thus' — [say] the <s>Aitareyins</s>. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Elsewhere [where there are] two deities each, and the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> deities as well. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Because it is so observed [in scripture]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
[It should follow] the basic form — [says] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
For what has arisen [and is] recorded in the tradition, when there is no difference in meaning, a modification is purposeless. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Between the two half-verses of the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), the <s>vasāhoma</s> (fat oblation) should be performed. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

They proceed with the <s>vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest [offering]). The <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory and offering verses) [are recited] on either side of the directive. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Where [the formula says] 'Of <s>Agni</s>, of the ghee, of the oblation' — there the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) [are offered]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'<s>Ayāḷ</s>, of <s>Agni</s>, of the ghee, of the oblation' — in the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings). Having invoked <s>Iḷā</s>, they proceed with the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Their directives — the third directive hymn, eleven [verses] here. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

Before the last [verse], two should be inserted: 'May the divine <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest) go to the wealth-winning, wealth-bestowing [sacrifice]' and 'May the divine <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) of the <s>vāritī</s> [waters] go to the wealth-winning, wealth-bestowing [sacrifice].' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
He directs the <s>anavāna</s> (unceasing [offering]). He offers the <s>anavāna</s>. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
It has been stated in the last [section]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
In the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn recitation) directive, in the former prescription, where it says 'grasping' — there the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) [are offered]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'Binding such-and-such [animal] to such-and-such [deity], binding such-and-such to such-and-such' — [naming] both the animals and the deities. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Only the deities [are named] when there is a single animal. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Only the animals [are named] when there is a single deity. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
'With the subsequent ghee' — the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions). 'To such-and-such with such-and-such' — has been stated in the preceding [section]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Having completed the directive, one should cast the staff into the fire when there is no <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
At the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), [the staff is cast] elsewhere. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

The done and undone is known [as] the spreading of the grass. Having exited by the proper path, without separating the fire and animal markers, they should consecrate the heart-spit being brought near [reciting]: 'You are pain; afflict him who hates us and whom we hate.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

Above that they touch water [reciting]: 'On the island is the house of King <s>Varuṇa</s>, measured, golden. May that king of firm vows release us here from place to place. From place to place, O King <s>Varuṇa</s>, release us from here.'

'Whatever, O waters, [is] inviolable' — 'if we swear by <s>Varuṇa</s>, from that, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, release us. May the waters and plants not harm me; from that you became all-pervading; from here, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, release us. May the waters and plants be friendly to us.' And [reciting this]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Without touching, without looking back, not making contact [with each other], returning, they make the fuel-sticks — three each, one by one. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'You are the fuel-stick of <s>Agni</s>, you are splendor, give me splendor' — [with this] the first. 'You are kindling, may we kindle' — the second. 'You are a fuel-stick, may we be kindled' — the third. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

Having approached, they stand [reciting]: 'O waters, today we have followed along.' Then they place the fuel-sticks as taken [reciting]: 'Fuel-stick of the limbs of <s>Agni</s>' — 'You are splendor, you have placed splendor in me, svāhā.' 'Fuel-stick of <s>Soma</s>' — 'Protect me from ill-performance, svāhā.' 'Fuel-stick of the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors)' — 'Protect me from death, svāhā.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Then the concluding recitation — thus [ends] the <s>paśutantra</s> (animal sacrifice procedure). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
The directives for the offerings have been stated. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
Their <s>yājyā</s> (offering verses) and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verses) [are as follows]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
For all [offerings], first the <s>anuvākyās</s> (invitatory verses), then the <s>yājyās</s> (offering verses). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)
The variety of animals [is determined] by the deity. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to prosperity' — two [verses]. 'Protect us, O <s>Agni</s>, with unfailing guardians. Give to you the bright radiance. As by the offerings of the wise man, the praises of the reciter being uttered.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'One she is among rivers, <s>Sarasvatī</s>.' And 'May that <s>Sarasvatī</s> delight in us.' '<s>Sarasvatī</s>, lead us to the best.' 'She has flowed forth with flooding nourishment, purifying, radiant, youthful maiden of wondrous life-span. Your breast that is inexhaustible, that which is life-giving.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'You, O <s>Soma</s>, have perceived through wisdom' — two [verses]. 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, [are] our all-protecting strength. Your abodes in heaven and on earth. Unconquered in battles, filling the combats. Your abodes they worship with oblations.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'O <s>Pūṣan</s>, those boats of yours within the ocean' — two [verses]. '<s>Pūṣan</s> knows all these directions. One of yours is bright, the other worthy of worship. <s>Pūṣan</s> was born forth on the path of paths. The lord of the paths, through praise, along the way.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, that which is the highest distance' — two [verses]. 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, beyond what the noble one deserves. The seasonal [hymns of praise] accompany the utterances; the channels of praise lead [them]. Thus indeed to <s>Viśvedeva</s>, the bull, to all the forefathers.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'All the <s>Maruts</s> today with all assistance.' 'May the praise of the gods approach.' 'May all the <s>Viśvedevas</s> come to us.' 'O <s>Viśvedevas</s>, hear this invocation of mine — whoever are powerful, great, free from deceit. O <s>Agni</s>, go as messenger, [may we] not be harmed.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'Men invoke <s>Indra</s>, the irresistible one' — three [verses]. 'You lead us to a wide space, knowing. You have conquered enemies, O much-invoked one. For well-being and with prizes, O leader.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'Pure are your oblations, O <s>Maruts</s>, for the pure ones. Now [give us] the firm, hero-rich [blessing].' 'Your <s>hotṛ</s> seated calls upon you. Sing the wondrous song for the swift one. Like spokes of a wheel, unceasing like days. Whatever shelter [you give] to the toiling one.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'O slayers of <s>Vṛtra</s>, with <s>Vṛtra</s>-slaying powers.' 'Bring [victory], be skilled, O wielders of the thunderbolt. To invoke both of you, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.' 'A pure, newly-born hymn today — the inspired one, seeking wisdom, with songs, has drawn forth [the hymn] from the warrior-clans in battle invocations.' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> of good treasures come' and 'The god <s>Savitṛ</s> the powerful, the conqueror' — two [verses]. 'Raise up the most wise among the wise' and '<s>Bhaga</s>, the prayer, seeking reward, and <s>Purandhī</s> (abundance)' — two [verses]. — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'<s>Varuṇa</s> descended upon the river as heaven stands' and 'This one [is offered] to you, O self-ruling <s>Varuṇa</s>' and 'Thus praise the great <s>Varuṇa</s>' and 'I approach you with prayer, worshipping' — two [verses]. 'The all-knowing <s>Asura</s> established heaven' — [these belong to] the <s>Aikādaśinas</s> (the eleven-verse [section]). — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, accept this [offering] of mine' and 'You two, these lights in heaven' — two <s>tṛcas</s> (sets of three). 'May you, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [accept] the oblation-enjoying [offering].' 'Come, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, with good praise.' 'O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [accept] the oblation-enjoying [offering] for us.' 'You two wear rich garments.' 'Extend your arms, [you who are] the life of the army.' 'When most generous, O bountiful ones, you do not exceed [propriety].' — (<s>paśubandha</s>)

'<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the golden embryo) came into being first' — six [verses] for <s>Prajāpati</s>. 'The wondrous face of the gods rose up' — five. 'Be auspicious to our eye; be auspicious to our days.' 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come purifying, approach us.' 'By whichever [courses] you go to the liberal giver, come to our sacrifice with your hundred-yoked [steeds].' 'Rich in food, increaser of wealth, wise' — 'For wealth, on account of whom the two world-halves were born for me.' 'Toward <s>Vāyu</s> [goes] the great inspired thought.' — (paśubandha)

'Your, O <s>Vāyu</s>, of the one whose [enemy] has been slain' — 'You indeed are of most beautiful splendor' — these two. 'Will he indeed?' 'By homage those who have grown powerful.' 'For the Lord, whoever has brought the offering forth.' 'Toward <s>Vāyu</s>, harness-yoked, make [him ready] for you.' 'And you, O <s>Aditi</s>, the great, without hostility.' 'Wide the enclosure; <s>Aditi</s> indeed was born for good protection.' 'Earth, heaven, without hostility.' 'Great, O mother of the pious, <s>Aditi</s> is heaven, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere.' — (paśubandha)

'No one born, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nor yet born' — 'You, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of all-encompassing benevolence.' 'He strode across the earth, this very one.' 'Thrice the god [strode across] this earth.' 'He grew beyond the measure, with his body.' 'Rich in refreshment, rich in cows, indeed, is the earth.' — (paśubandha)

'O <s>Viśvakarman</s>, having grown with the oblation' — two. '<s>Viśvakarman</s>, the wise-minded, from the vast expanse.' 'What was the support?' 'He who is our father, the begetter, the ordainer.' 'Your supreme abodes [we seek] with grain.' — (paśubandha)

'O you in whom these heaven and earth, the two progenitresses' — 'That is our fourth, that which nourishes.' 'The god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, of all forms.' 'For the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, what beauty he has attained.' 'Of tawny form, the good bearer, the sustainer of life.' 'The first partaker, the glorious, the sustainer of life.' — (paśubandha)

'O <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>, the generators of riches' — [the entire] hymn. 'With the recent help of the <s>Ādityas</s>.' 'These songs to the <s>Ādityas</s>, dripping with ghee.' 'Those <s>Ādityas</s>, vast and deep.' 'This praise, O you of united power, today for me.' 'Three earths they upheld and three heavens.' 'Not with the right [hand] does the left discern.' — (paśubandha)

'Great heaven and earth, the eldest here.' 'Truth I spoke to heaven, that I proclaimed to earth' — these two. 'Forth with twofold sacrifices and homages, earth' — these two. 'Forth with sacrifices, earth the truth-increaser, heaven.' — (paśubandha)

'Be merciful to us, O <s>Rudra</s>, and make us joyful' — these two. 'May the benevolence of you, the father of the <s>Maruts</s>, come to us.' 'To the tawny one, the bull, and the bright one' — these three. — (paśubandha)

'From behind, O <s>Nāsatyas</s> (Aśvins), from the front.' 'O <s>Gotamas</s>, [come] with the chariot, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>' — these four. 'O golden one, honey-colored, dripping with ghee.' 'With creative power, O <s>Indra</s>, you became supreme on earth.' 'You are great, O <s>Indra</s>; to you the [mountains] yield.' 'The ever-conquering, the bold, the mighty <s>Indra</s>.' 'Much-invoked, dwelling with <s>Dānu</s>.' 'The praised <s>Indra</s>, the bountiful, when indeed the enemies.' 'Thus is <s>Indra</s>, the true, the sovereign.' — (paśubandha)

'What speech speaks, not understanding.' '<s>Pataṅga</s> (the sun-bird) bears speech with the mind.' 'Speech has four measured feet.' 'By sacrifice they followed the track of speech' — these two. 'The gods generated the divine speech.' — (paśubandha)

'Being born, they went forward' — these three. 'The divine, beautiful eagle-like bird, the great' — 'He has grown among the women of the hero.' 'He whose ordinance all animals follow.' 'He whose ordinance the waters attend upon.' 'He whose ordinance <s>Puṣṭipati</s> (lord of nourishment) has accepted.' 'That <s>Sarasvat</s> we invoke for aid.' — (paśubandha)
Thus [are enumerated] the animal [sacrifices]. — (paśubandha)
[They are] both <s>Soma</s>-related and designated. — (paśubandha)
The designated one is for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>. — (paśubandha)
[It is performed] every six months or every year. — (paśubandha)

For <s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>upāṃśu</s> (whispered), for <s>Savitṛ</s>, for <s>Sūrya</s>, for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and for <s>Viśvakarman</s> — of these, we shall describe the modifications of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (whispered offering) there. — (paśubandha)
The directive beginning [is substituted] with the <s>āgur</s> (call of assent) in the improper place. — (paśubandha)
'He should take, he should eat, he should do' — these are [recited] in their respective places, in a whisper. — (paśubandha)
In the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> [sacrifice]: — (sautrāmaṇī)

The animal victims are for the <s>Aśvins</s>, for <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and for <s>Indra</s>. Or the fourth is for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. The <s>paśupuroḍāśas</s> (animal-accompanying cakes) are for <s>Indra</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>. — (sautrāmaṇī)

Having purified — 'You two, the <s>Aśvins</s>, [drink] the <s>surā</s> (liquor)' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the cups. 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker) offer to the <s>Aśvins</s>, to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, to <s>Indra</s> the good protector — may they enjoy, may they go forth, may they drink, may they be intoxicated by the <s>somas</s> of the liquor-offering! O <s>hotṛ</s>, offer!' — this is the directive. 'As both parents [cherish] a son, the two <s>Aśvins</s>' — this is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse). — (sautrāmaṇī)

'O <s>Agni</s>, announce!' — this is the assenting call (<s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>). Or: 'O <s>Agni</s>, announce [to enjoy] the pressed liquor!' 'For different indeed is the seat made for you by the gods.' 'Lest you two destroy in the highest firmament during the month.' 'You are <s>surā</s> (liquor), O powerful one!' — looking at the liquor with arms held down. 'This is <s>Soma</s>' — [looking at] the <s>Soma</s>. — (sautrāmaṇī)

'Whatever of the pressed, juicy [soma] was scattered here, whatever <s>Indra</s> drank with his powers — that very thing, with a tranquil mind, I now partake of <s>Soma</s>, the king' — this is the murmured verse at the partaking. — (sautrāmaṇī)
Here [is performed] the <s>prāṇabhakṣa</s> (life-breath partaking). — (sautrāmaṇī)
When there is a ritual error, [there is] an expiatory rite. — (prāyaścitti)
In the absence of the prescribed [substance], a substitute [is used]. — (prāyaścitti)
When one who has established fires must travel, they should carry the fires separately. — (prāyaścitti)
Or, having offered an <s>ājya</s> (ghee) oblation [with the verse] 'For you, O best of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>,' he should merge [the fires]. — (prāyaścitti)
'This is your womb, O seasonal one' — one should rub [the fire] into the <s>araṇī</s> (fire-drill) at the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire). — (prāyaścitti)

Or with the hands: 'O <s>Agni</s>, that sacrificial body of yours — by that ascend; ascend, self to self, creating abundant noble riches. Having become sacrifice, come and sit in the womb, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, be present, being born.' — (prāyaścitti)
Thus for one who has not established fires, without making an offering. — (prāyaścitti)

If he should churn [fire] from the <s>araṇī</s> (fire-drills) after touching [them] with the hands: 'Descend again, O <s>Jātavedas</s>; carry the oblation again to the gods for us. Knowing [us], place in us offspring, nourishment, and wealth; then be auspicious for the sacrificer.' — (prāyaścitti)

If the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) is about to go out, he should join it from the near side by means of the <s>śamyā</s> (yoke-pin) brought from beyond [saying]: 'This one [is] your one, the other one too is [your] one' — he should fan [it]. — (prāyaścitti)

If one should transgress — if one should pass over the new-moon day or full-moon day, or if one should sacrifice on another's fires, or if another should sacrifice on one's fires, or if another fire should penetrate one's fires, or if at the time of the <s>agnihotra</s> offering, when the oblation has been poured, a dog, person, or wheel should pass between [the fires] in the fire-hall, or if [the sacrificer] should die on the road — an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) [is prescribed]. — (prāyaścitti)
<s>Agni</s> is the path-maker [for that iṣṭi]. — (prāyaścitti)
'For you know, O ordainer, the paths to the gods.' 'We have gone off the path.' An ox is the sacrificial fee. — (prāyaścitti)

But if there is an intrusion [by a dog or person], before the [expiatory] offering, he should cause [the fire] to cross over between [the fires] by means of a cow [placed] without fire. — (prāyaścitti)
He should stamp out the footprint of the dog with ashes [reciting]: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode across this.' — (prāyaścitti)

Between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>, he should connect [them] with ashes mixed with ghee and water mixed with ghee [reciting]: 'Stretching the thread, follow the light of the atmosphere.' — (prāyaścitti)

Having caused [the fire] to follow along, and having carried forward the <s>āhavanīya</s> again, he should attend upon it: 'O <s>Agni</s>, the first [fire] established in the established place — it spread along the rays of the sun. May the richest [blessing] follow along there; unite us with benevolence and with prize-winning [power].' And: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are widely extending.' — (prāyaścitti)

For one who has died on the road, having carried [him], they should silently offer the <s>agnihotra</s> as a complete offering (<s>sarvahuta</s>) with the milk of a cow that has a calf, until the [next] assembly. — (prāyaścitti)
If one who has established the fires should die in the dark fortnight, they should carry him with oblations through the bright fortnight. — (prāyaścitti)
When there is a defect in the oblations — if the deities have been omitted — completing the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) with ghee, the sacrifice should be repeated. — (prāyaścitti)
The oblations are spoiled by hair, nails, insects, moths, or other disgusting things. — (prāyaścitti)
And [those that are] broken or spilled. — (prāyaścitti)
They should remove them with water. — (prāyaścitti)

'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you [encompasses] these' — and [at] the ant-hill, or with fat [he should offer]. The <s>sāmnāyya</s> (mixed offering) one should offer with a middle <s>palāśa</s> (butea) leaf. — (prāyaścitti)
If [the milk] overflows: 'Great heaven and earth, not [so]' — they should pour [it] out at the inner edge of the enclosing [sticks]. — (prāyaścitti)
If one [half] is without defect, having poured [the other] out, they should proceed. — (prāyaścitti)
Or a <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) in place of that. — (prāyaścitti)
If both are defective, [one should offer] a five-dish <s>odana</s> (rice porridge) for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>. — (prāyaścitti)
The preparation for each of those two is separate. — (prāyaścitti)
Some [say it should be] for <s>Indra</s> alone. — (prāyaścitti)
When calves [drink the milk, one should offer] <s>dhāna</s> (parched grain) [or] <s>yavāgū</s> (barley gruel) for <s>Vāyu</s>. — (prāyaścitti)

If the <s>agnihotra</s> [milk], having been placed on the fire, flows out, one should recite over it: 'I have made the flowing embryo firm. May <s>Agni</s> the <s>hotṛ</s>, may earth, atmosphere, and wherever it has flowed from, let it not reach <s>Nirṛti</s> (destruction) beyond [but fall] into <s>Agni</s> alone.' — (prāyaścitti)

If the <s>agnihotra</s> cow, when released, sits down while being milked, one should recite over it: 'That from which you sit down in fear, from that make us free from fear. Protect all our cattle. Homage to <s>Rudra</s> the bountiful.' — (prāyaścitti)

Then one should raise her up: 'The divine <s>Aditi</s> has risen; she has placed life-span in the lord of sacrifice — for <s>Indra</s> making a share, for <s>Mitra</s>, and for <s>Varuṇa</s>.' — (prāyaścitti)

Then, holding a water-vessel at her udder and mouth, having milked her, one should feed [the milk to] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose food would not be consumed — for as long as one lives, or for a year. — (prāyaścitti)
If [the cow] is lowing, one should give her grass [reciting]: 'From the good pasture, may you be blessed.' — (prāyaścitti)
If blood is milked, having destroyed [it] in the <s>gārhapatya</s>, he should offer with another [cow's milk]. — (prāyaścitti)
If [milk is] broken or spilled, one should recite over it: 'I send you to the ocean; go to your own womb. May our heroes be unharmed; may the cows be with me, the lord of cattle.' — (prāyaścitti)

If the <s>agnihotra</s> cow, when released, kicks while being milked — whatever she should spill there, having touched that, one should recite: 'Whatever milk today has crept upon the earth, whatever has crept over the plants, whatever over the waters — may the milk be in the cows, may the milk be in the unslaughtered [cow], may the milk be in the calves, may that milk be in me.' — (prāyaścitti)
Whatever is left over there, with that one should offer. — (prāyaścitti)
Or having brought [milk] from another [cow]. — (prāyaścitti)
This [procedure applies] from the milking onward, up to the carrying forward. — (prāyaścitti)
'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, you are the all-sustaining one; what is offered is your body' — this is the touching [mantra] for what is spilled there. — (prāyaścitti)
With the remainder one should offer. — (prāyaścitti)
Having drawn out again when there is no remainder. — (prāyaścitti)
Ghee [is to be used] when there is no remainder. — (prāyaścitti)
This [applies] up to the offering. — (prāyaścitti)
Having recited a <s>Vāruṇī</s> (verse to <s>Varuṇa</s>), one should offer with a <s>Vāruṇī</s> [verse]. — (prāyaścitti)
Fasting until the next offering time. — (prāyaścitti)
And a re-offering [is required] — [according to] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>. — (prāyaścitti)
The <s>agnihotra</s> — [if it is] scattered or dried up: 'such-and-such' — one should name the enemy. — (prāyaścittāni)
'That which flows out — great heaven and earth, not [so]' — one should carry the ashes of the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) to the inner edge. — (prāyaścittāni)
As with the <s>sāmnāyya</s> (mixed offering), [so too] when there is disgust. — (prāyaścittāni)
When rained upon: '<s>Mitra</s> guides the people, speaking' — [one should perform] the placing of fuel. — (prāyaścittāni)
'Where you know, O lord of the forest' — when the latter oblation is spilled. — (prāyaścittāni)
The time for the [evening] offering ends at nightfall. — (prāyaścittāni)
The morning [offering ends] at the end of the <s>saṃgava</s> (mid-morning) period. — (prāyaścittāni)
Having let that [time] pass, one should offer ghee taken in four portions. — (prāyaścittāni)

If in the evening: 'Homage to the evening star, <s>svāhā</s>.' If in the morning: 'Homage to the morning star, <s>svāhā</s>.' Having approached the <s>agnihotra</s>, having recited '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>' and having given a gift, one should offer. — (prāyaścittāni)
And a <s>Vāruṇī</s> (offering to <s>Varuṇa</s>) <s>iṣṭi</s> (oblation). — (prāyaścittāni)
After offering, the gift-giving [is done] in the morning. — (prāyaścittāni)

And having caused the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) to follow, one should carry it forth again [saying]: 'Be here for our dwellings; do not leave — such-and-such one, son of such-and-such.' — (prāyaścittāni)
Then the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) [is performed]; <s>Mitra</s> [and] <s>Sūrya</s> [are the deities]. — (prāyaścittāni)

'He who by greatness [extends] to heaven' — 'May this mortal be liberal toward <s>Mitra</s>' — when [the iṣṭi] is concluded, [the sacrificer], together with his wife, observing a vow of silence, should sit attending the blazing fires for one day without eating. — (prāyaścittāni)
With milk from two [cows] milked into one vessel, one should offer the <s>agnihotra</s>. — (prāyaścittāni)
When one [pot of milk] has been placed on the fire, one should strain the second. — (prāyaścittāni)
The morning <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) [follows]. — (prāyaścittāni)
<s>Agni</s> is the vow-bearer [of that iṣṭi]. — (prāyaścittāni)

'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the vow-bearer, bright one; O <s>Agni</s>, bring the gods hither, to the sacrifice and our oblation. Bearing vows, the vow-keeper, inviolable, unaging, sacrificing to the gods, with noble heroes, bestowing treasures, gracious, O <s>Agni</s>, protecting for life, O <s>Jātavedas</s>.' — (prāyaścittāni)
This same [procedure applies] for the distressed one when tears flow. — (prāyaścittāni)

If the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), not having been carried forward, should go out, a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should carry the fire forward with <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), with gold being carried in front. — (prāyaścittāni)
When [the sun] has risen, they should carry gold in front as with gold, [along with] ghee taken in four portions and silver. — (prāyaścittāni)
Then one should offer this ghee, sitting down facing west in front [of the fire, reciting]: 'May <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) be pleased with the signal, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (prāyaścittāni)
The rest [follows the rule] for passage of time. — (prāyaścittāni)
But here the fire is not to be made to follow. — (prāyaścittāni)

If, while the <s>āhavanīya</s> is being maintained, the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire) should go out, they should churn [new fire] from their own fire-drills for it, but the other [fire] should be made to follow. — (prāyaścittāni)

In the absence of fire-drills, having touched the <s>araṇī</s> (fire-sticks) with ashes, one should churn [fire, reciting]: 'From here was born first, from these wombs, <s>Jātavedas</s>; with <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, carry the oblation to the gods for us, O knower.' — (prāyaścittāni)

Having churned [fire] and carried it forward to the <s>āhavanīya</s>, one should attend upon [it, reciting]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, sovereign, for sustenance, for wealth, be pleased, for strength, for splendour, for vigour, for offspring. You are sovereign, you are self-ruling; may the two <s>Sārasvatī</s> springs protect you. I establish you as a food-eater, for food and offspring.' — (prāyaścittāni)
From this same [fire] some carry forward the southern [fire], having offered [into it]. — (prāyaścittāni)
Or, having placed the ashes together at the site of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, one should then take up the <s>āhavanīya</s> eastward. — (prāyaścittāni)

Then the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) [is performed]; <s>Agni</s> as <s>Tapasvān</s> (the austere one), <s>Janadvān</s> (the people-possessing one), and <s>Pāvakavān</s> (the purifying one) [are the deities]. — (prāyaścittāni)

'Come with austerity among people, O <s>Agni</s>, purifier, with flame; to this praise of mine. Come to us with austerity among people, O <s>Agni</s>, purifier, blazing; placing our oblations among the gods.' When [the fire] has been carried forward and made to follow, before the offering, the <s>iṣṭi</s> [is performed]. — (prāyaścittāni)
<s>Agni</s> as <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> (the luminous one) [and] <s>Varuṇa</s> [are the deities]. — (prāyaścittāni)

'Rise up, O <s>Agni</s>, your bright [flames]'; '<s>Agni</s>, the great one, has risen above the dawns' — if the sun should rise over all [fires] that have been made to follow, or should set [while they are being carried], [one should perform] the fire-establishment (<s>agnyādheya</s>) anew (<s>punarādheya</s>). — (prāyaścittāni)
And when [the fires] have been heaped together, if the <s>araṇī</s> (fire-drills) are lost. — (prāyaścittāni)
Now [follow] the <s>iṣṭi</s>s (offerings) to <s>Agni</s>. — (prāyaścittāni)
When there is a transgression of the vow, [the offering is] to the lord of vows (<s>Vratapataye</s>). — (prāyaścittāni)
When carrying the fire forward together with [another] fire, [the offering is] to <s>Agnivat</s> (the fire-possessing one). — (prāyaścittāni)
[The offering is] to <s>Kṣāma</s> (the exhausted one) when there is a house fire; to <s>Śuci</s> (the bright one) when there is commingling with another fire. — (prāyaścittāni)
If [the fires] should be separated from each other. — (prāyaścittāni)
[The offering is] to <s>Vīti</s> (the partaker) [when there is separation] of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>. — (prāyaścittāni)
[The offering is] to <s>Saṃvarga</s> (the all-consuming one) when [there is commingling] with a village fire. — (prāyaścittāni)
[The offering is] to <s>Apsumat</s> (the water-possessing one) when [there is] lightning [strike]; to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when eating food of the confused. — (prāyaścittāni)
This same [procedure applies] when the <s>kapāla</s> (potsherds) are lost or not removed. — (prāyaścittāni)
Or when [the milk] has been caused to boil over. — (prāyaścittāni)
[The offering is] to <s>Surabhi</s> (the fragrant one) when the report of death [comes] while [the person] is alive. — (prāyaścittāni)

'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the vow-keeper'; 'Whatever vows of yours we have transgressed'; 'By <s>Agni</s>, <s>Agni</s> is kindled'; 'You indeed, O <s>Agni</s>'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, drive away from us the ailment'; '<s>Agni</s> roared like the thundering sky'; 'Far and wide your wind-driven [flames], O <s>Agni</s>'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, the human clans invoke'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, come for the enjoyment.' — (prāyaścittāni)

'He who [worships] <s>Agni</s> for divine enjoyment'; 'Will he perhaps for our cattle-seeking'; 'Do not [harm] us in this great contest'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, you are well-established in the waters'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, born of heaven'; '<s>Agni</s>, the <s>hotṛ</s>, sat down, the most sacrificing'; 'You have made the divine enjoyment successful for us today.' If his wife or cow should give birth to twins, an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) [is performed] to the <s>Maruts</s>. — (prāyaścittāni)

For the <s>sāmnāyya</s> (mixed offering), when the moon rises before [the proper time]: <s>Agni</s> the giver, <s>Indra</s> the bestower, <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s> [are the deities]. — (prāyaścittāni)
