'O <s>Agni</s>, give wealth to the giver'; 'They resting, inspired ones of these'; 'Long be your goad'; 'Blessed are your hands, well-made, with palms'; '<s>Vaṣaṭ</s> to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I perform'; 'That famous name of yours, O <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, today.' Or alternatively, in place of the expiatory <s>iṣṭi</s>s, one may offer a full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>) to each respective deity — thus it is known. — (prāyaścittāni)

For oblations that are spilled, one should touch [them, reciting]: 'The sacrifice has gone to the divine assembly; may its blessing protect and increase me. May prosperity release [us] with ghee; may the sacrifice release the lord of sacrifice from distress. To the lord of beings, <s>svāhā</s>; to the lord of the world, <s>svāhā</s>; to the lord of creatures, <s>svāhā</s>. By the measured, unmeasured, counter-measured, and re-measured portions of the sacrifice, [if] a drop has fallen.' — (prāyaścittāni)
If the oblation [falls] outside the enclosing sticks, the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-tender) should offer it. — (prāyaścittāni)
One should give a full vessel to the <s>hutavat</s> (offerer). — (prāyaścittāni)

If the deity, invitatory verse, or offering verse has been exchanged, or if the ghee libation or the oblation has been interchanged: 'Whatever [offenses] of yours, O gods, we have overstepped — by speech, by negligence, or by offending the gods — may the <s>Maruts</s> deposit that elsewhere from us, who are free from the ill-wisher, <s>svāhā</s>' — having offered a ghee oblation, one should give the principal sacrificial fee. — (prāyaścittāni)
If one has not invoked the presiding deity, one should rise and invoke [it]. — (prāyaścittāni)
Some [say] mentally. One should sacrifice with ghee to a non-presiding [deity]. — (prāyaścittāni)
When the oblation is badly cooked, one should feed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s with a four-dish <s>odana</s> (rice porridge). — (prāyaścittāni)
When [the fire] is exhausted, having sacrificed with the remainder, one should sacrifice again. — (prāyaścittāni)
When there is no remainder, a repetition [of the entire rite is required]. — (prāyaścittāni)
And for a fault [occurring] before the invocation [of the deity]. — (prāyaścittāni)
Even for the extremely subsidiary [elements]. — (prāyaścittāni)
For the principal elements, [the rule] stated before the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to the fire-god) [applies]. — (prāyaścittāni)
When there is a fault in the cutting [of portions], a re-cutting from the original source [is required]. — (prāyaścittāni)
But here one should give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) to the enemy. — (prāyaścittāni)
As <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee), one should give a field. — (prāyaścittāni)

If the <s>kapāla</s> (potsherd) is broken before the ritual has commenced: 'With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of a hundred syllables I mend you' — having mended [it], they should pour water [reciting]: 'The unbroken <s>gharma</s> (heated milk), the quick-flowing one, having been distressed, has come again. The fuel, the altar, the enclosing sticks, and all — may they restore the life of the sacrifice. The thirty-three threads which the weavers weave — this sacrifice with proper offerings by which they worship — we patch the gap, O worthy ones. <s>Svāhā</s>, may the sacrifice reach the gods.' — (prāyaścittāni)
Likewise for [vessels that are] licked or when [things] are thrown. — (prāyaścittāni)
But other earthen [vessels] should be discarded [reciting]: 'Earth has gone to earth; mother has gone to mother. May we prosper with sons and cattle; may he who hates us be broken.' — (prāyaścittāni)

If the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) should crack or jump up, having placed it on the sacred grass, one should recite over it: 'Why do you jump up? Why do you rise? Come here for pacification. Having become non-terrifying and fit for sacrifice, sit down in your own seat, sit down in your own seat.' 'Do not harm [us], O one sent by the gods; be lustrous with ghee and splendour; do not injure us in any way. For the peace of the sacrificial welfare, sit on this sacred grass.' — (prāyaścittāni)
For the <s>agnihotra</s>, when the fire does not ignite at the proper time, even having brought another [fire], they should offer. — (prāyaścittāni)
In the absence of the first [option], each successive one [is to be used]. — (prāyaścittāni)
In [a fire of] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or also [on] a goat's ear, <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), a clump [of grass], in water, or on wood, or on earth. — (prāyaścittāni)
But even after offering, churning [new fire is required]. — (prāyaścittāni)
If [one offers] in the hand, [there is] no obstruction [to offering] in a vessel. — (prāyaścittāni)
If [one offers on] an ear [of a goat], [one must observe] abstention from meat. — (prāyaścittāni)
If [one offers on] a clump [of grass], one should not lie down [on grass]. — (prāyaścittāni)
If [one offers] in water, [there is] no distinction [required]. — (prāyaścittāni)
This vow [lasts] for a year, or for life. — (prāyaścittāni)
When the fire has gone out between the two oblations, one should offer ghee taken in four portions, with gold placed on top; one should offer [with] gold placed on top. — (prāyaścittāni)

Having sacrificed with <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon offerings), [then] with <s>iṣṭi</s> (offerings), <s>paśu</s> (animal sacrifice), and <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal offerings); then with <s>soma</s>. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)
After the <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon offerings), in whatever order is suitable. Some [say] even before, with <s>soma</s>. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)
Its priests [are as follows]. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)
Four [groups of] three persons [each]. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)
For each [of the four chief priests], the subsequent three [are assistants]. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)

The <s>hotṛ</s>, <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s>, <s>acchāvāka</s>, <s>grāvastut</s>; the <s>adhvaryu</s>, <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s>, <s>neṣṭṛ</s>, <s>unnetṛ</s>; the <s>brahmā</s>, <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>āgnīdhra</s>, <s>potṛ</s>; the <s>udgātṛ</s>, <s>prastotṛ</s>, <s>pratihartṛ</s>, <s>subrahmaṇya</s>. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)
These [priests] officiate at <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) and <s>ekāha</s> (single-day) [soma] sacrifices. — (soma: general: soma pravacana)

These same [priests], being <s>āhitāgni</s>s (those who have established the sacred fires), having performed the first sacrifice, having been consecrated as a group of seventeen with the householder, and having assembled the fires, sit facing them for <s>sattra</s> (communal soma sessions). — (soma: general: soma pravacana)
The designation of the <s>samāvāpa</s> (collection) and other [elements] in accordance with their purpose [follows] the procedure of the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) system.
From the consecration onward, [the rules apply] for those who have not established the [sacred] fires.
'<s>Agni</s> is the mouth [of the gods]' — and [this applies] in the invitatory and offering verses.
At the giving of the staff.
In the <s>praiṣa</s> (directive formulas) and <s>nivit</s> (laudatory insertions).
In the ghee offering verse.
And in the <s>kuhū</s> (new-moon day verse).
And in the <s>acchāvāka</s>'s recitation, the invocations, and the counter-invocations.
The <s>ārṣeya</s> (lineage) of the householder should be announced — for the principal [participants], beginning with himself.
Likewise for the second, third, and fourth [participants].
For as many as have the same <s>gotra</s> (clan lineage) without interruption, [the announcement is made] once.
Or the <s>saṃskāras</s> (ritual procedures) should be repeated according to the lineage of the [ritual] materials.
In sacrifices involving fire-altar construction, some [prescribe] the <s>ukhā-sambharaṇīyā iṣṭi</s> (offering for collecting the fire-pan).
<s>Agni</s> possessed of <s>brahman</s> (sacred power), <s>Agni</s> possessed of <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power), <s>Agni</s> the upholder of <s>kṣatra</s> [are the deities].

'By this sacred word (<s>brahman</s>), O <s>Agni</s>, may you grow'; 'Both <s>brahman</s> and homage to you, O <s>Jātavedas</s>'; 'Many [blessings], O <s>Agni</s>, for abundant nourishment'; 'That brilliant one, making the brilliant shine upon us'; '<s>Agni</s> rules over the great ruling power'; 'I praise your benevolence, calling aloud hither.' From this point onward, each successive ritual act [should be performed] progressively more softly.
But this [rule applies] also from the full-moon [offering onward].
The conveyance of <s>Soma</s> [extends] up to the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening) [offering].
After the first carrying forward of the fire, at the <s>upavasatha</s> (preparatory day), there is no restriction.
[This applies] from the intoxicating [drink] onward, in the <s>gharma</s> (heated milk offering).
In the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration offering), the <s>dhāyyā</s> (introductory verses) are in the <s>Virāj</s> [meter].
<s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> [are the deities].

'<s>Agni</s> was the mouth, the foremost of the gods; <s>Viṣṇu</s> was the highest among those assembled. Encompassing the gods for the sacrificer, come to us with the oblation of consecration. O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, your highest austerity — for the guardian of consecration, for you are mighty; being in accord with all the divine sacrificial [gods], bestow consecration upon this sacrificer.'
<s>Vaiśvānara</s>-<s>Āditya</s>, or <s>Sarasvatī</s>-<s>Aditi</s> [are alternative deities].
'The <s>Ādityas</s>, upholding, stationed in the world' — two [verses]. 'For those possessing worlds, the lords of the world' — or [these verses].
There is no [ritual] sprinkling beginning with 'this' [from the consecration] until the <s>udayanīyā</s> (concluding offering).
Beginning with 'this,' in the <s>iḷā</s> and the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn invocation), there is an <s>āgūr</s> (assent) in place of the blessing.
'This sacrificer has been invited; may I obtain the <s>āgur</s> (assent) and the surplus of this sacrifice' — thus [is the formula] when he is invited.
'This sacrificer wishes; may I obtain the <s>āgur</s> and the surplus of this sacrifice' — thus [is the formula] when he wishes.
And here there is no naming [of the sacrificer by name].
In the natural [order], after the last [one], upward from the <s>paśu-iḷā</s> (animal-offering iḷā).
The movement of the consecrated ones [is restricted to] between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> [fires], from the carrying forward of the fire.
The consecrations are unlimited in number, counted by nights beginning from the consecration day.
From one day up to a year; but for the <s>savrata</s> (observance sacrifice), exactly a year.
In the twelve-day [sacrifice] and in those involving [fire-altar] construction, the <s>upasad</s> (preparatory offerings) [are performed] as on the pressing day.
But the ritual procedure follows that of one-day [sacrifices].
One or three consecrations, three <s>upasad</s>s (preparatory offerings), and the last day is the pressing day.
At the end of the consecration [comes] the purchase of <s>Soma</s> (<s>rājakraya</s>).
On that day [is performed] the <s>prāyaṇīya iṣṭi</s> (opening offering).

<s>Pathyā Svasti</s> (the goddess of auspicious paths), <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Aditi</s> [are the deities]. 'Well-being to us on paths and in wilderness-ways' — two [verses]. 'O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to wealth.' 'We have reached the path of the gods.' 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, enlightened by wisdom.'

'Those abodes of yours in heaven and on earth.' 'Come, the all-god, the true lord.' 'He who [created] all these beings.' 'The well-protecting earth and the harm-free heaven.' 'The great mother of the pious ones.' 'That <s>Agni</s> alone [surpasses] other fires' — two [verses are] the concluding offerings. This [offering] has a <s>śamyantā</s> (pacifying conclusion).
[It is] without <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions).
When [the prāyaṇīya iṣṭi] is completed —
They purchase the king [<s>Soma</s>].

When [the cart] is about to be driven forward, standing behind the cart at a distance of three footsteps, between the two wheel-tracks, when directed [with] '<s>Agni</s>' and the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (exclamation): 'You are the inspired sage, you are the seer, you who sustain all things.'

'Drive away the fear from hostile men' — causing [the cart] to move forward, striking the right-side [wheel] thrice with the tip of the foot, he should recite: 'Go forth from the good toward the better; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [goes] before this [path] of yours. Then, in this most excellent [place] on the earth, make enemies far away, O possessor of all heroes' — [recited] while standing.
Following along, between the two wheel-tracks only.

'O <s>Soma</s>, those life-giving [powers] of yours' — three [verses]. 'All rejoice at one come with fame.' 'The god has come; may he increase [our] dwelling with the seasons' — one should begin with the half-verse. When the cart has stopped, approaching from the right side, one stands facing the king [<s>Soma</s>].
When the king [<s>Soma</s>] is being brought forth, one should follow in front of the cart.

'Those abodes of yours, which they worship with oblations'; 'O god, [grant] this thought of one striving to learn' — when [<s>Soma</s>] is deposited, one should place [the covering] around, touching the king [<s>Soma</s>].
On the garment or on the <s>Soma</s> stalks.
Now [follow the rites] ending with the <s>ātithya</s> (hospitality offering) <s>iḷā</s>.
For that [offering], fire-churning [is required].

The <s>dhāyyā</s> (introductory verses): those containing [the word] 'guest.' 'With fuel, serve <s>Agni</s>.' 'Be nourished; may [all] come together for you.' <s>Viṣṇu</s> [is the deity]. 'This <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth.' 'That beloved abode of his, may I attain.' '<s>Hotṛ</s> of the brilliant chariot, of the sacrifice.' 'Listen, this <s>Agni</s> of the <s>Bharatas</s> resounds forth' — [these are] the concluding offerings.

When [the ātithya iṣṭi] is completed, those about to perform the <s>tānūnaptra</s> (self-binding oath) touch the ghee [reciting]: 'You are unassailable, the unassailable vigor of the gods, the protector from malediction. Free from malediction, may I straightforwardly attain the truth; place me in your own light.'
Having touched water, they consecrate the king [<s>Soma</s>] by nourishing [him].
Beginning with 'this,' [the verses] containing 'rejoicing' and 'water-meaning' [are used] in the <s>upasad</s>s (preparatory offerings).

'Stalk by stalk, O divine <s>Soma</s>, may you be nourished for <s>Indra</s>; O finder of singular wealth. May <s>Indra</s> be nourished for you; may you be nourished for <s>Indra</s>. Nourish us, friends, with sacrificial wisdom. Well-being to you, O divine <s>Soma</s>; at the pressing may I obtain the surplus.'

Having touched water, they make the <s>nihnava</s> (secret declaration), placing their hands on the sacred grass — right [hands] palms upward, left [hands] palms downward: 'Seeking well-being, seeking wealth, I send forth blessings for fortune. Truth to the truthful ones, beginning [with them]. Homage to heaven, homage to earth.'

Having touched water, when they are about to perform the <s>Pravargya</s> (heated-milk offering), going around the <s>khara</s> (support) on the north side, sitting down behind it, when directed, one should praise the <s>ṛgāvāna</s> (Ṛg-Veda recitation).
Having recited each verse without a break, having chanted the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), one should conclude.

'<s>Brahman</s> (the sacred word) was born first, from the front, from the summit, from the beautiful light, <s>Vena</s> [came].' 'From the depths, may its manifestations [come] upon me; the womb of the existent and the non-existent [is] its opening.' 'This [hymn is] for the father, for royal power' — 'For the first-born, the foremost in creation.' 'That brilliant, calling <s>gharma</s> they heat for the first offerer.' 'The great one established the great [heaven]; the mightily-born [established] the sky, the father's seat, and the earthly realm.' 'From the depth, upward from birth, the one arched upward — <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the deity of that, the sovereign.' 'I praise that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, at both [praisings], of true impulse, the wise creator, the treasure-holder, the beloved, the thoughtful sage.' 'Whose thought, directed upward, has shone upon [us]; golden-handed, of good wisdom, he measured out [the spaces]; kindly toward the sun, [or] kindly toward the sun.'

'Sit down; you are great' — when [the vessel] is being set down. 'They anoint [him], spreading [him] forth, like inspired sages' — when it is being anointed. 'The winged one anointed by the magic of <s>Asura</s>'; 'He who would assault us from near, O <s>Agni</s>'; 'Be of good mind to us, O <s>Agni</s>, when approached' — [these are] pairs of verses.

'Make strength, as if an extensive expanse' — five [verses]. 'Around you, O lover of songs, the hymns.' 'Upon both you have placed the utterance, the bright word.' 'One of yours is brilliant, the other is worthy of worship.' 'I saw the herdsman, never resting.' 'At the lips [flowed] drops.' 'This <s>Vena</s> has impelled the cloud-wombed ones.' 'Your sieve is spread out, O lord of sacred speech' — two [verses]. 'The far-spread sieve the divine powers stretched.' '[Those] bearing the blazing <s>gharma</s> in the chants.'
'Within the ocean, for the far-seeing one.' 'Thrice in the day they conceived the name of the sun.'

'You, the first of the troops' — and [with the verse] 'that of which I beheld you,' with the first [verse] one should look at the sacrificer, with the second at [his] wife, with the third at oneself. 'Who shall succeed? O <s>Hotṛ</s>, O <s>Aśvins</s>, for you' — nine [verses].

'<s>Agni</s> shines forth.' 'Like pressing-stones, I invite.' 'Heaven and Earth' — before the last [verse]. 'The tawny one of the dawn has shone forth first' — at the pouring-in, with the latter half-verse one should look at the wife. [With] the last [verse], when [the vessels are] placed around, having made them rise, 'the <s>Adhvaryu</s>s cause [them] to recite' — thus [ends] the first section.
Now the latter [section].
When [all] are seated, the <s>adhvaryu</s> calls the <s>gharma-dughā</s> (cow to be milked for the gharma); that is the directive of the latter [section].
Without [making] the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (exclamation).

Having invited [with]: 'This cow of good milk' — two [verses]. 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, [impel] you.' 'As a calf with [its] mothers.' 'As a calf with mothers.' 'That breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which is life-giving.' 'The cow has lowed after the yearning calf.' 'Approach with homage.' 'Those who recognize [each other], let them sit down; those who know [each other].' 'With ten [fingers], the [daughters] of <s>Vivasvat</s> milk the one [cow] — seven [do so].' '<s>Agni</s> is kindled, O <s>Aśvins</s>; your heated <s>gharma</s> has come.'

'The cows are milked, O mighty one; here the milch-cows [give milk]; O wondrous ones, the singers rejoice. <s>Agni</s> is kindled, O mighty ones; the gift of heaven — the heated <s>gharma</s> is milked for you, [yielding] honey for nourishment. For we, most abundantly, O <s>Aśvins</s>, invoke you at the drinking-feasts, as singers.'

That indeed is his most visible ritual act: 'The self-possessing sky yields ghee and milk.' Having recited 'Rise, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>,' one stands still. 'She who has been milked yielded the overflowing nourishment' — as [the milk] is being brought, [one recites] with the running: 'O milker of cows, pour the milk of the cow into the <s>gharma</s> (heated vessel) with the milk.' — (soma: pravargya)

'<s>Savitṛ</s>, the most excellent, has opened up the sky; well-guided are heaven and earth' — while [the milk] is being poured. 'Now, of the <s>Aśvins</s>, the seer' — for the cow's [milk]. 'Pour in the splendour when pressed' — for the goat's [milk]. When both have been poured in together: 'Great waters.' — (soma: pravargya)

Taking up the <s>mahāvīra</s> (great hero vessel), when they rise: 'Up rises that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, golden' — one should rise after [them]. 'Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth' — one should follow. '<s>Gandharva</s> protects his footstep' — having looked at the mound and having crossed over it. 'The beautiful eagle flying up to heaven' — having completed [the recitation], one should sit down with the <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable Om) without pushing aside the grass; being directed, one sacrifices. — (soma: pravargya)

'Your heated <s>gharma</s> (offering) approaches, [called by] its own <s>hotṛ</s> (good invoker); your <s>adhvaryu</s> (priest) proceeds, being liberal. Of the sweet milked [offering], O <s>Aśvins</s>, [given] for offspring, drink of the fluid of the cow.' — (soma: pravargya)

'Drink both, O <s>Aśvins</s>' — with both [verses], without interruption. 'O <s>Agni</s>, carry forth' — this is the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (responsive exclamation) of the <s>gharma</s>; or 'O <s>Agni</s>, carry forth the <s>gharma</s>.' The <s>brahmā</s> (priest) recites silently at the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and at the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>: 'In all directions from the south, all gods — gods, come here! Of the <s>gharma</s> that has been offered with <s>svāhā</s>, drink the sweet [essence], O <s>Aśvins</s>.' Thus also for the afternoon [offering]. — (soma: pravargya)

'The ghee and milk offered in the cows — this, O <s>Aśvins</s>, is your portion that has come. O sweet ones, supporters, lords of the assembly, true lords — drink the heated <s>gharma</s>, the <s>soma</s>-like honey.' — (soma: pravargya)

'Drink of this, O <s>Aśvins</s>' — and being directed, the <s>hotṛ</s> [recites] at the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>: 'Offered with <s>svāhā</s>, the bright <s>gharma</s> among the gods, which is the cup of the <s>Aśvins</s>, the divine drink.' — (soma: pravargya)

'May all the immortals, delighting in that, carry [it] to the presence of the <s>Gandharva</s>. The inspired one raises a wave from the ocean; the drop goes toward the ocean that it seeks to win.' 'Turn, O friend, to the friend.' 'Upward indeed [be] your aids' — these two [verses]. — (soma: pravargya)

'Those reverential ones indeed thus' — the <s>Prāgāthī</s> [hymn] for the forenoon, the <s>Kāṇvī</s> for the afternoon, or either one throughout; but the <s>Kāṇvī</s> certainly for the last [day]. Having recited 'O purifier, bright one, for your dwelling,' one should await the partaking. The approach to partaking is with the <s>vājina</s> (prize-winning formula): 'The oblation has been offered; the honey-oblation, O most <s>Indra</s>-like, in <s>Agni</s> — may we attain your <s>gharma</s>, O god.' — (soma: pravargya)

'Of the honey-laden, nourishing, swift, <s>Aṅgiras</s>-descended — homage to you; be [gracious]; do not harm me' — this is the silent recitation at partaking. The ritual performers should partake of the <s>gharma</s>; but all the consecrated ones [should partake]. When all are consecrated, the householder's [portions are] the third and the last partakings. Being directed: 'Like a hawk to its nest, to the seat made by wisdom, in which the seven ancient <s>Vasus</s> ascend — ascend!' — (soma: pravargya)
'The seer of the longest hearing, the <s>gharma</s> is the guest of <s>Indra</s>. May [the wife] be glorious through the hero's wealth' — one should place [the vessel] around. — (soma: pravargya)
On the last [day], before the last [oblation]: 'The great divine seat of the oblation-possessor' — one should make the offering. — (soma: pravargya)
Now [follows] the <s>upasad</s> (approach offering). — (soma: second upasad day)
In that [upasad], the silent recitations [are those] of the ancestral [rites]. — (soma: second upasad day)
And at the <s>prādeśa</s> (span-measure) and the sitting down. — (soma: second upasad day)
The attending upon [the fire] here is according to the standard [procedure]. — (soma: second upasad day)
'For approaching the bountiful one' — three [verses], each one [recited] thrice, without interruption. These are the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses). — (soma: second upasad day)
With the concluding <s>praṇava</s> (Om) of those [verses], having invoked <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, one should sit down. — (soma: second upasad day)
Some [say] one should not invoke. Even without invocation, these same deities [are understood]. — (soma: second upasad day)

'<s>Agni</s> shall slay the foes' — 'He who, fierce like an arrow-slayer' — 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, are the true lord, prosperity-giving, disease-removing' — '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode across this, he strode with three steps.' The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to Agni as the one who makes the offering successful) and what follows are omitted, as well as the fore-offerings and <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee portions). — (soma: second upasad day)
The <s>āpyāyana</s> (swelling rite) and the <s>nihnava</s> (concealment rite) are constant [features]. — (soma: second upasad day)
This same [procedure applies] for the afternoon. — (soma: second upasad day)

'O <s>Agni</s>, [accept] this fuel of mine; this' — these are the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses). The <s>yājyā</s> (offering verses) and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verses) are reversed. And the <s>nihnava</s> (concealment) [is done] with the palms — thus [are] the <s>upasad</s>s (approach offerings). — (soma: second upasad day)
[With the words] 'good forenoon' and 'good afternoon.' — (soma: second upasad day)
Starting from the day of purchasing the king [<s>Soma</s>], by the count of single-day [rites], [there are] three [upasad days]. — (soma: second upasad day)
Or six. — (soma: second upasad day)
For <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day rites), twelve; for <s>sattra</s> (communal sessions), twenty-four or a year [of upasad days]. — (soma: second upasad day)
Some [do] not [perform] the <s>gharma</s> (pravargya) at the first sacrifice. — (soma: second upasad day)
On the <s>upavasatha</s> (preparatory) day, both [upasads are performed] in the forenoon. — (soma: second upasad day)

When the first <s>upasad</s> (approach offering) has been completed, being directed, the <s>hotṛ</s> recites for the <s>purīṣya</s> (filling) layer along with the consecrated one. — (soma: second upasad day)
[He says] 'sacrificer' when [the person] is not consecrated. — (soma: second upasad day)

Standing back at a span's distance, having uttered the <s>hiṃkāra</s> (the syllable 'hiṃ'), [one recites] 'The fire-altar-building fires' three times in a low voice, with the <s>praṇava</s>. — (soma: second upasad day)
Or also [the hymn] 'delightful.' — (soma: second upasad day)
When [the fires] move, one should follow along. — (soma: second upasad day)
When they stop, with speech released, one should say 'Carry forward.' — (soma: second upasad day)
Then one should recite the praise of the fire that has been built up and sung over. — (soma: second upasad day)
Sitting behind the tail of the fire [altar], having uttered the <s>hiṃkāra</s>: 'I am <s>Agni</s> by birth, <s>Jātavedas</s>' — three times in a middle voice. — (soma: second upasad day)
At this same seat, one offers the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> [oblation]. — (soma: second upasad day)
These three [acts are performed] when there is fire-altar building. — (soma: second upasad day)

The <s>brahmā</s> (priest), having recited the <s>Apratiratham</s> (hymn of invincibility), sits to the south of the fire, outside the <s>vedi</s> (altar), until the sprinkling with the <s>audumbara</s> (Ficus) [ladle]. — (soma: second upasad day)
The carrying forward of the fire has been described. — (soma: second upasad day)
But the consecrated one should approach the <s>vasor dhārā</s> (stream of wealth oblation). — (soma: second upasad day)
They set in motion the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation carts). — (soma: third upasad day: havirdhāna pravartana)
That has been described with the <s>soma</s>-carrying [cart]. — (soma: third upasad day: havirdhāna pravartana)
Between the southern <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation cart) and the northern wheel, at the track, [he stands] at the feet. — (soma: third upasad day: havirdhāna pravartana)

'I yoke for you the ancient prayer with homages; may the auspicious one [be] extended for the sacrifice — you two. When, as in <s>Yama</s>'s [case], striving, you placed this laudable speech upon both' — one should stop [reciting] at the half-verse, if it does not come to a standstill. — (soma: third upasad day: havirdhāna pravartana)

body.text:
viśvā.rūpāṇi.pratimuñca.te.kavir.iti.vyavasthāām./ (soma: third upasad day: havir.dhāna.pravartana)
  (soma: third upasad day: havir.dhāna.pravartana)
body.translated_text: 'The wise one puts on all forms for you' — [one recites] when it comes to a standstill. — (soma: third upasad day: havirdhāna pravartana)
When the two poles have been set down: 'I place around you, O faultless one, the hymn' — one should place [the enclosures] around. — (soma: third upasad day: havirdhāna pravartana)

When they are about to lead <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> forward, having entered by the passage, north of the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's) site and the <s>sadas</s> (assembly shed), having entered the <s>patnīśālā</s> (wife's hall) by the front door, having passed north of the hall entrance and sat down behind it, being directed, one should recite: 'O <s>Savitṛ</s>, divine one, to the first father, [you gave] height and breadth to him. Then for us, O <s>Savitṛ</s>, of complete [gifts], day by day, grant abundant cattle' — [reciting while] seated. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
While following along, the subsequent [verses are recited]. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)

'Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth; the <s>hotṛ</s>, the god, the immortal.' 'In the morning to you, O <s>Agni</s>, day by day, O radiant one, we come near with devotion, [with] homage' — one should stop at the half-verse. When [the fire] has been placed in the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth) and is being invoked: 'O <s>Agni</s>, be pleased with, accept that speech' — having completed [the verse], one should stop with the <s>praṇava</s>. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)

When they pass north of the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s>, having passed by: '<s>Soma</s> goes, the path-finder; of the gods, that king <s>Varuṇa</s>; those <s>Aśvins</s>' — one should stop at the half-verse. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)

As the king enters, one should follow after [him, reciting]: 'Within and facing east — may <s>Aditi</s> be [for you].' 'Like a hawk to the nest, the seat made by wisdom.' 'The <s>Asura</s>, the all-knowing, propped up the sky' — one should place [the enclosures] around, with the subsequent [verse], or when there is a journey for welfare. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
The <s>brahmā</s> (priest), having similarly entered and crossed beyond the altar, should sit down to the south of the hall entrance. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
He should rise after the <s>hotṛ</s> and walk in front of [him] as before, if he is to lead the king [<s>Soma</s>] forward. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
The procedure when one does not lead [<s>Soma</s>] forward has been stated. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)

Having reached the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation carts), having handed over the king [<s>Soma</s>] to the householder, having passed in front of or behind the <s>havirdhāna</s>, one should sit down to the south of the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire). — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
[He sits] at the tail of the fire [altar] when there is fire-altar building. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
This is the seat of the <s>brahmā</s> (priest) at the animal [sacrifice]. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
And in the morning, until the offering of the <s>vapā</s> (omentum). — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
But if one should return from the front when [the king] is entering. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-soma praṇayana)
Then they proceed with the <s>Agnī-Ṣomīya</s> (animal sacrifice to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>). — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-somīya paśu)
At the <s>uttaravedi</s> (northern altar), until the handing over of the staff. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-somīya paśu)

Having handed over the staff, having placed the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s> (priest) in front, having passed north of the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation carts), having entered the <s>sadas</s> (assembly shed) by the front door, having passed north of their respective <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (hearth-mound), the <s>hotṛ</s> sits down behind his own <s>dhiṣṇya</s>. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-somīya paśu)
The others stand. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-somīya paśu)

If they should bring the oblations for the <s>Devasū</s> (gods' pressing): <s>Agni</s> the householder, <s>Soma</s> the lord of the forest, <s>Savitṛ</s> the true impeller, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the lord of speech, <s>Indra</s> the chief, <s>Mitra</s> the true, <s>Varuṇa</s> the lord of dharma, <s>Rudra</s> the cattle-possessing or the lord of cattle. — (soma: third upasad day: agnī-somīya paśu)

'You, O <s>Agni</s>, of great power'; '<s>Agni</s>, the oblation-bearer, the unaging, our father'; 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, [are] our desired one'; '<s>Brahmā</s> (the prayer), the path-finder of the gods, of the sages'; 'To <s>Viśvadeva</s> (All-Gods), the true lord'; 'I shall not perish'; 'the established [gift] of the divine, that.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the first utterance of speech'; 'Like swans, with companions speaking'; 'You have conquered, O much-invoked one, the enemies'; 'You became great, O <s>Indra</s>, through prayer'; 'Free from disease, rejoicing with refreshment.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'May that mortal, O <s>Mitra</s>, be prosperous, the offering one'; 'Asking you for greatness'; 'Bound by you, one who wishes to be released. You protect from every world by your law; you protect from the sun by your law'; 'Whatever [offense] here, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, among the divine people'; 'I have made hymns to you like a herdsman of cattle' — two [verses]. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

If indeed all the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants) [are used]: <s>Agni</s> [with] <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter], <s>trivṛt</s> (nine-fold) <s>stoma</s>, <s>Rathantara</s> <s>sāman</s>, [associated with] spring; <s>Indra</s> [with] <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter], fifteen-fold [stoma], <s>Bṛhat</s> [sāman], [associated with] summer; the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-Gods) [with] <s>Jagatī</s> [meter], seventeen-fold [stoma], <s>Vairūpa</s> [sāman], [associated with] the rainy season. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

<s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> [with] <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meter], twenty-one-fold [stoma], <s>Vairāja</s> [sāman], [associated with] autumn; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [with] <s>Paṅkti</s> [meter], twenty-seven-fold [stoma], <s>Śakvara</s> [sāman], [associated with] the winter season; <s>Savitṛ</s> [with] <s>Aticchanda</s> (hypermetric) [meter], thirty-three-fold [stoma], <s>Raivata</s> [sāman], [associated with] the cool season; <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s consort, <s>Anumati</s>. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'The kindling-fuel lying in the directions, the sun-possessing one; may <s>Madhuretas</s> (honey-seed), <s>Mādhava</s> (spring), protect us. <s>Agni</s>, the divine, hard to cross, unerring — may this <s>kṣatra</s> (sovereign power) protect and guard us. May the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>sāman</s> protect us; <s>Gāyatrī</s>, of all forms, among the meters.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'May the nine-fold <s>stoma</s> with its arrangement, the ocean, and the wind carry this strength to us. Fierce, the overpowering one of the directions, bestower of life-force, pure in the bright days, among the powerful. May lord <s>Indra</s> sustain us from here; sustain this great sovereign power on all sides. The <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>sāman</s>, bearing sovereignty, endowed with increasing virility; the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>'s strength, resplendent, of fierce heroes.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'O <s>Indra</s>, with the fifteen-fold <s>stoma</s>, protect this middle [region]; with wind and ocean, guard [it]. The eastern direction, glorious with glory, with the sun; the <s>Viśvedevas</s> [are associated with] the rainy season, the days possessing the sun.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'May this sovereign power be unconquerable, strong, unassailable, forceful, possessing force. In the <s>Vairūpa</s> <s>sāman</s>, may I have that power; through the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter] may I establish him among the people. The <s>Viśvedevas</s> with the seventeen-fold [stoma] — this sovereign power, strong as ocean and wind.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'The supporting direction has upheld this sovereignty; may its strength be like <s>Mitra</s>'s, [standing] among the foundations. O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [associated with] autumn among the days — the wise ones — grant great peace to this kingdom.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'In the <s>Vairāja</s> <s>sāman</s>, my thought [rests]; through the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meter], combined might and force. May this sovereignty, generous like <s>Mitra</s>; O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, protect [it] in lordship. Supreme ruler of the directions, forceful, possessing force; the winter season with its arrangement — may it sustain us.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'Seeking aid, the winds [blow] broadly through the great <s>Śakvarī</s> [meter]; may they protect this sacrifice for us, rich in ghee. Sun-possessing, yielding good milk, rich in milk — may the divine [deity] of the directions protect us, rich in ghee. You are the protector in front and behind, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s> — yoke speech with both [modes].' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'The upward direction, the share of joy, of the plants; with the year, <s>Savitṛ</s> [protects] our days. The <s>Raivata</s> <s>sāman</s>, the <s>Aticchanda</s> (hypermetric meter), exceeding the meter — may [he who is] unborn-as-enemy be gracious to us.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'The <s>stoma</s> in the thirty-three-fold [arrangement], the mistress of the world; O wind born of the shining one, praise us. Rich in ghee, O <s>Savitṛ</s>, in lordship; rich in milk, may the share of joy be ours. The firm direction, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s consort, non-terrifying, the sovereign of force, the one who perceives.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Mātariśvan</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s> — may the blowing winds praise us. The pillar of heaven, the support of earth — the sovereign of the world, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s consort. Far-seeing, nourishing, of good prosperity — may she be auspicious to us in the lap of <s>Aditi</s>.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'Today may <s>Anumati</s> (Approval) approve our sacrifice among the gods. And may <s>Agni</s>, the oblation-bearer, bring delight to the generous one. Indeed, O <s>Anumati</s>, may you think [well of us] and grant us well-being.' — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'Impel us for resolve and skill; extend our lifespans' — thus. The ninth [hymn is] the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> (hymn to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>), the tenth [is] the <s>Kāya</s> (bodily hymn). — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

'Who today yokes the cows of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) to the pole?' — two [verses]. With the supplementary-offering coals, when there is no circumambulation, they should proceed. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)
If from the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-kindler's hearth), [one should pass] to the north of the <s>hotṛ</s>. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)
If from the <s>śāmitra</s> (animal-slaughtering fire), [one should pass] to the south of the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s>. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)
Having first stood up, having gone out, one should take the <s>veda</s> (grass-bundle). — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)
This heart-piercing [rite is] not [performed] at the beginning [but] before the <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary cow). — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)
When [the rite] has concluded, they distribute the <s>vasatīvarī</s> (overnight waters); the consecrated ones should have them carried around. — (soma: third upasad day: agnīṣomīya paśu)

Then, at the time of awakening during that night, before the singing of birds, having been invited for the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> (morning litany), observing silence, having approached by the ford, bending the knee at the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-kindler's hearth), one should offer an oblation: 'Protect me from the nearby danger, from any curse, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

At the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire): 'May Speech, going foremost, go first. To <s>Sarasvatī</s>, to Speech, <s>svāhā</s>.' 'Divine Speech, mind-guided, sovereign, fierce, victorious, supreme — partake here. Let us mount that [speech] like the <s>Ādityas</s> [mount] a ship — approved, carrying [us] along the paths, <s>svāhā</s>' — the second [oblation]. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
From here onward, [it is] the same as [the procedure] of the <s>Brahman</s> (prayer). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
Having reached the <s>havirdhāna</s> (soma-cart shed), he touches the crossbar [reciting]: 'Wide is the atmosphere; enter.' — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
'The two door-posts, the divine doors — do not shut me out. Make for me a place, you two who create a place.' — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
Having entered, having sat down between the yoke-supports, when directed, he should recite the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> (morning litany) in a soft [voice]. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

body.text:
āpo.revatīḥ.kṣayathā.hi.vasva.upa.prayanta.iti.sūkte.avā.no.agna.iti.ṣaḷ.agnim.īḷe.agnim.dūtam.vasiṣva.hi.iti.sūktayor.uttamām.uddharet./ (soma: sutyā day: prātar.Anuvāka)
  tvam.agne.vratapā.ity.uttamām.uddharet.tvam.no.agne.mahobhir.iti.nava.ime.viprasya.iti.sūkte.yukṣvā.hi.preṣṭham.vas.tvam.agne.bṛhadvaya.ity.aṣṭādaśa./ṣoma: sutyā day: prātar.Anuvāka)
body.translated_text: 'O rich waters, you dwell in wealth'; 'Come near' — in these two hymns; 'Help us, O <s>Agni</s>' — six [verses]; in the hymns 'I praise <s>Agni</s>' and '<s>Agni</s> the messenger, inspire' — one should omit the last [verse of each]. 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the vow-keeper' — one should omit the last. 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, with great powers' — nine. 'These [hymns] of the inspired one' — in the hymn; 'Yoke the most dear one'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, of great power' — eighteen. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

In the hymn 'Worshipping you'; in the hymn 'O <s>Agni</s>, pure one, messenger'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, the <s>hotṛ</s>, of our sacrifice' — three [verses]; '<s>Agni</s> the <s>hotṛ</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, <s>Iḷā</s>' — four [verses]. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'Forth for you, O <s>Vājas</s>, for the <s>upasadya</s> (approach offering)'; 'That <s>Agni</s> of the sacrifices' — three, one should omit the last; '<s>Agni</s>, the swan'; 'May they invoke <s>Agni</s> for us'; 'Forth to <s>Agni</s> with speech' — in the hymn; 'This [fuel] for me, O <s>Agni</s>, the kindling, this' — of the three, one should omit the last — thus [ends] the <s>Gāyatra</s> (Gāyatrī section). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'You, O <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>'; 'You indeed [are] the possessor of the dwelling'; '<s>Agni</s> the <s>hotṛ</s> was born'; 'Forth for the god <s>Agni</s>'; 'How [shall we praise] you?' — five [verses]. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'O friends, together'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, rich in oblations' — in the hymn; 'Of great power' — of the ten, one should omit the fourth and ninth, and the last and the last, and the first three — thus [ends] the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> (Anuṣṭubh section). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'<s>Agni</s> blazed forth unobstructed, with the kindling-fuel' — four [hymns]; 'Forth to <s>Agni</s>, the great, the wise, the sage'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, knowing <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [bonds]' — from this onward, four [hymns]. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'Upward, indeed, for us'; 'Of [him who is] sleeping, when separated' — five; in the hymn 'Auspicious for you, O <s>Agni</s>'; 'Of <s>Soma</s>'; 'The powerful one'; 'Against <s>Agni</s>, the dawns' — three; 'O <s>hotṛ</s>' — of ten, the third in the eighth should be omitted. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

Of the two hymns 'From heaven' — one should omit the last of the first; 'For you indeed, O <s>Agni</s>, the first' — of six, the second should be omitted; 'Before you, the delightful one' — four. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'That one of beautiful face' — six; 'I invoke you of beautiful shining'; 'O <s>hotṛ</s>, at the <s>hotṛ</s>'s seat' — in the hymn; 'Three-headed' — three; 'The swift one, the glorious one, urging on' — three. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

In the hymn 'Who approaches?'; 'Golden-haired' — three; in the hymn 'I have seen of that great one'; in the hymn 'Of different form'; '<s>Agni</s>, lead'; 'The great one in front' — of eight, one should omit the last three from the end. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'You, O <s>Agni</s>, easy to invoke, delightful to behold' — five; '<s>Agni</s>, your god' — of ten, the third and fourth should be omitted — thus [ends] the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> (Triṣṭubh section). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'Thus your <s>Agni</s>'; 'Forth, O vigorous one'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, descendant of <s>Vivasvat</s>'; 'O friend, you'; 'This <s>Agni</s>'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, come to us; sharp-flamed' — six. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'The path-finder has appeared' — seven — thus [ends] the <s>Bārhata</s> (Bṛhatī section). 'O <s>Agni</s>, of the prize' — three; 'Much you'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, I praise' — [thus ends] the <s>Auṣṇiha</s> (Uṣṇih section). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'The guardian of the people'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, lovers of <s>Ṛta</s>'; 'This guest of yours, the dawn-waking one' — nine; in the hymn 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, with days'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, the first <s>Aṅgiras</s>'; 'Born of force, immortal, shake not'; 'Shake' — five. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)

'Seated on the <s>vedi</s>' — of six, the third should be omitted; 'This praise to the worthy one'; 'With those who are awakened'; 'The wondrous one'; 'Of the young one'; 'The beneficent one'; 'Not the wondrous one of great [power]' — thus [ends] the <s>Jāgata</s> (Jagatī section). 'I consider that <s>Agni</s>' — [thus ends] the <s>Pāṅkta</s> (Paṅkti section). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
Thus [concludes] the <s>Āgneya Kratu</s> (rite dedicated to <s>Agni</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
Now [the hymns] to the Dawns. — (soma: sutyā day: prātaranuvāka)
'Against that beautiful woman, the Dawn' — three — thus [ends] the <s>Gāyatra</s> (Gāyatrī section). 'O <s>Uṣas</s>, with blessings' — [thus ends] the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> (Anuṣṭubh section).

In the hymn 'This best, broad-charioted one,' [reciting] 'Reflecting back' — eight [verses]. 'Shining, O <s>Uṣas</s>, with prize' and in the hymn 'This indeed, that, up the splendor' [reciting] 'O dawn-born, to you' — six [verses] — this is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [portion]. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

'It has been seen with wealth' — [this is] the <s>Bārhatam</s> (Bṛhatī meter portion). 'O <s>Uṣas</s>, bring that wondrous [wealth]' — three [verses, in] <s>Uṣṇih</s> meter. 'These with help' — four [verses, in] <s>Jagatī</s> meter. 'For us today' — [in] <s>Paṅkti</s> meter — these are the <s>uṣasya</s> (dawn-related) <s>kratu</s> (rites). — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Now the <s>Āśvina</s> (relating to the <s>Aśvins</s>) [hymns]. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

'This dawn, with the morning-yoked ones' — four [verses]. '<s>Aśvins</s>, [you who receive] the offerings of the worshippers.' '<s>Aśvins</s>, with horse-rich [offerings].' 'O rich in cows, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>' — [these are] <s>tṛcas</s> (sets of three verses). — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

'From far away, right here' — three [verses]; one should remove the last. 'Most invoked among your invocations' — four [verses]. 'Rise up, come to my call' — [this is in] <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter]. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
In the hymn 'When you came' [reciting] 'To us with all [aids]' and 'That same <s>Atri</s>' — [this is] the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [portion]. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

In the hymn 'The fire shines forth,' '<s>Nāsatyas</s>, like pressing-stones' — three [sets]. 'The milk-cow of ancient [lineage]' and 'Who shall hear of [his] fame' — in [that] hymn. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

In the hymn 'I praise the heroes,' from 'Your realms' — of the five [verses], one should remove the third. 'Your chariot' — of the seven [verses], one should remove the second — this is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [portion]. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

'These indeed for you,' 'This one for you,' 'O, that one I have called,' 'To the chariot' — seven [verses]. 'O resplendent ones, when you are' — [this is] the <s>Bārhatam</s> (Bṛhatī meter portion). '<s>Aśvins</s>, your turning [to us]' and '<s>Aśvins</s>, come here' — [these are] two <s>tṛcas</s>. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

'I invoke your chariot' — fifteen [verses] — this is the <s>Uṣṇih</s> [portion]. '<s>Agni</s> has been awakened; the radiance of this one [shines] over the earth.' 'Your chariot has come.' 'This one who goes around you' — three [verses]. 'Thrice for us today.' 'I invoke heaven and earth' — [this is] the <s>Jagatī</s> [portion]. 'The most beloved' — [this is] the <s>Paṅkti</s> [portion]. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Thus, the separate hymns of these meters [constitute] the morning <s>anuvāka</s> (litany). — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Beginning with a hundred [verses], it is unlimited. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
One should not replace the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] addressed to <s>Agni</s> with others, for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Nor the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter] for a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior). Nor the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter] for a <s>vaiśya</s> (commoner). — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Those with one foot or two feet [are used] when there is a surplus. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Whose fixed positions are the auspicious [verses]: 'We have attained,' 'May we cross over,' 'I invoke heaven and earth.' — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
'With those who are awake' — and [this verse is] for one who is directed [and] desires heaven. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
One should repeat the 'I invoke heaven and earth' [verse] until the dispelling of darkness. — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)
Having ascended to the time-ending [verse], from the seated middle position, one should continue joining with 'the most beloved.' — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

Having ascended again with the final [verse] from the highest position, one should enclose [the recitation], between the two doorpost pillars, as if calling out 'Hear ye!', as if calling out 'Hear ye!' — (soma: pressing day: morning <s>anuvāka</s>)

When [the fire has been] enclosed, having sipped [water], when told 'O <s>Hotṛ</s>,' without uttering the hiṃkāra, he recites the <s>āponaputrīyā</s> (hymns to the waters, sons of the gods), softer than the <s>paridhānīyā</s> (enclosing verse). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

Their <s>nigada</s> (recitation formulas) and so forth [are recited] softly, and [also] those [up] until the crawling forth (<s>prasarpaṇa</s>). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
After that, in a sweet [tone]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
And the morning pressing [is performed]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
The first [verse] with one-and-a-half <s>kāras</s> (syllables), the subsequent ones in the normal <s>ṛgāvāna</s> (Ṛg-Veda recitation style). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
For one desiring rain, [the recitation follows] the basic form. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
When the basic form applies, one should look for identifying marks in the first half-verses of those [hymns]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
'Forth to the gods, may the path go for the prayer' — nine [verses]. 'Quicken our sacrifice, O worship of the gods' — as the tenth. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
'The returning ones' and 'Now with double streams' — [these are used] at the turning, in the single-prize [contests]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
'When the waters were seen coming back' — when [the waters are] being seen. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
'The milk cows with milk, swiftly [coming] for the purpose.' — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
'Some come together, others approach.' — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

At the <s>tīrtha</s> (proper place), when the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup is being filled with water [one recites]: 'The divine waters approach the <s>hotrīya</s> (hotṛ's cup)' — having completed [this], one should conclude with the <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable 'om'). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

When the <s>adhvaryu</s> has arrived, [the hotṛ] asks: 'Have you obtained the waters? O <s>adhvaryu</s>?' [Reciting] 'And these [waters] bowed down.' When answered, pronouncing the <s>nigada</s> (formula), he should go out to meet [him]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

Among those [recitations]: 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, you will press <s>soma</s> for <s>Indra</s> — honey-sweet, rain-winning, sharp-ended, full in the middle — for the <s>Vasu</s>-possessing, <s>Rudra</s>-possessing, <s>Āditya</s>-possessing, <s>Ṛbhu</s>-possessing, <s>Vibhu</s>-possessing, <s>Vāja</s>-possessing, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>-possessing, <s>Viśvedeva</s>-possessing one' — having stated the <s>anavāna</s> (unceasing invocation) up to the end, one should stand to the north of their path. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
When [the waters] have passed by, one should turn and follow. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

'Of which, <s>Indra</s> having drunk, slew the <s>Vṛtras</s>; may we cross over the battle-fields; the waters go along the paths' — three [verses]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)
One should follow along with the last [verse]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

'These abundant, life-giving ones have come' — two [verses]. When [the waters are] settled, having enclosed [them] with the latter [verse], having placed [oneself] at the northern doorway, one should sit facing the king [<s>Soma</s>], without pushing aside the grass. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>Āponaputrīyā</s> etc.)

When the <s>upāṃśu</s> (silent offering) is being poured: 'Give breath, <s>svāhā</s>; you of good invocation, you of good invocation, for <s>Sūrya</s>, breath — give me breath' — having consecrated [with this mantra], one should breathe after [reciting] 'uḥ.' — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

For the <s>antaryāma</s> (inner restrainer [cup]): 'Give the down-breath, <s>svāhā</s>; you of good invocation, for <s>Sūrya</s>, down-breath — give me down-breath' — having consecrated [with this], one should also breathe downward [reciting] 'ūm.' — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
Having touched the <s>upāṃśu savana</s> (silent pressing) stone [reciting] 'For the diffused breath, you' — one should release speech. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

For the <s>Pavamāna</s> (purifying [Soma]) procession, following the <s>chandogas</s> (Sāma-Veda singers) — the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and the <s>Brahman</s> [priest go] as permanent [attendants]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
Between those two, the other consecrated ones, if any. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

Having offered the two <s>vipruṭhomas</s> (scattered-drop oblations) with the two [verses] 'The drop has fallen,' facing the <s>adhvaryu</s>, holding on to each other, they crawl forward up to the proper place (<s>tīrtha</s>). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
They sit down for the <s>stotra</s> (chant), facing the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanter). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

The <s>hotṛ</s> consecrates them, sitting right there: 'Among the gods here, the <s>soma</s>-drinking is at the sacrifice, on the sacred grass, on the altar. We partake of that; you are the mouth, may I become the mouth.' — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
If a consecrated one should go [outside], [he returns] for the <s>stotra</s> response. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
And he should crawl [back] at the two later pressings. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
'O <s>Brahman</s>, we shall chant; O <s>Praśāstṛ</s>' — when released for the <s>stotra</s>, they complete [the recitation]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

Having muttered '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, O <s>Indra</s>-possessing ones, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>,' the <s>Brahman</s> [says] 'Om, chant!' at the morning pressing. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

'<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>' at the midday [pressing]. '<s>Svaḥ</s>' at the third pressing. '<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>, O <s>Indra</s>-possessing ones, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>' — after the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> (hymn to <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)

Having been praised by the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, impelled [by him]: 'Speak truth and right. Sing verses that give long life. Protect the body with <s>sāman</s> (chant). Om' — having muttered [this], 'O <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, chant!' — loudly. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>upāṃśu graha</s> etc.)
Then they proceed with the <s>savanīya paśu</s> (pressing-day animal [sacrifice]). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
According to whatever deity it belongs to. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)

[The animal] for <s>Agni</s> [is offered] at the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> at the <s>Ukthya</s> — the second; for <s>Indra</s> the bull at the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> — the third; a <s>Sārasvatī</s> (ewe for <s>Sarasvatī</s>) at the <s>Atirātra</s> — the fourth. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
These are the animals for the [respective] rites. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)

From the circumambulation, [the procedure is] linked with the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>), up to the purification at the <s>cātvāla</s> (pit), except for the handing over of the staff. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
Having sat down and uttered the <s>hiṃkāra</s>, [one recites] the circumambulation [verses] three times. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)

'I invoke the gods for the pressing sacrificer' — the invocation begins [with this]; the word 'pressing' [comes] before the word 'sacrificer' in the <s>iṣṭi</s>-related prescriptions. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
Not beyond the final <s>hāriyojana</s> (yoking for Hari [<s>Indra</s>]). — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)

No <s>pavitra</s> (purification). 'Well for you, O sacrificer; the deities consent; om; they follow along in this sacrifice, O sacrificer' — and [this formula]. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)

Before the ghee-drinkers [receive their portions], one should invoke the pressing-day deities: 'Bring <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Vasus</s>; bring <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Rudras</s>; bring <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s>, with the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, with the <s>Vibhus</s>, with the <s>Vājas</s>, with <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, with the <s>Viśvedevas</s> — invoke!' — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
One should continue those [invocations] in the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn recitation) itself. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
They offer the preliminary oblations; the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> callers are others than the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)

Having purified [themselves] at the <s>cātvāla</s> (pit), they attend upon the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (subsidiary fire-hearths) beginning with the <s>Āditya</s> one, along the <s>adhvaryu</s>'s path. — (soma: pressing day: morning: <s>savanīya paśu</s> – <s>prasarpaṇa</s>)
First, [one should venerate] the sun. 'O lord of paths, best of paths, may I safely reach the end of this path.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

From the sacrificial post onward, the fires are churned from the <s>āhavanīya</s>; [they are called] <s>sagara</s> fires: 'You are fires, you are <s>Sagaras</s>, by the name <s>Sagara</s>. Protect me, O fires; I, the fallen one, [belong to] <s>Agni</s>. Homage to you; do not harm me.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

Turning to the left, [one passes by] the <s>śāmitra</s> (slaughter-shed), <s>ūvadhya</s> (refuse-pit), <s>goha</s> (cattle-pen), <s>cātvāla</s> (pit), <s>utkara</s> (heap), and <s>āstāva</s> (praise-station). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

Likewise, turning to the right, [one passes by] the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), the <s>acchāvāka</s>'s seat, the southern <s>mārjalīya</s> (purification-shed), and the <s>khara</s> (hard ground). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

Having circumambulated to the north of the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> and having reached the <s>sadas</s> (assembly-shed), they touch [it saying]: 'Wide is the atmosphere; consume!' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
Having touched both door-posts, they similarly approach the others. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
[They approach] both those standing and those not standing, not looking [at them], not examining [them]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

The <s>hotṛ</s>, <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s>, <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>potṛ</s>, and <s>neṣṭṛ</s> enter the <s>sadas</s> (assembly-shed) through the front door, murmuring: 'You, knowing, will lead us to a wide realm.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

To the north of all the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-hearths), one by one, having sat down behind their respective <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> from the west, they murmur: 'Whatever <s>Soma</s>-born weapon of the malicious ones may arise today — like separating [arrows] with a bow, may they be scattered, [aimed at] the highway-robber. Homage to the lord of the seat.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

Thus, from the approach onward to the end of the murmuring, [the procedure] is extended [to all]. The priests who perform the <s>prasarpaṇa</s> (solemn entry) follow him. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

To the east of the <s>audumbarī</s> (udumbara post), to the west of the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>, they sit down one after another in their respective positions. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)

By this same procedure, the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-tender) [approaches] the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), even [when there is] an open space. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
The <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (fire-hearths) of the <s>prasarpiṇs</s> (processional priests) begin from the south and end in the north. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
But the first two are reversed. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
Their movement when leaving [is] to the north of their respective <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
[They move] to the south of the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-paśu - prasarpaṇa)
Then they perform [the offering] with <s>puroḍāśas</s> (sacrificial cakes) for <s>Indra</s>, at each pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)
'With parched grain and gruel' — this is the invitatory verse (<s>anuvākyā</s>) at the morning pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)

'The parched grain of the midday pressing' — at the midday [pressing]. 'The parched grain at the third pressing, O much-praised one' — at the third pressing. 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Indra</s>; may <s>Indra</s> of the bay horses eat the parched grain' — the <s>praiṣa</s> (direction) [varies] at each pressing by characteristic words. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)
Having extracted the directive word, the offering [is made] with that very [word]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)

'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to that [deity]' — in the offering [and] the <s>āguḥ</s> (response) and <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation) at their proper places, wherever one offers with a <s>praiṣa</s> (direction). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)

Then, for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to the fire): 'O <s>Agni</s>, enjoy our oblation'; 'At the midday pressing, O <s>Jātavedas</s>'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, at the third pressing, whom do you desire?' — these are the invitatory verses at each pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)

'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Agni</s> the <s>puroḍāśas</s>' — this is the <s>praiṣa</s> (direction). 'O <s>Agni</s>, consume the oblation' — this is the offering verse. In these invitatory verses, some [treat] the word '<s>puroḍāśa</s>' as plural. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)
It is known: 'That syllable of the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) which one modifies is corrupted or decays; therefore one should not modify a verse.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: savanīya-puroḍāśa)
They perform [offerings] with two-deity [cups]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

For the <s>Vāyava</s> (Vāyu offering) and <s>Indra-Vāyu</s> [offerings]: 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come, beautiful to behold'; '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, these [soma juices] are pressed' — these are the invitatory verses, without lowering [the voice], with separate <s>praṇavas</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Vāyu</s> the foremost'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s>, the worthy ones' — these are the two <s>praiṣas</s> (directions), without lowering [the voice]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

'Drink first of the sweet [soma juices]' — these are the offering verses, without lowering [the voice], with a single <s>āguḥ</s> (response) and separate <s>vaṣaṭkāras</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
This 'without lowering' [rule] is first [applied to] the invitatory verses of the morning pressing offerings. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
And the <s>praiṣas</s> (directions) for the latter two cups. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
Having offered, the <s>adhvaryu</s> brings back this cup-vessel. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
One should receive it [saying]: 'May the wealthy one, the one of many riches, come.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
Having received [it], uncovering the right thigh, having placed [it] on that, one should cover [it] with fingers leaving spaces [between them]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
Likewise for the subsequent [cups]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

body.text:
savyena.tv.apidhāya.tayoḥ.pratigraho.bhakṣaṇam.ca./ (soma: sutyā day: morniṅg: misc.)
  maitrāvaruṇasya.ayam.vām.mitrā.varuṇā.hotā.yakṣan.mitrā.varuṇā.gṛṇānā.jamadaginnā.ity.aitu.vasur.vidadvasur.iti.pratigṛhya.dakṣiṇena.aindra.vāyavam.hṛtvā.abhyātmam.sādanam./(soma: sutyā day: morniṅg: misc.)
body.translated_text: But covering with the left [hand], [there is] the receiving and partaking of those two. For the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [cup]: 'This is yours, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'Being praised by <s>Jamadagni</s>' — having received [saying] 'May the wealthy one, the finder of wealth, come,' having carried [it] to the right of the <s>Aindra-Vāyava</s> [cup], the placing is inward. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

For the <s>Āśvina</s> (offering to the <s>Aśvins</s>): 'Awaken at dawn with your partner'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Nāsatyas</s>, the increasing ones, the lords of beauty.' 'May the wealthy one, the well-united wealthy one, come' — having received [it], having carried [it] in the same way, having passed it over the head to the north, the placing is still more inward. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
In the invitatory verses, <s>praiṣas</s> (directions), and offering verses, the <s>sampraiṣa</s> (joint direction) from the <s>adhvaryu</s> is constant. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
As [the cups] are being raised, he recites [the following verses]: 'May they carry you hither; that [deity] is divine; come here' — at each pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Indra</s> of the morning, of the morning pressing'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Indra</s> of the midday pressing'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Indra</s> of the third pressing' — thus directed, the <s>hotṛ</s>, being directed at each pressing, offers with the <s>prasthita-yājyās</s> (processional offering verses). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
The others [offer] with a name-substitution. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
The praised ones [are]: <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>potṛ</s>, <s>neṣṭṛ</s>, <s>āgnīdhra</s>, and <s>acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

At the latter two pressings, before the <s>āgnīdhra</s>'s [portion]: 'This is your <s>soma</s> drink'; 'We invoke <s>Mitra</s>'; '<s>Indra</s>, you the bull, we [invoke]'; 'O <s>Maruts</s>, in whose abode'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, bring hither the wives'; 'For one who eats ox-food, for one who eats cow-food' — these are the <s>prasthita-yājyās</s> (processional offering verses) belonging to the morning pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

'Drink the <s>soma</s>, O you who powerfully struck' — three [verses]; 'Come hither, O <s>Soma</s>; they call you desirable; this <s>soma</s> is yours; come hither; for <s>Indra</s>, the <s>soma</s> juices, known from heaven; the full vessel is [offered], <s>svāhā</s>' — these are for the midday [pressing]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

'O <s>Indra</s>, with the <s>Ṛbhus</s> who possess prizes, [the soma] sprinkled'; 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, drinkers of the pressed [soma], this pressed [soma]'; '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, drink the <s>soma</s>'; 'May the seven swift ones carry you here'; 'O you of the beautiful forest, come here at our invocation'; 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, drink of this sweet [soma]'; 'This praise for worthy <s>Jātavedas</s>' — these are for the third pressing. 'Of <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, consume' — this is the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response exclamation). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

Among the <s>prasthita-yājyās</s> (processional offering verses) [and] the <s>śastra-yājyās</s> (recitation offering verses): in the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation], the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [cup], and the <s>Mahimna</s> [cup]; and in the <s>Āśvina</s> [recitation] and the <s>Tairaahnya</s> (third-day rite). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

On this, this sacrificial song (<s>gāthā</s>) is sung: 'The seasonal offerings, the two-deity [offerings], and whatever is the <s>Patnīvata</s> cup, the <s>Āditya</s> cup, and the <s>Sāvitra</s> [cups] — to those you should not give the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response exclamation).' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
The partaking [follows] each <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
The latter [partaking is done] silently. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
The <s>adhvaryu</s> comes. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
'Has he offered?' he asks the <s>āgnīdhra</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
'He has offered,' [the <s>āgnīdhra</s>] replies. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)
'He has done well who will give us <s>soma</s> to drink' — the <s>hotṛ</s> murmurs. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: misc.)

Having taken the <s>Aindra-Vāyava</s> [cup] in the upper half, one should hand it to the <s>adhvaryu</s> [saying]: 'This is the wealthy one, the one of many riches; here is the wealthy one, the one of many riches; in me is the wealthy one, the one of many riches. O speech-protector, protect my speech. May speech, invoked, together with breath, invoke me. May speech together with breath call upon me. May the invoked divine sages, the self-purifiers, the austerity-born, call upon me. May the divine sages, the self-purifiers, the austerity-born, call upon me.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)

Having said 'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, invite,' having smelled with the nostrils, 'May the goddess Speech be satisfied with <s>soma</s>' — thus one should partake, everywhere. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)

Having poured a little of what has been partaken back into the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup, without sipping water, having caused [the others] to partake again beginning from the invitation — 'They do not become polluted by <s>soma</s>,' so they declare. The remainder, having been brought to the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup, one should release. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)
Likewise for the subsequent [cups]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)
But for those two [latter cups], there is no re-partaking. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)
One should not release any of the two-deity [cups] without having poured back [a portion]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)

For the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [cup]: 'This is the wealthy one, the finder of wealth; here is the wealthy one, the finder of wealth; in me is the wealthy one, the finder of wealth. O sight-protector, protect my sight. May sight, invoked, together with mind, invoke me. May sight together with mind call upon me. May the invoked divine sages, the self-purifiers, the austerity-born, call upon me. May the divine sages, the self-purifiers, the austerity-born, call upon me.' — (soma: sutyā day: morning: soma-bhakṣaṇa - āpyāyana)
But the looking here [is done] with the eyes, with the right [eye] first.
One should take the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup with the left hand [reciting]: 'May the lord of the <s>Vasus</s>, the kindling of all the gods, come.'
Uncovering the garment from his thigh with the elbow of that [hand], having placed [the cup] on it, one should cover [it] with fingers leaving spaces between them.

Having carried the <s>Āśvina</s> (Aśvin cup) around as brought, having placed [it] again, one should hand [it] to the <s>adhvaryu</s> [reciting]: 'This is the wealthy one; the well-united wealthy one; here is the wealthy one; the well-united wealthy one; in me is the wealthy one; the well-united wealthy one. O hearing-protector, protect my hearing. May hearing, invoked, together with the self, invoke me. May hearing together with the self call upon me. May the invoked divine sages, the self-purifiers, the austerity-born, call upon me. May the divine sages, the self-purifiers, the austerity-born, call upon me.'
But one should raise [the cup] to the ears here, placing it to the right [ear] first. Having touched the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup and touched water, one invokes the <s>iḷā</s>.
They raise the cups.
Having tasted the intermediate <s>iḷā</s> and sipped water, one should partake of the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup, having said 'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, invite.'
'O consecrated ones, invite yourselves.'
Or [they say]: 'O sacrificers.'
Likewise for the others.
They look at [each cup] according to [which has] the same partaking.
Those without cups [partake] from the principal cup.
Or from the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> (large soma vessel).
The <s>soma</s>-partaking murmured prayer has been stated [and applies] everywhere.

At the <s>hotṛ</s>'s <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation), the cups call [to the deities for] the <s>udgātṛ</s>, <s>brahmā</s>, and the sacrificer. Of these, the <s>hotṛ</s> should partake first — so [says] <s>Gautama</s>, because the partaking follows the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>.
The others should not partake — so [says] <s>Taulvali</s>, because the purpose has been accomplished.

They should partake — so [says] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>, because [the rite] here has the character of a <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecrating act); what else would constitute their cup-status, and there is no other connection.
Having partaken, 'We have drunk <s>Soma</s>; we have become immortal; be auspicious to us, O drop drunk into the heart' — they should touch the mouth and heart.
'Be nourished; may [all] come together for you; may the nourishing fluids be [plentiful]; may the prizes come together' — the first and second cups [are used] at the first two pressings.
The first [cups are used] at the third pressing.
Everywhere [one nourishes] oneself, except for the single-vessel [cups].
Having nourished the cups, they set them down; those become the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (belonging to Narāśaṃsa) [cups].

At this time, the <s>acchāvāka</s>, going forth, passing to the north of the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), should sit down at the place of his <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-hearth) in front of the <s>sadas</s> (sitting hall).

Having raised the <s>puroḍāśa-dṛgaḷa</s> (cake-portion) that has been offered, like an <s>iḷā</s>, when told 'O <s>acchāvāka</s>, speak,' he recites the <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse hymn): 'To your <s>Agni</s>, for help.'

With the final <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) he should continue: 'O sacrificer, <s>hotṛ</s>, <s>adhvaryu</s>, <s>āgnīdhra</s>, <s>brahmā</s>, <s>potṛ</s>, <s>neṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>upavaktṛ</s> — seek nourishment, win vigor. Let your kinswomen yield [to you], let the non-kinswomen [yield]; let rivals be driven away on the road. Win the unconquerable [power]; win the unconquerable [power]. May <s>Indra</s> hear you; may <s>Agni</s> hear you. Having gone forth, proclaim the <s>soma</s> to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>. Call us <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s to yourselves, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s.'
When this recitation is complete, the <s>adhvaryu</s> awaits the invocation from the <s>hotṛ</s>.
'The pressing sacrificer has come toward [us]; he has grasped the well-recited [hymns] for you. And the <s>upavaktṛ</s> stands firm.' 'Our cows are invited; invited' — thus he invites.
'Having been invited, [the response] to him' — having recited along with the [soma] being drawn up, 'With the morning [hymns] by which you came' — thus he offers.
Having set down the <s>puroḍāśa-dṛgaḷa</s> (cake-portion) and touched the cup, one should partake.
Without touching water, they should not touch other oblations after [touching] <s>soma</s>.
