Having taken it, having attended upon the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (fire-hearths) beginning with the <s>Āditya</s> one, entering the <s>sadas</s> (sitting hall) through the back door, having sat down behind his own <s>dhiṣṇya</s>, one should eat.
When [all are] seated, having brought the <s>brahmā</s>'s [portion] to the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), all should eat the remainder of the oblation. The others have already gone before.
Having eaten, having crept back.
They perform the <s>ṛtu-yājas</s> (seasonal offerings).
Their <s>praiṣas</s> (directive formulas) [are as follows].
The fifth is the <s>praiṣa-sūkta</s> (directive hymn).
Being directed by each respective [formula], each one offers according to the directive.
The <s>hotṛ</s>, when told 'O <s>hotṛ</s>, offer this,' by the <s>adhvaryu</s> and the householder.
[He offers] by himself on the sixth day, the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back) day.
The <s>adhvaryu</s> sits down behind the northern <s>vedi</s> (altar). The householder [sits] behind the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire).
Then they partake of this <s>ṛtu-pātra</s> (seasonal cup) in succession — those who perform the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation).
The <s>adhvaryu</s> should partake separately.
And the invocation [is made] in that very [cup].

After the latter [offerings], when the <s>adhvaryu</s> has turned back, having murmured: 'The well-footed one with good songs, father <s>Mātariśvan</s>, placed unbroken steps; unbroken songs the sages recited. <s>Soma</s> the all-knowing shall lead the tracks; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> shall recite the hymn-ecstasies. Speech, life-span, universal life, universal life-span — who will recite this? He will recite this' — without making the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (exclamation), calling out aloud '<s>śoṃsāvom</s>' (let us recite), one should recite the silent recitation, in a low voice, with the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), without continuation.

This is the invocation (<s>āhāva</s>) at the morning pressing, at the beginning of the recitations; and of [the sections] beginning with the <s>paryāya</s> (cycle); and everywhere the inner recitation.
And through that [is made] the continuation.
The recitation tone, the response — '<s>othāmo daiva</s>' (we praise, O divine one).
'<s>Śoṃsāmo daiva</s>' (let us recite, O divine one) — at the invocation.
Prolonged [vowel] at the beginning of the <s>praṇava</s>, short [vowel] at the beginning of the conclusion.
After the <s>praṇava</s>, the <s>praṇava</s>-invocation [follows].
And at the conclusion.
Or ending with the <s>praṇava</s>.
Wherever the inner recitation concludes with the <s>praṇava</s>, there the response also ends with the <s>praṇava</s>. But at the end of the [full] recitation, [there is] a <s>praṇava</s>.

'<s>Bhūḥ</s> — <s>Agni</s> is light, light is <s>Agni</s>. <s>Indra</s> is light — <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> — light is <s>Indra</s>. <s>Sūrya</s> is light, light — <s>Svaḥ</s> — is <s>Sūrya</s>' — the three-footed silent recitation. But if it is six-footed, one should conclude with the earlier 'light' words first.
Aloud [one recites] the <s>nivid</s> (laudatory insertion), as at the conclusion [of recitation]: '<s>Agni</s>, kindled by the gods.'
There is no invocation for it.
And no continuation.
With the last foot 'Forth to the god,' one should continue [into] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee hymn).
By this [rule, the continuations] after the <s>nivid</s>s [are governed].
And all the foot-by-foot recitations.
But the continuation [is done] otherwise [than the nivid].
And the invocation of the <s>nivid</s>s.
The first <s>ājya</s> (ghee verse) should be recited three times, in half-verses, with pauses.
We shall demonstrate that: 'Forth to the god <s>Agni</s>, recite the highest [hymn] to him. May he come with the gods to the seat, the most sacrificing, sitting on the sacred grass.'
Or the <s>ṛgāvāna</s> (verse-recitation) in just this way. By this [rule], the initial verses of the <s>pratipads</s> (opening verses) [are recited] without the <s>ṛgāvāna</s> [style].
Or [one follows] the order according to the <s>anubrāhmaṇa</s> (supplementary Brāhmaṇa).
Having called out, one encloses [the hymn] with the final [verse].
Thus for the enclosing verses of all recitations.

'The utterance in speech, for your glory' — having recited, one should murmur. 'O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>, in the dwelling of the worshiper' — this is the offering verse. One should partake of the <s>uktha-pātra</s> (utterance-cup) first.
Then the cup-holders [partake of] the cups — at the end of the offering verse of every recitation.
The one who performs the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> [partakes of] the single-vessel [cups], except for the <s>Āditya</s> cup, the <s>Sāvitra</s> [cup], and the <s>graha</s> (cup).
The <s>stotra</s> (chant) [comes] before the recitation.
When 'this one' has been announced, at the <s>udgātṛ</s>'s <s>hiṃkāra</s> (humming), they should summon [the recitation] at the morning pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
At the <s>pratihāra</s> (response) in the latter two pressings. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

'<s>Vāyu</s> is the foremost, delighting in sacrifice' — of the seven <s>purorucas</s> (dawn-hymns), after each one, he should recite a <s>tṛca</s> (group of three verses). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come, beautiful to behold' — seven <s>tṛcas</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
The second [<s>puroruc</s> is recited] three times in the <s>prauga</s> (opening recitation). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
He should summon from the <s>purorucas</s>; at the sixth, he should pause thrice, at each half-verse. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
The last [<s>puroruc</s>] he should not recite. Some recite [it]; the <s>tṛca</s>-summoning [replaces it] when not reciting. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
They call this the <s>Mādhucchandasa</s> <s>prauga</s> (opening recitation [composed by <s>Madhucchandas</s>]). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

'The recitation is in speech; for the sake of fame [I recite] to you' — having recited thus, one should murmur. 'With all [gods] the <s>soma</s> sweetness' — [this is] the offering verse. The praised [reciters are]: <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>acchāvāka</s> — these are the <s>hotraka</s> (assistant <s>hotṛ</s>) reciters. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
Their recitations have four summonings at the morning pressing, third pressing, in the <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds), and in the additional [recitations]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
Five summonings at the midday [pressing]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

From the <s>stotriya</s> (praise-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse), from the <s>pratipad</s> (opening verse) and <s>anucara</s> (accompanying verse), from the <s>pragāthas</s> (chant-pairs), from the <s>dhāyyās</s> (meditation chants) — [there is] a separate summoning [for each]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
Also [for] the <s>hotṛ</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
And [for] another [element] immediately following those. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
At the beginning, if there are multiple hymns with <s>nivids</s> (ritual insertions), the summoning [is made] at the first ones. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
And in the <s>tṛca</s> (triad) addressed to the waters as deity. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

Of those, the <s>stotriyas</s> (praise-verses) and <s>anurūpas</s> (corresponding verses) are <s>tṛcas</s>, everywhere at the beginnings of recitations. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
At the midday [pressing], <s>pragāthas</s> (chant-pairs) [are] the third [element]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
The rest [is] as prescribed. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
The recitations end with the offering verse (<s>yājyā</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
'The recitation is in speech' — this is their murmuring after recitation at the morning pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
And above [i.e., after] the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteenth cup), for all [reciters]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

'The recitation is in speech, for <s>Indra</s>' — at the midday [pressing]. 'The recitation is in speech, for <s>Indra</s>, for the gods' — at the <s>ukthas</s> (praise-recitations) together with the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)
The immediately following [is recited] before [the preceding one]. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

The <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse) [should match] the <s>stotriya</s> (praise-verse) in meter, measure, characteristic mark, and deity. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.) (Comm: the mark [refers to words like] 'āvatī,' 'pravatī,' etc.)
And some [say it should also match in] the seer (<s>ārṣa</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

'Come to us, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'Come to us, O destroyer of foes'; 'Forth to <s>Mitra</s>'; 'Of the two <s>Mitras</s> and <s>Varuṇas</s>' — nine [verses]. 'Come, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — [this is] the offering verse. 'Come, O [<s>Indra</s>] of beautiful songs, for you indeed' — six [verses as] <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>; the immediately following [are] seven. '<s>Indra</s>, you the bull'; 'Rise up' — three [verses]. '<s>Indra</s>, the drink of pressed [<s>soma</s>]' — [this is] the offering verse. 'O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, come to the pressed [<s>soma</s>]'; 'O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, from [your] works'; 'The praise-singer of the <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayers I invoke' — three [verses]. 'Here, O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, by your thought' — nine [verses]. 'O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, come to the pressed [<s>soma</s>]' — [this is] the offering verse. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: prauga-śastra etc.)

When the pressings are concluded, and after the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteenth cup) and the <s>atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice), when the <s>praśāstṛ</s> (director) has said 'Direct,' [and the <s>hotṛ</s>] has been told 'Proceed,' the <s>praśāstṛ</s> should dismiss [them saying] 'Move forth.' The <s>hotṛ</s> [exits] to the south of the <s>audumbarī</s> (udumbara post), going straight; the others [exit] through the back door, proceeding forth toward the northern hip of the <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: finale)
They call this the 'deer-ford' (<s>mṛgatīrtha</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: finale)
Having gone out by this [path], [they attend to] whatever purpose, but never for anything other than urination. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: finale)

Having gone out by this [path], having performed ablutions, having attended upon [the fires] together on the <s>vedi</s> (altar), [they return] through the back door by the customary circuit, and having touched the door-posts of the <s>sadas</s>, they silently re-enter (<s>pratiprasarpanti</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: morning: finale)
This circuit [is followed] when 'Move forth' has been said. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: finale)
The householder [enters] through the front door only. — (soma: sutyā day: morning: finale)
At this time, the <s>grāvastut</s> (stone-praiser) takes his position. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
His approach (<s>upasthāna</s>) has been described. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)

Having entered the <s>havirdhāna</s> (soma-cart shed) through the front door, having cleared grass from the front-north [area] of the southern <s>havirdhāna</s> and from the axle-head of the northern one, he stands facing the <s>Soma</s> king. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
Here there is no sitting down. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
But [he recites] 'Whatever <s>Soma</s>-born [weapon today].' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
Then the <s>adhvaryu</s> hands him a turban (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)

Having received that with joined palms, having wound it three times clockwise around the head so as to cover the face, when they push apart the <s>soma</s> stalks for pressing, then he should praise the pressing-stones (<s>grāvāṇas</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
In a middle-pitched voice for this pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)

'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, they yoke the mind to you, and they yoke the thought'; 'Come to us, O <s>Indra</s>, with abundance'; 'Do not proclaim anything else'; 'Let him recite the <s>Arbuda</s> [hymn].' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
Before the last [verse]: 'For you [the soma juices] flow forth'; 'Forth, O pressing-stones' — thus. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)

Between the two hymns, or after or before [them], having inserted the <s>Pāvamānī</s> (purificatory) [verses], as needed, [he continues] until the taking of the <s>āvā</s> cup; with the remainder, he should place the <s>yajamāna</s>'s turban (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>) on the <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
Having taken [it] for whatever purpose on the last days. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
On the other [days], he should hand it back. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
Then one should make another beautiful [turban] — [according to] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)

'Swell up; let [the juices] unite with you' — three [verses]. 'The ten fingers cleanse you'; 'Throw this'; 'The ten fingers'; 'Being cleansed with skillful [hand]'; 'By ten, from <s>Vivasvat</s>, they milk'; 'Seven [sages] milked the one yielding rich nourishment'; 'Into the vessels it flows'; 'Being poured on the filter' — one [verse]; 'Into the vessels it flows'; 'The falcon dives into the armour' — two [verses]. Having extracted the fourth of the <s>Arbuda</s> [hymn] from these, one should place [groups of] <s>tṛcas</s> at the ends of the <s>tṛcas</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
The first [<s>tṛca</s>] while [the soma] is being swelled (<s>āpyāyyamāna</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
The second while [it is] being cleansed (<s>mṛjyamāna</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
The third while [it is] being milked (<s>duhyamāna</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
The fourth while [it is] being poured (<s>āsicyamāna</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
At the sound of the <s>Bṛhat</s> [<s>sāman</s>], at the sound of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, the fourth [<s>tṛca</s>]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
'Do not proclaim anything else' — [this is recited] if the pressing-stones should resound. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
The rest is the same. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
Only the <s>Arbuda</s> [hymn] — [according to] some. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
'Forth, O pressing-stones' — [according to] some. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
The processional entry (<s>sarpaṇa</s>) has been described. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
When the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> (purificatory chant) has been sung, having spread out the coals — — (soma: sutyā day: midday: grāvastut)
They perform [the offering] with the <s>dadhigharma</s> (hot curd offering), if [the sacrifice] includes the <s>Pravargya</s> (heated-milk rite). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
Its <s>ṛgāvāna</s> (verse-chanting) with the <s>gharma</s> (heated offering) has been described. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
And [so have] the offering and the partaking. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
When told 'O <s>hotṛ</s>, speak,' he says 'Rise up, behold.' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
When told 'The oblation is cooked,' he responds 'The oblation is cooked.' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)

'I consider it cooked in the udder, cooked in the fire' — thus he offers. 'O <s>Agni</s>, consume' — this is the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response exclamation). 'O <s>Agni</s>, consume the <s>dadhigharma</s>.' 'May that great <s>Indra</s>-power be in me, may splendour and wisdom [be in me]. May the <s>gharma</s> of triple radiance shine for me, together with resolve and mind, together with the <s>Virāj</s> [meter] and radiance. May I enjoy your stream. Of that [<s>soma</s>] of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, that has been drunk, invoked with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, being invoked, being invoked, I partake' — this is the murmured partaking formula. [This is for the <s>dhiṣṇya</s>-holding priests] toward whom they would spread the coals forward. Having sat down behind his own <s>dhiṣṇya</s> and having desired the invitation, he should murmur: 'O <s>Agni</s>, we [place] a rampart around you.' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
Without having offered — [this applies to] the consecrated one (<s>dīkṣita</s>). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
Before or after the <s>savanīya</s> (pressing-day offerings), they perform [the rite] with a <s>paśu-puroḍāśa</s> (animal-cake offering). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
Some [say there is] no performance, other than when the purpose-related discourse is being spoken. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
<s>Āśmarathya</s> [says there is] performance, because of [its] connection and non-prohibition. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)

The <s>puroḍāśa</s> and the rest have been described, up to the placing of the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [cup]. But here, the two-deity [cups are] not [offered] at this time; the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) are distributed in <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) and <s>ekāha</s> (single-day) sacrifices. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)

Shaking black antelope skins, the consecrated ones (<s>dīkṣitas</s>) themselves go along the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (southern) path in <s>sattras</s> (communal sessions), murmuring: 'I lead myself as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> for the sake of auspicious fame, splendour, glory, and immortality.' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
While [the cups] are being raised, he offers the two <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's) oblations. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)

'I shall give,' says <s>Agni</s>; 'So be it,' says <s>Vāyu</s>; 'Yes!' [says] the Moon; 'True,' [says] the Sun; 'True, Om,' the Waters brought that truth. 'The directions are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fees) of the sacrifice; may I be dear to the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>s, <s>svāhā</s>.' 'Go forth to the east, delighting in the east; may [the stream] of ghee flow, <s>svāhā</s>' — the second [oblation]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)

'Who gave? Who gave to me? Desire gave to desire. Desire is the giver, desire is the receiver. Desire, enter the ocean; with desire I receive you. O Desire, this is yours.' 'You are rain; may heaven give you, may earth receive you' — one should recite over [the dakṣiṇā] as they pass by, if [they are] living beings. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
One should touch [them] if [they are] non-living. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
And [likewise for] a maiden. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
And thus everywhere. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)

Having received [them], having reached the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), they should eat the remnant of the oblation at [that] pressing. Having eaten, having crept back. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: dadhi-gharma etc.)
They proceed with the <s>Marutvatīya</s> cup. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)

'O <s>Indra</s>, accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, drink the <s>soma</s> here'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, together with [them]'; '<s>Indra</s> with his troop of <s>Maruts</s>.' Having partaken, [with] this cup [being] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>, one should recite the <s>śastra</s> (recitation). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, let us recite, Om' — this is the invocation at the beginning of the midday <s>śastras</s> (recitations). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)

'To you, O [<s>Indra</s>], as if to a chariot for aid'; 'This, O <s>Vasu</s>, is the pressed, dark [soma]' — these are the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
'O <s>Indra</s>, come nearer!' — this is the <s>Indra-nihava</s> (invocation of <s>Indra</s>) <s>pragātha</s> (paired verse). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
'Now forth, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>' — this is the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> [verse]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)

Groups of three [verses] are the opening and following [verses]; groups of two are the <s>pragāthas</s> (paired verses). Everything up to the half-verse [is included]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
The <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse) are the opening and following [verses] and the <s>pragāthas</s>, everywhere. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
The metres [are recited] before the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> [section]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
And all [metres] up to the four-footed [ones]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
In the stanzas, one should lower [the voice] twice, at every two feet. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
Or by half-verses in the <s>Āśvina</s> [recitation]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
What has been recited foot by foot, that [goes] foot by foot. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
A compound [is formed] in the last foot. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
The other [is recited] foot by foot. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
The continuation [is made] with feet ending at the half-verse, by lowering [the voice]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
'<s>Agni</s> is the leader'; 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, by rites'; 'They swell the waters' — these are the <s>dhāyyās</s> (meditation verses). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
'Forth to you, O great <s>Indra</s>' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>pragātha</s> (paired verse). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
'The mightiest, fierce ones.' — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
Having recited one [verse] more, one should insert the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>nivid</s> (invocation formula), everywhere. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
Thus [it is done] at the midday [pressing] in odd [numbers]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
One [verse extra] in a group of three; halves in even [numbers]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
Having left one [verse], at the third pressing. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
Wiping the eyes, one should place [the fire] around [the altar], meditating upon it from the self. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)
Elsewhere also, when placing around, one should do thus. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)

'The <s>uktha</s> (praise) is in speech; for <s>Indra</s> who listens, you' — having recited, one should murmur. 'Those who indeed strengthened you for the contest, O <s>Maghavan</s>' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: marutvatīya śastra)

'We praise you, O hero'; 'You are the first to drink' — these are the <s>pragāthas</s> (paired verses), the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. If the <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman] is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
But if the <s>Bṛhat</s> [sāman is the pṛṣṭha]: 'You indeed we invoke'; 'Come, O eager one' — [these are the stotriya and anurūpa]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
These become <s>pragāthas</s> (paired verses). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
One should recite them two or three times. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)

In the <s>Bārhata</s> (pertaining to Bṛhat) <s>pragātha</s>, having repeated the fourth and sixth feet, one should lower [the voice] on the following [feet]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
If [recited in] <s>Bṛhatī</s> [metre] form, those same [feet are recited] twice. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
But the third and fifth [feet are recited] in the <s>Kakubh</s> [metre versions]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
The subsequent [verses begin] from the <s>pratyādāna</s> (reclaiming). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)

Thus on the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) days, the <s>Indra-nihava</s> (invocation of <s>Indra</s>) and <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> [verses follow the same pattern]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
The <s>Bṛhatī</s> [metre] form [is used] for the other <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s (back-chants). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
And for the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> when they are in a <s>tṛca</s> (group of three) position. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
And for the <s>hotraka</s> (assistant priest) [recitations] whose <s>pragāthas</s> are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
Everything else [is recited] as it was chanted. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
A single day [rite] has a fixed number of recitations. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
If it has both <s>sāmans</s> (chants), the <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse) belongs to the <s>yoni</s> (source) that is in the <s>Pavamāna</s> [chant]. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
One should recite it in the <s>yoni</s>-position (source-position) elsewhere. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
The <s>yoni</s>-position is above the <s>dhāyyā</s> (meditation verse). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
When there are multiple [anurūpas] not in succession, the invocation [is done] once or separately. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)
Thus above the <s>Indra-nihava</s>, for the <s>pragāthas</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)

'That which has been won' — this is the <s>dhāyyā</s> (meditation verse). 'Drink of the pressed, juicy [soma]' — this is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s> (chant paired verse). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)

body.text: indrasya.nu.vīryāṇi.ity.etasminn.aindrīm.nividam.dadhyāt./ (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya.śastra)(the most Important Hymn in the midday Offeriṅg. mylius.p.306.n.127.)
body.translated_text: 'Now [I shall proclaim] the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>' — in this [hymn] one should insert the <s>Aindrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Indra</s>) <s>nivid</s> (invocation formula). — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)

Or the accent [follows] according to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. 'The <s>uktha</s> (praise) is in speech; for <s>Indra</s> who listens nearby, you' — having recited, one should murmur. 'Drink the <s>soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; may it delight you' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: niṣkevalya śastra)

For the <s>hotraka</s> (assistant priest) [recitations]: 'By what wonderful [aid] has he come to us?'; 'By what aid of yours?'; 'Who shall [praise] that <s>Indra</s> to you, the wealthy?'; 'Immediately upon birth indeed, you, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'Willing, well-minded, come near to us' — [these are the] offering verses. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: hotraka śastras)

'By your aids, [we seek] the wealth-finder'; 'The rescuer indeed seeks to win' — these are the <s>pragāthas</s>, the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. 'His [fame] overflows'; 'More and more indeed'; 'Come now' — one should extract the most excellent [verse], everywhere. 'Drink, grow; your days [are] pressed' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: sutyā day: midday: hotraka śastras)
Now the third pressing [is performed] with the highest pitch. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āditya-graha etc.)
They proceed with the <s>Āditya</s> cup. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āditya-graha etc.)

'With the aid of the <s>Ādityas</s>, the recent'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to the <s>Ādityas</s>, the dear ones, of beloved abode'; 'May the <s>Ādityas</s> and <s>Aditi</s> delight.' One should not look at this cup while it is being offered. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āditya-graha etc.)

When the <s>Ārbhava Pavamāna</s> has been chanted, having separated the embers, [one performs] the animal rite from the beginning through to the end of the <s>iḍā</s> (sacrificial portion), and having done the animal rite, the [procedure] with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) beginning has been stated, up to the seating of the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [cup]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āditya-graha etc.)

When [the fires] have subsided, from the softest [portion] of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake), three balls each, to the south, from their respective cups to their own ancestors, they should offer: 'Here, O ancestors, delight yourselves; satisfy yourselves each according to your share.' — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āditya-graha etc.)
Having turned to the left and reached the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), all should eat the remnant of the oblation. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āditya-graha etc.)

'The god <s>Savitṛ</s> has become worthy of praise for us now'; 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the home-dweller'; 'The god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the most excellent, bestowing treasures on the noble fathers for their lifetime'; 'May [<s>Indra</s>] drink the <s>soma</s>; the offerings have delighted him; even the Rain-god delights in his ordinance' — when the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> has been uttered, the <s>hotṛ</s> should recite the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods) <s>śastra</s> (recitation). — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
One should meditate on all the directions before reciting. [But] not [on] that [direction] in which [one's] enemy [dwells]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, let us recite, Om' — this is the invocation at the beginning of the third-pressing <s>śastras</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)

'That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose'; 'The guileless god <s>Savitṛ</s>' — these are the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 'The god became [present]'; 'With one and with ten'; 'For the self-born one'; 'With two, for the offering, and with twenty'; 'With three you carry, and with thirty yoke-mates — O <s>Vāyu</s>, unyoke them here.' '<s>Pra dyāvā</s>' (Heaven and Earth, go forth) — this is the <s>Dairghatamasa</s> [hymn]. 'The beautiful-formed one, for aid'; 'They fashioned the chariot'; 'This <s>Vena</s> impels'; 'Of the mottled-wombed one'; 'For whom the mother sweetly yields milk'; 'Thus to the father, the All-god, the mighty'; 'May auspicious intentions come to us from everywhere' — these nine [constitute] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [section]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)

In the hymns of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and <s>Agni-Māruta</s> [sections], one should insert the <s>nivid</s> (invocation formula) beginning with the <s>Sāvitra</s> [verse]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
Four [nivids] in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [section]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
Three subsequent [nivids] in the subsequent [section]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
For the hymns have that deity [as their subject]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
[The nivid is inserted] within the hymn, [arranged] by deity. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra-graha etc.)
And the <s>dhāyyās</s> (meditative chants) here [are] in single-cup [form]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra graha etc.)

'<s>Aditi</s> is heaven, <s>Aditi</s> is the atmosphere' — one should encircle [the fire]. Everywhere in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (All-Gods rite), twice recited backward by half-verses, touching the earth once. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra graha etc.)

'The <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise) in speech, for <s>Indra</s>, for the gods; for your hearing' — having recited thus, one should murmur. 'May the <s>Viśvedevas</s> hear this invocation of mine' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: sāvitra graha etc.)
'You, O <s>Soma</s>, in accord with the ancestors' — this is the offering verse for the <s>Saumya</s> (soma-related offering). — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)
They surround that [offering] with ghee offering-verses, silently, on both sides. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)

'<s>Agni</s> whose oblation is ghee, whose back is ghee, established in ghee, whose abode is ghee — may the ghee-sprinkled tawny [horses] carry you; drinking ghee, you sacrifice, O god, to the gods' — this [is recited] in front. 'Wide, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, stride forth; make wide room for our dwelling. Drink ghee, O ghee-born one; extend far the lord of sacrifice' — this [is recited] above. If on one side [only]: 'O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, your beloved great abode' — silently. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)

Having brought the <s>Saumya</s> [cup], having first taken [a portion] for the <s>Udgātṛs</s> (chanters), one should look [at the soma]: 'That eye of yours [which is] in heaven, that [which is] in the eagle, by which you won sole sovereignty — indeed, the far-reaching eye of <s>Aditi</s>, the infinite — may <s>Soma</s>, the observer of men, place that in me.' — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)

'Not seeing, touching the heart, touching the mind, bestowing splendor — place splendor in us. Whatever mind of mine has gone to <s>Yama</s>, or whatever has gone far away — with King <s>Soma</s>, we hold that in ourselves. May we hear auspicious things with our ears, O gods.' — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)
With the thumb and ring finger, having anointed the eyes with ghee, one should give [the ghee-offering] to the <s>ājya-chandogas</s> (ghee-chanters). — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)

When the ladle-portions have been distributed, the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-tender) sacrifices the <s>Pātnīvata</s> (wives' cup) [offering]: 'With these [flames], O <s>Agni</s>, come hither on the same chariot' — silently. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)
Having followed the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> (leader) with the return-procession, having sat down in his lap, one should partake. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: saumya caru)
Then, as [the procedure] has been described. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)
The <s>Āgni-Māruta</s> (hymn to <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>) [is recited] with its own beginning. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)
Its first [section is recited] in backward verse-order — if it is to be recited in backward order. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)
The other [section is recited] by half-verses. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)
The continuous [recitation ends] with the last utterance. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)

'To <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, of broad brilliance; may he bring us good fortune'; 'Come forward, O skilful ones'; 'Of great might'; 'Sacrifice upon sacrifice for your <s>Agni</s>'; 'The god, the giver of wealth, for you' — these are the <s>pragāthas</s> (chant-pairs), the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse). — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)

'The mightier one, the more mighty one'; 'O waters, you are indeed' — three [verses]; they reach the <s>viyat</s> (open space) touching the waters. With those who have held on, with uncovered head — this beginning; response verse by verse. 'And may <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> hear us'; 'May the wives of the gods, the willing ones, help us' — two [verses]. 'O <s>Rākā</s>, I' — two [verses]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)

'<s>Pāvīravī</s>, the maiden, of wondrous life'; 'O <s>Yama</s>, sit upon this seat of sacred grass'; '<s>Mātali</s> with the sages'; '<s>Yama</s> with the <s>Aṅgirases</s>'; 'Let the lower ones rise up and the higher ones'; 'I have found the ancestors of good offering'; 'Homage be to the ancestors today'; 'Sweet indeed is this' — four [verses]. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)

And in the middle, the invocation: 'We rejoice in the divine; we delight in the divine' — in the response to these. 'By whose might the regions are supported, mightiest in valor, most powerful — who advance unconquered with force; <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> have come, invoked first.' — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)

'Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'; 'Weaving the thread, enter the luminous region of the atmosphere'; 'Thus indeed <s>Indra</s>, the bountiful, the generous one' — one should encircle [the fire], touching the earth. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)
With the last utterance, one should await the bringing down of the <s>Dhruva</s> (fixed cup). — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)

'The <s>uktha</s> in speech, for <s>Indra</s>, for the gods, for the one who has been heard' — having recited thus, one should murmur. 'O <s>Agni</s>, with the <s>Maruts</s>, the resplendent, the singers' — this is the offering verse. Thus ends the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. — (soma: sutyā day: evening: āgni-māruta śastra)
But in the <s>Ukthya</s> [sacrifice], for the <s>hotṛ</s>'s assistants: — (soma: ukthya)

'Come, let me speak to you'; '<s>Agni</s> of the <s>Bhāratas</s> was approached'; 'The cherished one of the peoples'; 'He supported what the <s>Asura</s> [made]' — two <s>tṛcas</s> (three-verse groups). '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, you two'; 'O kings, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'Of the sweetest' — these are the offering verses. — (soma: ukthya)

'We indeed, you, O ancient one'; 'He who for us, this, formerly' — these are the <s>pragāthas</s> (chant-pairs). All the <s>kakubh</s> (irregular meter) [verses]: 'For the most impelling one'; 'The streaming ones'; 'We resort to <s>Indra</s>'; 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you two'; '<s>Indra</s> and [the lord] of wealth' — these are the offering verses. — (soma: ukthya)

'Then indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, lover of praise'; 'They come, O <s>Indra</s>, lover of praise'; 'Resolve [is] the generator' (or: 'the season [is] the generator'); 'Now, O mortal, be [like] <s>Mitra</s>'; 'He [is] of that deed of yours'; '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lords of intoxication among intoxicating [drinks]' — these are the offering verses. — (soma: ukthya)
Thus ends the <s>Ukthya</s> [sacrifice]. — (soma: ukthya)
Now the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> (sixteenth cup). — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
'The <s>Soma</s> has been pressed, O <s>Indra</s>, for you' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse). — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
'May the tawny [horses] carry you hither' — three <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
'Come, hear these songs'; 'You of beautiful appearance, we [invoke]'; 'O bountiful one' — one and two <s>Paṅkti</s> [verses]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'When, O <s>Indra</s>, in the battle-contest'; 'This [soma] is yours, O beloved one' — an <s>Uṣṇih</s> and a <s>Bṛhatī</s> <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse group). 'Yoke for us' — in two-footed [verses]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'O <s>Brahman</s>, O hero, be pleased with the prayer-making' — a <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. 'This is the <s>Brahman</s> who [acts] seasonally'; '<s>Indra</s>, the famous by name, I praise'; 'As if along spreading paths'; '<s>Indra</s>, your hundreds go forth.' — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'To you, lord of might, the praises go, not restrained' — three two-footed [verses]. 'For your greatness I shall declare; I shall proclaim the two bay horses' — three <s>Jagatī</s> [verses]. 'At the three <s>Trikadrukas</s>, the bull [drinks] the barley-mixed [soma]'; 'Forth for him the fore-chariot' — two <s>tṛcas</s> in hypermetric [verses]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The first [section is recited] in backward verse-order, in two-part manner. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The latter [section is recited] in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>-<s>Gāyatrī</s> manner. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'Come forth, O conscious one; make conscious; drink; be intoxicated; O will-desiring one, the truth, the great; place blessing in us, O beneficent one' — an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. 'Forth, forth'; the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [hymn of] nourishment; 'Praise, praise forth'; 'Who has cleared the obstacles away' — these three <s>tṛcas</s> are in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meter]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
Having left the last [verse] of the final [section], one should insert the <s>nivid</s> (invocatory formula) at the end. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

We shall explain word by word, in order of the feet, by characteristic marks: 'Was intoxicated'; 'The serpent'; '<s>Vṛtra</s>'; 'Of the waters'; 'Impelling'; 'The noble one'; 'Rising'; 'In heaven'; 'The ocean'; 'The mountains'; 'Here.' — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'When [it rises] from the seat of the tawny one' — this is the encircling verse. 'Thus indeed, thus indeed <s>Indra</s>. Thus indeed, <s>Śakra</s> (the mighty one), command, O <s>Śakra</s>' — having murmured thus. 'The [soma] drinks of the previous, O possessor of bay horses, of the pressed ones' — thus one sacrifices. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'Of the distributed [soma]: O <s>Indra</s>, accept; carry forth; come, O hero, [with] the two bay horses here. Drink of the pressed [soma]; this thought — bow down — is beautiful for intoxication. O <s>Indra</s>, fill your belly as [one fills] something new, with honey, as [one fills something] from heaven.' — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'Of this pressed [soma], like gold; intoxications approach you; the well-spoken [praises] stood. <s>Indra</s> <s>Turāṣāh</s> (the victorious one), like <s>Mitra</s>, slew <s>Vṛtra</s>; like an ascetic, he split the fortress; like <s>Bhṛgu</s>, he conquered the enemies in the intoxication of <s>Soma</s>.' — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'Hear [our] call; not like <s>Indra</s>; accept the songs; not like a prize-winner. O <s>Indra</s>, with the yoke-fellows — bow to the missile — for intoxication, for the great battle. May the pressed [soma juices] enter the self, like a sage; O <s>Indra</s>, like <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.' — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'Fill the two flanks; not like <s>Soma</s>; strengthen, O hero, by thought. For he who [is] good for us; not greedy; not like <s>Ṛbhu</s>; like a master — the hero — not like a cup. Not like a traveler — the terrible one — like <s>Viṣṇu</s>; indeed fierce — together, not like one of good resolve' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
After the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>, one should distribute that same [section] for recitation. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
Having separated the feet, one should recite by half-verses. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The first feet of the earlier [verses]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The <s>Gāyatrīs</s> [are combined] with the <s>Paṅktis</s>. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
But of the <s>Paṅktis</s>, two each remain; with those, one should extend. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The <s>Uṣṇihs</s> [are combined] with the <s>Bṛhatīs</s>; but of the <s>Uṣṇihs</s>, the last feet should be made into two. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The first [foot has] four syllables. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
Having divided the two-footed [verses] into four, the first [combines] with <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the latter with <s>Jagatī</s> [verses]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The fourth syllable of the last [verse becomes] the final [syllable] of the preceding [line and] the first of the following. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
At the end of the third feet of the second and third [verses], one should insert [the extra syllable]. 'Pracetana' [goes] in the former [position]; 'Pracetaya' in the latter. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
In the latter [verses], having made the other feet into six [syllable groups], one should recite in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> manner. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
After the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>, from here onward [is] the distributed [section]. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
There, the response [is]: 'We exult in the divine intoxication; we delight in the divine' — then. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
One should introduce the offering verse with a murmur. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'Thus indeed; the [soma] drinks of the previous, O possessor of bay horses, of the pressed ones — thus indeed, <s>Indra</s>; and this pressing [is] yours alone. Thus indeed, O <s>Śakra</s> (mighty one), rejoice in the <s>soma</s>; drink the honey-sweet one, O <s>Indra</s>; command, O <s>Śakra</s>; pour [it] into the belly along with the rains.' — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The rest is the same. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The invocations [are]: for the <s>stotriya</s>, the <s>nivid</s> (formula), and the encircling verse. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
They partake of the offered <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> (sixteenth) cup with a collective invocation. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
And those who partake of the <s>gharma</s> (heated milk oblation). — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and the three <s>Chandogas</s> (chanters). — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

'O <s>Indra</s> of the sixteen[-fold], O powerful one; you are powerful among the gods — make me powerful, long-lived, and splendid among men. Of that [soma] of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, not yet drunk, invoked in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter, being invoked, I partake' — this is the partaking murmur. — (soma: ṣoḍaśin)

In the <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice), the <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds) have been stated. What has been recited along with the <s>hotṛ</s>'s [portion] also [applies] to the assistant priests' [portions]. — (soma: atirātra: paryāyas)

In the first <s>paryāya</s> (round), omitting the first [verse] of the <s>hotṛ</s>, in the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> for each verse, having recited the first feet twice, they descend. — (soma: atirātra: paryāyas)
Having combined the remainder, they extend [the recitation]. — (soma: atirātra: paryāyas)

All [priests], having taken up the middle [portions] from among all [hymns], chant with <s>praṇavas</s> (sacred syllables) at the ends of the <s>ṛcs</s> (verses). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
The final [portions are chanted] at the last [round]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
But the <s>Acchāvāka</s> [recites] four-syllabled ones. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
The <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds) have four <s>śastras</s> (recitations) each. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
The first [belongs] to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
The <s>paryāsas</s> (concluding hymns) [come] before the offering verses. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'Have drunk,' 'To you from the plant,' 'He drank indeed from the teat of the plant,' 'That constant one for you' — the remainder of the hymn. 'Bring this ram to <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Adhvaryus</s>; bring <s>soma</s> to <s>Indra</s>' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'Forth for <s>Indra</s>, the inebriating [drink]' — the standard ones. 'O seeker of the juice, to the one to whom [praise] is promised, boldly' — fifteen [verses]. 'From heaven indeed' — this is the <s>paryāsa</s> (concluding hymn). 'May he, with new [hymns]' — and. 'In his intoxication, knowing the many forms' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'We indeed you,' 'For that purpose,' 'We, O <s>Indra</s>, your [devotees],' 'For the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>' — one should remove the last. '<s>Indra</s> indeed [dispelled] the great fear,' 'Recite the speech,' 'Of the one shaken in waters, O lord of bay horses, drink here' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'For <s>Indra</s>, to drink, the pressed [soma],' 'The singers [praise] <s>Indra</s> indeed, greatly,' '<s>Indra</s>, the victorious one, come,' 'Now let us praise <s>Indra</s>, the lord,' 'Do not [abandon] us in this, O bountiful one,' 'O <s>Indra</s>, drink; pressed for you, for intoxication' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'This your, O <s>Indra</s>, <s>soma</s>,' 'This for you among the human folk,' 'Rise up indeed' — one should remove the last. 'I have become the protector of this plant; for intoxication' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'Come to us, O <s>Indra</s>, with nourishing [gifts],' 'Come running from afar,' 'For there is no other much-accomplishing one' — eight [verses]. 'The swinging ones,' 'I am the protector,' 'May <s>Indra</s> drink the pressed <s>soma</s>; may he be the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'O bull, at the pressing for you,' 'The leader of cows, with song,' in the hymn 'Come to us, O <s>Indra</s>, look this way' — 'The horse-rich one.' 'I send forth the true drink of the bull' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'This, O <s>Vasu</s>, is the pressed drink,' 'Come, O <s>Indra</s>, be delighted by the pressed [soma],' 'Come forth, O sovereign, approach,' 'Bring boldly,' 'That new [hymn] for him,' 'Drink of this; O <s>Indra</s>, of whom being born' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'This indeed with power,' 'Great <s>Indra</s> who with power,' 'To his wrath, the clans' — forty-two [verses]. 'For the all-conquering one, stand firm; the bay horses being yoked to the chariot' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'Come, sit down here,' 'Come, O conqueror,' 'None is higher than you, O <s>Indra</s>' — one should remove the last. 'I place faith in you,' 'This cup, O <s>Indra</s>, [is] for drinking' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'In every yoking, the strongest one,' 'They yoke the tawny, ruddy one,' 'Whatever, O <s>Indra</s>, I,' 'Forth to your great help,' 'O powerful one, by your heroic power' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)

'<s>Indra</s> among the pressed <s>soma</s> juices,' 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, who drink <s>soma</s> most,' 'Indeed those who kindle <s>Agni</s>' — seventeen [verses]. 'O <s>Indra</s>, in the cups,' '<s>Soma</s>, for you a hundred,' 'In the wooden vessel, the bay [horses], the ritual actions have come' — this is the offering verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
Thus [end] the <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
Except for the <s>paryāsa</s> (concluding hymn), [all are in] <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>paryāyas</s>)
When [the rounds] are concluded, they chant for the <s>Āśvina</s> (offering to the <s>Aśvins</s>). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

About to recite, having exited through the dismantled joining-passage, having bent the knee at the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), one should offer oblations: '<s>Agni</s> the impeller, by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter — may I attain him; may he protect me; to him, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
'<s>Uṣas</s> the impelling, by the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter — may I attain her; may she protect me; to her, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

'The <s>Aśvins</s>, the impelling, by the <s>Jagatī</s> meter — may I attain them; may they protect me; to them, <s>svāhā</s>.' [Then reciting] 'Great indeed are you, O <s>Sūrya</s>' — with two [verses], and '<s>Indra</s>, from all sides to you.' — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

Having consumed the remainder of the ghee and touching water, one should sip. It is known: 'This <s>hotṛ</s> is indeed the chariot of the gods; let me perform with those who are not weary.' — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

Having consumed [the remainder] and having crawled back, one should sit behind one's own <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-hearth), with legs and thighs drawn together, making a lap with the forearms and knees, like a bird about to fly up. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
But having made the lap, one should recite the <s>Āśvina</s> [<s>śastra</s>] (recitation for the <s>Aśvins</s>). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

'<s>Agni</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the householder, he is the king' — this is the opening verse, the one-footed <s>paccha</s> (response verse). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
With this one should continue the <s>Āgneya</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s>) <s>Gāyatrī</s> [portion]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

According to the rule of the morning <s>anuvāka</s> (litany), of that very collected tradition, one should recite at least a thousand [verses] from the <s>odetas</s> (collections). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

The <s>Bārhatī</s> (Bṛhatī-meter) ones — three <s>tṛcas</s> (sets of three) are the <s>stotriyas</s> (chant-verses), or <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns). One should recite them before [the rest], according to each deity, of one's own meter, as they were chanted. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
Or in whatever other [verses]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
The <s>pacchas</s> (response verses) are two-footed. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
One should continue with one-footed [verses]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
And those subsequent to them. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
One should remove [verses] of irregular meter. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
Or the recitation [may be done] according to that [standard] method. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
But [one should] not [use] other <s>Triṣṭubh</s> or <s>Jagatī</s> [verses] as <s>pacchas</s> (response verses). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
When [the sun] has risen, with the <s>Pāṅkta</s> (Paṅkti-meter [verses]), one commences the solar [hymns]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

'The sun for us from heaven,' 'Rise up, that <s>Jātavedas</s>' — nine [verses]. 'Wondrous among the gods,' 'Homage to <s>Mitra</s>,' '<s>Indra</s>, bring here the design.' 'O hero, we praise you,' 'Many are [your] sun-eyed [ones]' — these are the <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns). 'Great heaven and earth for us,' 'Those two, heaven and earth, all-beneficent.' 'Of all the divine creation,' 'By her may he not be seized by anger' — these are the two-footed [verses]. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, beyond what the noble one deserves' — this is the <s>paridhānīyā</s> (enclosing verse). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
The invocation [is]: 'To the opening verse, to the enclosing verse.' — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

If [the chant is in] the <s>Bṛhat Sāman</s>, [one should insert] its source [verse] as the second or third among the <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
Or not. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
They proceed with the <s>Āśvina graha</s> (cup for the <s>Aśvins</s>) together with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

'These <s>soma</s> juices, kept overnight, stand strong for drinking, for you two.' 'O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, come with the oblation-bearing chariot; come to adorn [the sacrifice]; drink!' — this is the invitatory verse. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

'May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer to the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>soma</s> [juices] kept overnight' — this is the <s>praiṣa</s> (direction). 'Forth for you, the intoxicating drinks have stood; drink, both <s>Aśvins</s>' — these are the offering verses, one-and-a-half, with the <s>anavāna</s> (concluding formula). — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)

If they should proceed with the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering for proper offering) of this <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake): '<s>Puroḍāśa</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, of the cooker,' 'O <s>Agni</s>, increasing,' 'The offered one' — these are the joint offering verses. — (soma: <s>Atirātra</s>: <s>saṃdhi stotra</s>: <s>āśvina śastra</s>)
If the <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds) should exceed [their allotted time], they should combine one from all [rounds]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)

From the first [round, the portion of] the <s>Hotṛ</s>; from the second, [that of] the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; from the last, [that of] the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
If [there are only] two, two from the first, two from the last. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
Or all [rounds] may be abbreviated in <s>stoma</s> (chant). — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
After the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse), they should recite the first and last <s>tṛcas</s> (sets of three). — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
The abbreviation [applies] to a single one [only]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
Except for the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s [portion] — thus some [say]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
For the <s>Āśvina</s> [recitation], the single <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) [is]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, [born] of <s>Vivasvat</s>, [and] the dawns.' — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
One should recite that before [the rest], according to each deity, of one's own meter, as it was chanted. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
Three hundred and sixty [is the count for] the <s>Āśvina</s> [recitation]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
When [there is] a simultaneous occurrence of pressings and impellings of those having different opinions, when not separated by a river or mountain. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
Some [say] even when separated. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
That being the case, [there should be] haste from the invocation of the deities. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
'By what splendor' — and [this verse] one should recite before the hymn in the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
'He who, just born' — in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [recitation]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
'O <s>Agni</s>, my splendor' — [this is recited before] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods) hymn. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
Or one may insert the <s>nivids</s> (laudatory formulas) into these very [hymns] and remove the others. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)

If one should skip the [proper] place for the <s>nivid</s> (laudatory formula): 'Let us not go astray' — having recited the hymn before [the missed place], one should insert [the <s>nivid</s>] in another [hymn] of the same deity. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
When there is excess <s>soma</s>, additional <s>stotras</s> (chants) and <s>śastras</s> (recitations) [are produced]. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)

At the morning pressing, 'There is <s>soma</s> here,' 'This is pressed,' 'The cow suckles the <s>Maruts</s>' — [these are] the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse). 'Great is <s>Indra</s> who with power,' 'May the gods help us from there' — with <s>Aindra</s> (verses to <s>Indra</s>) and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> (verses to <s>Viṣṇu</s>) [verses], having recited the <s>stoma</s> (chant) additionally, one should sacrifice with an <s>Aindrī</s> (verse to <s>Indra</s>). — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
Or with a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> (verse to <s>Viṣṇu</s>). — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
'<s>Aindrā</s> and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>' — [says] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>, because the deity is principal. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
'I yoke you together with ritual action, with offering.' — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)

At the midday [pressing]: 'Great indeed are you, O <s>Sūrya</s>,' 'Rise up, that visible form' — these <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns) [are] the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. 'Great <s>Indra</s>, [renowned] among men,' 'Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed,' 'The one which [is] the begetter of all thoughts' — these are the offering verses. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)
At the third pressing, they should proceed to successively higher concluding rites, up to the <s>Atirātra</s>. — (soma: <s>soma prāyaścitta</s>)

If [the deviation is] from an <s>atirātra</s> (overnight soma sacrifice): 'That famous name of yours, O <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>'; 'That of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by your heroic power' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse). The remainder [follows] the midday [pressing procedure].
'The fierce one, thus the battle of the mighty ones' — or this [is] the offering verse.
When the purchased king [<s>Soma</s>] is lost or burnt —
The lids, the <s>sadas</s> (sitting hall), the oblation hall, and the <s>dhānā</s> (grain store) should be made uncovered.
Or covered.
They should press another king [<s>Soma</s>].
When [Soma] is unobtainable, [they should use] <s>pūtīka</s> (putika grass) or <s>phālguna</s> (Arjuna tree products).
Or other plants together with <s>pūtīka</s>.
Or, having offered an expiatory [oblation], one should undertake the subsequent [rite].
One should consider the pressing day as if [it were performed with] the [proper] hymn.
Aftermilk [is used as a substitute] at the morning pressing.
Cooked [milk is used] at the midday [pressing].
Curd [is used] at the third pressing.
The <s>Śrāyantīya</s> [is used as] the <s>brahmasāman</s> (Brahmā's chant). If <s>phālguna</s> [products are used], the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [is used] in place of the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [sāman].
Having completed the sacrifice with a single <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee), having concluded the ceremonies, one should sacrifice again.
At that [second sacrifice], one should give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> of the former [sacrifice].
When <s>Soma</s> is obtained, [one proceeds] according to the standard procedure.

When the consecrated ones suffer from illness: when [the rite is] enclosed, [or] when the morning litany has not been performed — 'O lord of nourishment, give nourishment; give sight to [my] eye, breath to [my] breath, self to [my] self, speech to [my] speech; give these back to him, <s>svāhā</s>' — having offered a <s>brahma-āhuti</s> (Brahmā's oblation), having mixed together cold and warm waters, twenty-one [portions], having placed barley grains and <s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass) tufts in them, one should perform the water-rite with those waters.

One should bathe him with those [waters, reciting]: 'You who are the restorers of the living — revive this one. You who are the restorers of livelihood — revive this one. You who are the restorers of the living together — completely revive this one. You who are the restorers of shared livelihood — completely revive this one' — and with the plant hymn.
Having bathed [him], one should wipe [him] dry.

'The <s>Upāṃśu</s> (murmured libation) and <s>Antaryāma</s> (inner-restraining libation) — may they protect your <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (outbreath). May the <s>Upāṃśu</s> pressing protect your <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath). May the <s>Aindra-Vāyava</s> [cup] protect your speech. May the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [cup] protect your two eyes. May the <s>Āśvina</s> [cup] protect your hearing. May the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> [cup] protect your skill and purpose. May the <s>Uktha</s> [cup] protect your limbs. May the <s>Dhruva</s> (firm cup) protect your life-span.'
The circumambulation [should be performed] according to the seating arrangement.
'<s>Indra</s> the protector, <s>Indra</s> the helper' — beginning with [the verse to] <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
Even if from [a sacrifice] other than a one-day [rite], one should place the <s>nivid</s> (laudatory insertion) for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods offering) in the <s>Svasti-Ātreya</s> [recitation].
[One proceeds] according to the standard procedure when [the person is] free from disease.
When [the sacrifice] is concluded, having carried [the deceased] out through the proper passage, they perform the adornments at the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath).
They shave the hair, beard, body-hair, and nails.
They anoint [him] with <s>nalada</s> (spikenard).
They put on a garland of <s>nalada</s> (spikenard).
Some, having emptied [the vessel], fill [it] with speckled ghee.
Having cut a foot-length from the edge of an unworn garment, they cover [the deceased], with the visible fringe turned westward.
His sons should make the cutting at home.
Having placed his fires upon [the pyre], they should burn [him] outside the <s>vedi</s> (altar) on the south side.
For one who has not established the [sacred] fires, with a brought fire.
And [they should burn] the wife [as well].
Having returned, they should complete the day['s rites].
In the morning, the recitations, utterances, chants, and responsories [should be performed] without repetition and without the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s> (exclamation).
Before the drawing of the <s>grahas</s> (cups), having gone out through the proper passage, circumambulating the altar three times to the left, they sit down around [it].
The <s>hotṛ</s> [sits] behind.
The <s>adhvaryu</s> [sits] to the north. Behind him, the <s>chandogas</s> (Sāmaveda chanters).
'This dappled cow has stepped forth' — they chant in a low voice.
When the chant is complete, the <s>hotṛ</s>, circumambulating the altar to the left, should follow [reciting] the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) without the <s>praṇava</s>.
And the <s>yāmī</s> (road-going) [verses].

'Go forth, go forth, by the former paths' — from five [verses] one should extract the third. 'Do not burn him, O <s>Agni</s>; do not scorch [him]' — six [verses]. '<s>Pūṣan</s>, may he impel you from here, the knowing one' — four [verses]. 'Approach mother earth' — four [verses]. '[These are] from <s>Soma</s> for the individual [deceased].'

'<s>Urūṇasā</s>, the life-satisfying ones, the fig-tree-like ones' — and having completed [the recitation], having collected [the bones], having proceeded through the proper passage, they should take their seats as before.

During the partaking, having partaken of the <s>prāṇa-bhakṣas</s> (breath-partakings), they should lead [the remains] to the southern <s>mārjālīya</s> (cleansing-shed), or to the southern haunch of the <s>vedi</s> (altar).

It becomes a seventeenth day; the <s>pavamānas</s> (purifying chants) are <s>trivṛt</s> (threefold); the <s>pṛtha</s> (extension) uses the <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman]; [it is] an <s>agniṣṭoma</s> (soma sacrifice).
Some, at the conclusion, have the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) performed on this [seventeenth] day, calling it the day of this [deceased person].
Or, having burnt [the deceased] with a churned fire and having buried [the remains], after a year they should have him sacrificed with an <s>agniṣṭoma</s>.
Or they should consecrate the nearest relative.
Or [there is] a rising [ceremony] for the householder.
The modification of chants and recitations has been stated.
In one-day [sacrifices], [the substitute] should sleep in the sacrificer's seat.
When [the sacrifice] is concluded, as [the wives] depart, they should have the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) performed — so [says] <s>Ālekhana</s>.
They should burn [the deceased] to the east of the <s>sadas</s> (sitting hall) — so [says] <s>Āśmarathya</s>.
This alone is the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) [for the deceased].
<s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Atyagniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Uktha</s>, <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, <s>Vājapeya</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Aptoryāma</s> — these are the concluding forms (<s>saṃsthās</s>).
Whichever [form] they approach, the <s>yajña-puccha</s> (sacrifice's tail) [follows] at the end of that.
The <s>anuyāja</s> (after-offering) and so forth, as stated, [follow] from the animal [offering's] <s>śamyuvāka</s> (yoke-pin formula) onward.
But here, the last [formula] is the <s>sūktavāka-praiṣa</s> (hymn-utterance directive).
'He has been strengthened' — [one addresses] the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) deity.
If some should make a <s>paśu-puroḍāśa</s> (animal-cake offering) of the <s>savanīya</s> (pressing-day) animal, one should say 'They have been strengthened by the <s>puroḍāśas</s>.'
By the <s>savanīya</s> [offerings] alone, <s>Indra</s> is strengthened; by the <s>paśu-puroḍāśa</s> (animal-cake), the animal deity [is strengthened].
After the <s>śamyuvāka</s> (yoke-pin formula) [comes] the <s>Hāriyojana</s> (yoking of the bay horses).

'Go home having drunk <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>.' 'The <s>dhānā</s> (grain) of the <s>Soma</s> [offerings].' 'From <s>Indra</s>, both drink.' 'I yoke for you with sacred words the hairy bay horses.'
These [are] the invitatory verses on the last days.
'Stay here, O bountiful one, do not go away; this sacrifice [is] for the gods, this [is] the offering' — on the other [days].
'Go away, O bountiful one, and come [back]' — or this [is] the invitatory verse on the later days.

When the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response exclamation) has not been made, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> gives the <s>atipraiṣa</s> (supplementary directive): 'Here, in this very ecstasy, O bountiful <s>Indra</s>, your horses.'
'Today' — at the <s>atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice).
'Today at the pressing' — and [this formula].

Having heard its conclusion, the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-tender) announces: 'Tomorrow [is] the pressing day. For the pressing day of these <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s — that I announce to <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, to <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>, to the <s>Vasus</s>, to the <s>Rudras</s>, to the <s>Ādityas</s>, to all the gods, to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, to the <s>Soma</s>-drinkers, to the <s>Soma</s>-pressers. O <s>Brahmā</s>, grant speech.'
Having received the <s>droṇa-kalaśa</s> (large soma vessel) brought by the <s>unnetṛ</s>, like an <s>iḷā</s>, having performed the invocation, one should look [at the soma].

'Of the bay-horse-possessing <s>Hāriyojana</s>, of the praised chant, the recited utterance, the offered <s>yajus</s>-formula — that share which [brings] cattle-winning and horse-winning — of that, I, being invited, partake as an invited one' — having partaken of the <s>prāṇa-bhakṣa</s> (breath-partaking).

Having given back the <s>droṇa-kalaśa</s> (large soma vessel), having nourished oneself, having crept out as they had crept in, at the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth) they offer the oblations [for] those who have crept out: 'May this drunk <s>Soma</s> juice gladden <s>Indra</s>'; 'This inspired sage, restraining the verse-song of speech.'

'May this [Soma], in the encounter with any assailant — may king <s>Soma</s>, like a friend, ward off [harm], <s>svāhā</s>.' 'This wealth, given by <s>Agni</s>, has come — glory, splendor, together with vigor, energy, and strength.'
'For long life, for a hundred autumns, I accept [this]; for great heroic power, <s>svāhā</s>.'

On the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), they place six sticks each [reciting]: 'You are the expiation of sin committed by the gods, <s>svāhā</s>. You are the expiation of sin committed by the ancestors, <s>svāhā</s>.'

'You are the expiation of sin committed by humans, <s>svāhā</s>. You are the expiation of sin committed by us, <s>svāhā</s>. You are the expiation of sin upon sin, <s>svāhā</s>. Whatever heavy [sin] we have committed against you, O gods, with the tongue.'

Having taken <s>dhānā</s> (parched grain) from the <s>droṇa-kalaśa</s>, they should look [at them, reciting]: 'You are being filled; fill me with offspring and with wealth. You are the wish-fulfilling [cows] of <s>Indra</s>; yield my desires — offspring, cattle.'
Having smelled [them], they should scatter [them] in the area within the enclosing sticks.
Having returned to the place of the passage, [with] cups full of water — those they go around to the left.
Having wiped [themselves] with green grass, each from their own cups, three times to the left, they sprinkle themselves with water using the right hands.
Or with the other [hands], to the right.
'<s>Svadhā</s> (self-offering) to the father; <s>svadhā</s> to the grandfather; <s>svadhā</s> to the great-grandfather.'
The [formula for] the living and the dead has been stated.

Having placed the hands in the cups, [reciting]: 'O divine <s>Soma</s>, of the washed one, of that which is known by the wise, pressed by men, praised with <s>stomas</s> (chants), recited with <s>ukthas</s> (praises), offered with <s>yajus</s> (sacrificial formulas) — whatever portion [of yours] wins cattle and wins horses, of that invited [portion], being invited, I partake' — having partaken of the <s>prāṇabhakṣas</s> (life-breath partakings). — (soma: yajña-puccha)
'May I not lose my offspring' — these [mantras] one should not direct toward oneself. 'May this praise reach you, O <s>Maruts</s>' — with this [verse] they sprinkle. — (soma: yajña-puccha)

'I have made [a praise] of <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>' — at the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth), having tasted the drops of curd, they dissolve their friendships [saying]: 'Both wise ones, young, truthful, lords of the law, by the law of truth we dissolve [our] friendships.' — (soma: yajña-puccha)
Having performed the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> (offerings with the wives), they proceed to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath). — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
While proceeding, they join in the final cadence (<s>nidhana</s>) of the <s>sāman</s> (chant). — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
Standing, they perform [the rite] with the <s>avabhṛtha</s> sprinkling. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)

[The rite has] fore-offerings (<s>prayājas</s>) at the beginning and after-offerings (<s>anuyājas</s>) at the end. In this [rite], there is no <s>iḍā</s> (refreshment portion); the <s>prayāja</s> and <s>anuyāja</s> accompanied by <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) are accompanied by water. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
[They are in] <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter]. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
The oblation is for <s>Varuṇa</s>. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)

'May your anger be averted, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, by [our] homage' — two [verses]. <s>Agni</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> [is the deity] for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to the fire). — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)

'You, O <s>Agni</s>, knowing <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [ways]' — two [verses]. When [the rite] is concluded, they should place their feet at the water's edge [saying]: 'Homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>; I am submissive to <s>Varuṇa</s>'s command.' — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)

Then they sip [water saying]: 'You are the cleansing bath of the partaking; you are the cleansing bath of what has been partaken; you are the cleansing bath of what has been done.' — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
Snorting with the first [formula], they spit out; they pour out [water from the mouth] with the latter two. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
Then, having sipped [water], they bathe [saying]: 'O waters, you mothers, purify us'; 'Carry forth this, O waters'; 'May the waters and herbs be friendly to us.' — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
By this same procedure, even the unconsecrated ones should sprinkle themselves. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
The <s>unnetṛ</s> (scooper priest) raises them out [of the water]. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
'Up from darkness we have risen' — [reciting this], having come out. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
From this point onward, [the procedure is] the same with the <s>hṛdayaśūla</s> (heart-spit [offering]), up to the concluding murmured [formula]. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
All those whose ritual duties have been completed stand attending [the fires] with the concluding murmured [formula]. — (soma: yajña-puccha: avabhṛtha)
They perform the <s>udayanīya</s> (concluding offering) at the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire). — (soma: yajña-puccha: udayanīya iṣṭi)
That has been described [as being like] the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening offering). — (soma: yajña-puccha: udayanīya iṣṭi)
<s>Pathyā Svasti</s> (auspicious path) is here the foremost of the ghee oblations. — (soma: yajña-puccha: udayanīya iṣṭi)
And the offering verses (<s>yājyās</s>) and invitatory verses (<s>anuvākyās</s>) are reversed. — (soma: yajña-puccha: udayanīya iṣṭi)
Those very [priests] who [performed] the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> should perform [this]. — (soma: yajña-puccha: udayanīya iṣṭi)
The concluding offering (<s>saṃyājya</s>) [follows] the original model (<s>prakṛti</s>). — (soma: yajña-puccha: udayanīya iṣṭi)
When [the rite] is concluded, [there is] the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> <s>anūbandhyā</s> (after-bound [cow] for <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>). — (soma: yajña-puccha)
Some [say] in the <s>sadas</s> (assembly-shed). — (soma: yajña-puccha)
Some [say] on the northern <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (soma: yajña-puccha)

When the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) has been offered, if [the sacrifice falls] on the eleventh [day], having placed [the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal] in front, having proceeded with the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> procedure and having gone [to the <s>gārhapatya</s>], they perform the rite at the <s>gārhapatya</s> with an animal for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. — (soma: yajña-puccha)
Beginning from the anointing, having carried [the fire] around, they release [the fires] for non-return. — (soma: yajña-puccha)
But if the <s>adhvaryus</s> complete [the rite] with ghee, the <s>hotṛ</s> should do likewise. — (soma: yajña-puccha)
[He should give] the instructions as if [they were] joint-directions (<s>sampraiṣas</s>). — (soma: yajña-puccha)
The animal [related] formulaic passages (<s>nipātas</s>). — (soma: yajña-puccha)

If at the <s>anūbandhyā</s> (after-bound offering) one should prepare subsidiary oblations with the <s>paśu-puroḍāśa</s> (animal-cake): <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Anumati</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, <s>Sinīvālī</s>, <s>Kuhū</s> [are the deities]. — (soma: yajña-puccha)

'May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give to the giver an imperishable, forward-reaching livelihood. May we attain the good will of the god, the prize-possessor. <s>Dhātṛ</s> rules over offspring and wealth; <s>Dhātṛ</s> brought forth this entire world. <s>Dhātṛ</s> watches over the field without blinking; offer the oblation to <s>Dhātṛ</s>, rich with ghee.' — (soma: yajña-puccha)
If [the oblations are] for the goddesses: <s>Sūryā</s>, <s>Dyaus</s> (Sky), <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), <s>Gau</s> (Cow), <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth). — (soma: yajña-puccha)

'Come, O <s>Purandhi</s> (the bountiful one)' — two [verses]. 'With your rays you extend the first [light]'; 'Bringing nourishing and excellent [things]; not the swift chariot of Dust-destroyer reaches them; nor do they eat [those gifts]; the thief does not seize them; indeed, strong even [as] the mountains, [firm as] the trees.' — (soma: yajña-puccha)
When no animal is available, [one offers] a milk offering as the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī anūbandhyā</s> in its place. — (soma: yajña-puccha)
From the ghee-portion onward up to the <s>vājin</s> (swift offering). — (soma: yajña-puccha)
The ritual performers should partake of the <s>vājin</s> (swift offering). — (soma: yajña-puccha)
But all the consecrated ones (<s>dīkṣitas</s>) [partake]. — (soma: yajña-puccha)

All the consecrated ones who have arisen [from the consecration], having separately set up the fires, having churned [fresh fire] from the northern god-worship [altar], sacrifice with the <s>udavasānīya</s> (concluding) offering. — (soma: yajña-puccha)
The <s>paunarādheyikī</s> (re-establishment offering) [is performed] unmodified, unmodified. — (soma: yajña-puccha)
Of <s>sattras</s> (communal sessions): — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
The consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and <s>upasads</s> (approach offerings) have been described. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
The pressing-days (<s>sutyā</s>) [follow] this [same] day's [pattern]. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
