From the morning litany (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>) at the beginning to the concluding [rite] (<s>udavasānīya</s>) at the end — [these are] the final [day's elements]. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
The others [end] with the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> (offerings with the wives). — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
But the drop-tasting (<s>drapsa-prāśana</s>) and the friendship-dissolution (<s>sakhya-visarjana</s>) [belong] to the very last [day]. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
The fixed elements are the frameworks (<s>ātānas</s>) of the recitations. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
In <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) rites, hymns [are placed] indeed in the hymn-positions. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
The arrangement [is determined] by the deity. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
<s>Tṛcas</s> (verse-triads) [are used] in the <s>prauga</s> (opening recitation). — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
In all day-groups, the <s>abhyāsa</s> (repetition) and <s>atipraiṣa</s> (extended direction) proceed from the first day for those that are being drawn out. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
At the last recitation of the [final] day, having recited the last four-syllable word of the enclosing verse (<s>paridhānīyā</s>) twice, one should recite [it]. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
From the second [day] onward, 'That swift one, divinely impelled' — the <s>Tārkṣya</s> [hymn is recited] at the beginning of the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> hymns. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
'For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press the <s>soma</s>' — [this is recited] in the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> (Agni-Marut) [section], among the <s>Jātavedas</s> hymns. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)

The opening [hymns] up to the concluding cycle (<s>paryāsa</s>), the <s>kadvat</s> (containing 'kad') [hymns] to be recited day after day — the <s>hotrakas</s> (assistant priests) [recite these] from the second [day] onward only. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
All of those [are recited] everywhere, except on the last day. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
[They are] optional in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [form] when situated in the middle of the day-group. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
Or in <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>ayanas</s> (year-long rites). — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)

The others [are determined] by <s>abhyāsa</s> (repetition) and <s>atipraiṣa</s> (extended direction) — [according to] <s>Kautsa</s>, because in a modified [rite] they take on the nature of that [modification]. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)

[They are] fixed for the <s>hotṛ</s> — [according to] <s>Gautama</s>, because of their continuity from the beginning of the aggregate, and because of [their] being called 'unfallen.' — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
Also for the <s>hotrakas</s> (assistant priests) — [according to] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>, because of the fixed nature of the <s>sattra</s> (session) law's application. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)

In the cases of <s>pragātha</s> (chant-pair), <s>tṛca</s> (verse-triad), and hymn additions, one should extract [enough from] the single-day [material] to fill [the requirement]. — (soma: ahīna-satra: general)
On the <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth [day]), the <s>hotṛ</s> [recites]: 'He was born' — this is the <s>ājya</s> (ghee hymn). — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

'Come to us, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'We invoke <s>Mitra</s>'; 'I invoke <s>Mitra</s> of purified wisdom'; 'This is for you, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'Abundantly indeed'; 'Attend to [us], O sun, at your rising' — these are the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> (six-day) <s>stotriyas</s> (praise-verses) of the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s>. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras) (second ājya-śastra)

'Come, O [<s>Indra</s>] of beautiful songs, for you indeed'; '<s>Indra</s> [the one] with songs, great'; 'With <s>Indra</s> indeed you wish to see'; 'From his own power, one [verse]' and two [more]; '<s>Indra</s> from <s>Dadhīci</s>'s bones'; 'Rising with might'; 'Destroy all [our] enemies' — [these are] of the <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

'O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, come to the pressed [<s>soma</s>]'; 'To <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, great homage'; 'I invoke the two, of whom this'; 'By your thought'; 'O <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, these [offerings of] yours'; 'For you are indeed the priests of the sacrifice' — [these are] of the <s>acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
Of those, whichever [<s>sāman</s>] they chant on [a given day] — that is the <s>stotriya</s> (praise-verse). — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
Whichever [they will chant] on the next [day] — that is the <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse). — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

On days with a single <s>stotriya</s>, whichever other [verse] immediately follows — that is the <s>anurūpa</s>; [this applies] unless the entire day-group is a <s>ṣaḍaha</s> (six-day cycle). — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
The single-day [rule applies] when that condition obtains. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
And on the last [day]. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

Above the <s>anurūpas</s> (corresponding verses): '<s>Varuṇa</s> has led us on the right path'; 'We [invoke] <s>Indra</s> from all sides'; 'Whatever <s>soma</s> is pressed by men' — these are the opening [hymns]. Having recited, one should insert the remaining [verses], one by one, on the <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth), <s>mahāvrata</s>, <s>abhijit</s>, <s>viśvajit</s>, and <s>viṣuvat</s> days. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
And on all <s>stomas</s> (praise-forms) and all <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants). — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

Above the insertions: 'Attend to [us], O sun, at your rising'; 'It crossed the atmosphere'; 'Like a horse' — these <s>tṛcas</s> (verse-triads) are the concluding cycles (<s>paryāsas</s>). — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
That very [verse] is the last <s>ṣaḍaha</s> <s>stotriya</s> of the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s>, with its concluding cycle. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
One should substitute another [verse] of the same deity in the place of the former. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)
Elsewhere too, when by coincidence a <s>tṛca</s> or hymn would [appear] without interruption, at a single sitting one should recite [it] twice. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

If one should recite the <s>Mahābālabhid</s> [hymn], above the <s>anurūpas</s> or above the opening [hymns], one should insert the <s>Nābhāka</s> <s>tṛcas</s> in <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter]. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

'The companion, the embracer' — [this is] of the <s>maitrāvaruṇa</s>. 'You who hold the <s>Kakubh</s> [meter]' or 'The many first-praised [offerings], O <s>Indra</s>, as stimulants' — [this is] of the <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. 'For you indeed are the best of offerings' — [this is] of the <s>acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: ṣaḍaha: hotraka śastras)

In the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]: 'Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth'; 'Rise up, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>' — these two <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> (Brahmaṇaspati) [verses] are inserted before the fixed [portion]. — (soma: caturviṃśa day)
'Sing the great [chant] for <s>Indra</s>'; 'None [equals] the chariot of <s>Sudās</s>' — these are the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [verses] above the fixed [portion]. — (soma: caturviṃśa day)
'With what beauty' — and this should be recited in the <s>Marutvatīya</s> before the hymn. — (soma: caturviṃśa day)
One each of the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> [verses]. — (soma: caturviṃśa day)
Thus for the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitations]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
The <s>Indra-nihava</s> (invocation of <s>Indra</s>) is fixed. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
And the <s>dhāyyās</s> (meditation verses). — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
The <s>Bṛhat</s> [sāman is] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant). — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
Or the <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
When one of those two is not being performed, one should recite its <s>yoni</s> (source verse). — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
Of the <s>Vairūpa</s>, <s>Vairāja</s>, <s>Śākvara</s>, and <s>Raivata</s> [sāmans]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
The <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) <s>stotriyas</s> (chant-verses) [serve as] the source [verses]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
[They are recited as] half-verses. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
Their arrangement [changes] day by day. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
Above those, the <s>sāma-gāthās</s> (chant-verses). — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
That of the <s>Rathantara</s> has been stated. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
'May he hear both' — [this is the sāma-gāthā] of the <s>Bṛhat</s>. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)

'O <s>Indra</s>, the threefold refuge'; 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, at the onslaughts'; 'Let not the praisers, and us' — one should close with a six-footed [verse], combining two-footed [verses]. '<s>Indra</s> indeed for the worship of gods' — for the others. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
The <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) [hymns are recited] one each, day by day. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
'That indeed was' — and this one should recite before the hymn. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)

They partake of the <s>uktha</s> (praise) cup and the <s>camasas</s> (goblets) and, in between, the <s>atigrāhya</s> (supplementary cups), during the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [recitation]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
The silent recitation at partaking is constant. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
The partakers [use] a sixteen-[fold] vessel. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day)
Of the <s>hotraka</s> (assistant priest) [recitations]: — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: Hotrakās)

'By what wonderful [aid] has he come to us?'; 'By what aid of yours?'; 'Let none other speak'; 'Whatever these people [offer] to you' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse) of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: Hotrakās)

'That destructive one of yours, the death-conquering'; 'That heroic [deed] of yours I seek'; 'The abundantly giving, well-heard, abundantly giving one'; 'We, the pressers, invoke you'; 'Who indeed knows him at the pressing?'; 'The one who overcomes all armies'; 'That man, <s>Indra</s>, I repeatedly call'; 'O <s>Indra</s>, bring those [blessings]' — one and two [verses each]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

'<s>Indra</s> has grown for intoxication'; 'In every intoxication indeed you give to us'; 'The beautiful-formed one for aid'; 'The most impetuous one for our aid'; 'Like those facing the sun'; 'Great indeed are you, O <s>Sūrya</s>'; 'Rise up, that visible form'; 'Rise up, those most honey-sweet ones'; 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, at the onslaughts'; 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, are glorious'; 'O <s>Indra</s>, bring the design'; 'O <s>Indra</s>, bring the foremost'; 'To you a thousand, a hundred'; 'O hero, at the rising of the sun' — [these are] for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

'By your aids, [we seek] the wealth-finder'; 'The rescuer indeed seeks to win'; 'You indeed, today, O men, we [invoke]'; 'This one indeed today'; 'He who is the king of peoples'; 'He who is the all-destroying, all-seeing'; 'Of the sweet, thus varied'; 'Thus indeed, O <s>Soma</s>, in intoxication'; 'Both indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, the two worlds'; 'Even when you, O hundred-powered'; 'None has attained him by deed'; 'Not the great mountains, you'; 'May he hear both, and us'; 'Rain upon [us], O much-praised'; 'You are never barren'; 'You never withhold'; 'From whatever, O <s>Indra</s>, we fear'; 'As a wild ox set apart'; 'Whatever, O <s>Indra</s>, east or north'; 'As a wild ox set apart' — [these are] for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

Of the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse) — if they should chant upon the <s>anurūpa</s>, the <s>stotriya</s> becomes the <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

Above the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>: 'Who shall [praise] that <s>Indra</s> to you, the wealthy?'; 'Who new, from the linseeds?'; 'What indeed remains undone by him?' — these are the <s>kad</s>-beginning <s>pragāthas</s> (paired verses). — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

'Drive away, O <s>Indra</s>, all enemies eastward'; 'With prayer I yoke you, with prayer-yoked [ones]'; 'You, the knowing one, lead us to a wide space' — these are the opening [verses, to be recited] after the <s>kad</s>-verses. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

Above the opening [verses], 'Immediately upon birth' — [this is] to be recited day by day. The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [recites]: 'For him indeed, for the praise'; 'The messenger, ruling [over]' — these two [are] the <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day rite) hymns. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

'May the true one come here' — this is the second <s>ahīna</s> hymn of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. 'Rise up, the prayers [surround] you' or [an alternative] — these others [are] in the daily recitation. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)
'Now indeed' — this is the last and final [verse]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)
The <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) hymns [serve as] the <s>stotriya</s>s (chant-verses) for the six-day [rite] at the insertions. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)

'Rise up, that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, golden' — three [verses]. 'For you, O Heaven and Earth'; 'Of the sacrifice, the chariot' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods) [section]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)
'Of <s>Pṛkṣa</s>, the mighty'; 'For the mighty troop'; 'By sacrifice may you grow' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> (Agni-Marut) [section]. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)
This day [has the form of] an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)
Or an <s>Ukthya</s>. — (soma: Caturviṃśa day: afternoon: hotrakās)
The <s>Abhiplava</s> and <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [six-day periods follow]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
The <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman serves as] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) on the odd [days]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
The <s>Bṛhat</s> [sāman serves as] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> on the others. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
Beginning from the third [day], the second [sāmans] of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycle] day by day [are]: <s>Vairūpa</s>, <s>Vairāja</s>, <s>Śākvara</s>, and <s>Raivata</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
When they are being performed in their proper places, one should recite the source [verses]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
And everywhere when there is no source of its own, except in the <s>Āśvina</s> [recitation]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

But for the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [sāman], even when not being performed, one should recite the source [verse] together with the <s>anurūpa</s> and the invocation, above the <s>anurūpa</s> of the other. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
The <s>hotraka</s> (assistant priest) [recitations use] the remaining insertions, having extracted [them]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

'We invoke <s>Mitra</s>'; 'I invoke <s>Mitra</s> of purified wisdom'; 'This of yours, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'O our <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — these are the <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three). — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

'Forth for <s>Mitra</s>' — of the four, one should extract the second. 'Forth for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — six [verses]. 'By the poets, O inviolable one' — three [verses]. 'Of <s>Mitra</s>, the people-sustaining' — four [verses]. These are the <s>Maitrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Mitra</s>) [hymns]. 'Whatever, O you of the clan' — this is the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (pertaining to <s>Varuṇa</s>) [section]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest] should insert a <s>tṛca</s> (group of three) of this, more than the constant [amount], for the purpose of the <s>stoma</s> (chant). — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

Five [tṛcas] in the seventeen-fold [stoma]; nine in the twenty-one-fold; twelve in the twenty-four-fold; fifteen in the thirty-three-fold; twenty-one in the thirty-three-fold; thirty-two in the forty-four-fold; thirty-six in the forty-eight-fold. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
Or one less. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
In single-day [rites], or one more. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

The opening [verses] are not [taken]; the concluding [verses are] not the final ones; the <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three) for single-day [rites are placed] at the positions of the concluding [verses]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
For the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>: 'The beautiful-formed one for aid' — six hymns. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
The insertion has been described by the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [section]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

'Here, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>'; 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, come'; 'I invoke those two whose'; 'This indeed' — nine [verses]. 'This of yours, the mind's' — eleven [verses]. 'Of the sacrifice indeed you are' — [these are] for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

'May <s>Indra</s> come with aid' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [section]. 'To us, O <s>Indra</s>' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [section] of the first <s>Abhiplava</s> [day]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
'Midday' — the recitations described here [should be understood as] these [same] <s>śastras</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

In the place of the <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) hymns: 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, who'; 'Not, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'How great'; 'O <s>Indra</s>, the city-breaker'; 'He who alone'; 'Who, the sharp-horned one'; 'Come now'; 'They desire you'; 'The messenger, ruling' — these are the connecting [verses]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
Three each for each one. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
[These have been] described with the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [section]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
'They yoke the mind'; 'Here indeed'; 'I invoke the gods' — four [verses]. 'Invoke the gods' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods) [section]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
Of the second [day], with the twenty-four-fold [stoma is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblation). — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)

'O <s>Vāyu</s>, your thousandfold [gifts]' — two [verses]. 'Come, O strong <s>soma</s> [juices]' — one [verse]. 'Of the bright, divine, touching all' — two [verses]. 'Today, of the bright, mixed with cow's [milk]' — one [verse]. 'This of yours, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — five <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three). — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)
This is called the <s>Gārtsāmada</s> <s>prauga</s> (prefatory hymn). — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)

'Of the universal lord'; '<s>Indra</s> alone is the <s>soma</s>-drinker, the one' — these are the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. '<s>Indra</s>-<s>Soma</s>'; 'Come for aid'; 'The lowest' — [these are for] the midday [pressing]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)
If a <s>Bhāradvāja</s> [descendant] is the <s>hotṛ</s>, [it follows] the standard [procedure]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)

The third pressing [follows] the twenty-four-fold [stoma]. 'Of the all-god leader' — one [verse]. 'That most excellent of <s>Savitṛ</s>' — two [verses]. 'O all-gods, of the seventy' — these are the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)

The opening and following [verses] of both the <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblation) and <s>prauga</s> (prefatory hymn) [are used] in the even [days]; thus in the <s>Abhiplava</s> [cycle]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: second day)
Of the third [day]: 'Three noblemen'; 'He who was born as the first' — [these are for] the midday [pressing]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: third day)

'That of the god'; 'With ghee'; 'Heaven and Earth' — three [verses]. 'Born without a horse, from afar, who' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 'For <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the bearer'; 'The stream-like'; 'O <s>Maruts</s>'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the first <s>Aṅgiras</s>' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. Of the fourth [day]: 'The fierce one was born' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: third day)
'I call upon <s>Agni</s>'; 'My [call]'; 'Heaven and Earth' — three [verses]. 'The [prayer] stretched out for me' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: fourth day)
'<s>Vaiśvānara</s> with the mind' — three [verses]. 'Those who shine forth, the guardians of the people' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: fourth day)
Of the fifth [day]: 'By what beauty?'; 'Who, the sharp-horned one' — [these are for] the midday [pressing]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: fifth day)
But of the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> [hymn], the ninth [verse] is the last one, and also elsewhere where the <s>nivid</s> (invocation) would be placed. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: fifth day)

'The ghee-rich one'; 'Of beings, the supremely radiant'; '<s>Indra</s> with the <s>Ṛbhus</s> who possess prizes' — two <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three). 'How for the beloved one' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: fifth day)

'Of <s>Pṛkṣa</s>, the mighty'; 'For the mighty troop'; 'The strength-born one indeed' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. Of the sixth [day]: the <s>Sāvitra</s> and <s>Ārbhava</s> [sections]; with the third [pressing], also the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s>. 'Which of the two is earlier, the dawns or the nights?' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 'O you who are to be offered to'; 'This chant' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Thus [ends] the <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day [period]. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
Of that [cycle], the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>s [are] on both sides; the <s>Ukthya</s>s [are] in the middle. — (soma: Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
On the <s>ukthya</s> days, [these are] the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse) [pairs]. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>)
[These belong] to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest]. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>)

'Come now, let me speak to you'; '<s>Agni</s> the <s>Bhārata</s> went forth'; 'Forth for you, O heroes, the shining ones'; 'With praises, by conveyance'; 'Sing to the most bountiful one'; 'Forth, O <s>Agni</s>, with your protections'; '<s>Agni</s>, to you the increasing one'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, whatever sacrifice and worship'; 'Most worthy of worship, you we have chosen'; 'He who with kindling, with oblation'; 'We kindle your, O <s>Agni</s>'; 'Both with ghee, O beautiful-splendored one' — two and one. '<s>Agni</s> — I consider him [to be] the beneficent one'; 'To you the calf, the mind'; 'Whatever, O <s>Agni</s>, bring thick wealth'; 'Most dear to you, your guest'; 'Best, O youngest <s>Bhārata</s>'; 'Auspicious is our <s>Agni</s> when offered to'; 'If, offered with ghee'; 'Indeed those who kindle <s>Agni</s>'; 'These indeed I praise loudly.' — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)

Now for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>: 'Without a rival,' 'Not you,' 'But me,' 'Your unaging [qualities],' 'Thus indeed you are heroic,' 'Thus indeed is his bountiful nature,' 'That intoxication of yours we celebrate,' 'That indeed sing forth,' 'We, you, O ancient one.' — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)

'He who for us, this, this before'; 'Sing <s>sāman</s> to <s>Indra</s>'; 'O friends, let us pray for blessings'; 'He who alone knows'; 'You who, O <s>Indra</s>, drink <s>soma</s>'; 'O <s>Indra</s>, tell us here'; 'This, the sweetest of the sweet'; 'Now let us praise <s>Indra</s>'; 'O friends.' — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)

'Praise <s>Indra</s> [with] all-possessing [hymns]' (variant: 'universally'); 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, bring here'; 'We, you, O ancient one'; 'He who for us, this, this before'; 'Come, O <s>Indra</s>, [to] these [soma drops]' — thus the collected <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse) [is]: 'Without a rival,' 'Not you,' 'But me,' 'Your unaging [qualities].' — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)

Now for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>: '<s>Indra</s>, all have increased'; 'A hymn to be recited for <s>Indra</s>'; 'Hear the call, with cross-eared listening'; 'Hear the call'; '<s>Soma</s> has been pressed for you, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'Drink this pressed <s>soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'O <s>Indra</s> of wondrous generosity'; 'Most effective for your aid'; 'Breaker of citadels, young, wise'; 'For you are indeed the bull for generosity'; 'The <s>Gāyatrī</s> singers sing of you'; 'The self of songs, like a charioteer.' — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)
Having left one [verse] from each hymn, they should insert [additional verses]. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)
When the <s>stoma</s> (chant) is increasing. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)

'These indeed for you, the revolving ones, thinking' — three [verses]. In the hymn '<s>Indra</s>, who of you': 'Your willingness,' 'The sacrifice for you two,' 'You two heroes,' 'I purify you,' 'These for you,' 'The portions' — [these are assigned] to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> as appropriate. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)

In the hymn 'He who propped up, the rock-splitter, at the sacrifice of heaven': 'As if [coming] further from home,' 'May <s>Indra</s> come,' 'The self-ruler,' 'This prayer' — [these belong to] the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)
In the hymn 'Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed': 'Beyond measure' — [this belongs to] the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: <s>Abhiplava ṣaḍaha</s>: <s>ukthya</s> days)
Of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [ṣaḍaha], the days having been described by the <s>Abhiplava</s> [rules], the first [two days follow] the first two [Abhiplava days]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)
And the third pressings [follow] each day [respectively]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)
But 'They approach' — on the first day is the ghee [hymn]. 'Send <s>Agni</s> as messenger' — on the second. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)
On the third, 'Yoke up' is the ghee [hymn]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)

'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come for the enjoyment' — one [verse]. 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come, auspicious from heaven' — two [verses]. '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, of these pressed [soma juices]' — of the two, either one [is recited] twice. 'To <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, we'; '<s>Aśvins</s>, come here'; 'Come with the pressed [soma], the sweet one'; 'Together with all the gods'; 'And to us in pleasant and unpleasant [times]' — this is the <s>Uṣṇih</s>-meter <s>prauga</s> (opening litany). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)
At the last [verse], the repetitions verse by verse [are] four-syllabled. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)
Or not. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)

The midday [pressing] has been described by the third <s>Abhiplava</s> [day]. 'Him, him indeed for prosperity, great'; 'Three are <s>Indra</s>'s <s>soma</s> [drinks]' — these are the opening verse and subsequent verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]. If the <s>Vairūpa</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant): 'Whatever, O heaven,' '<s>Indra</s>, three hundred,' '<s>Indra</s>, as great as you' — these <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns) are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: days 1-3)
On the fourth day, in the opening [verse] of the morning <s>anuvāka</s> (litany), the <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulated chant) [begins] at the first half-verse. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The second [syllable is a] vowel, an 'o'-sound, three-<s>mātrā</s> (mora) in length, <s>udātta</s> (high-pitched), [recited] three times. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
And above each of those, unlimited — or five — half 'o'-sounds, <s>anudātta</s> (low-pitched). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
But for the last one, three. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The first syllable is suppressed during the <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulation). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
We shall illustrate that as an example. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
[Example omitted.] — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
'<s>Agni</s>, as if with self-made [praises]' — this is the ghee [hymn]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Except for the last [verse], in the third feet [of each verse, there is] the <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulation) and the <s>ninarda</s> (rumbling sound). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulation) has been described. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The <s>ninarda</s> (rumbling sound) [has] a vowel at the beginning and an 'o'-sound at the end, fourfold. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

The first and last [are] <s>udātta</s> (high-pitched). The other two [are] <s>anudātta</s> (low-pitched). The latter [of the two anudāttas is] more low-pitched. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The first [is] <s>pluta</s> (protracted). The last ends with 'm.' We shall illustrate that as an example. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
'<s>Agni</s>, as if with self-made [praises].' 'We choose you as <s>hotṛ</s>.' [Example omitted.] — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
[Example omitted.] — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Or alternatively: <s>udātta</s> (high), <s>anudātta</s> (low), <s>svarita</s> (circumflex), <s>udātta</s> — thus the fourfold <s>ninarda</s>. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
[Example omitted.] — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
From the first half 'o'-sound, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should begin the <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulation). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Or from the first or second. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
[There should be] a pause — so some [say]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Or as they think they will bring [the recitation] to completion. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

'O <s>Vāyu</s>, the bright one, I come to you'; 'Perform the offering, O invoker'; 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, a hundred bay horses'; '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, of these <s>soma</s> [juices]'; 'He has discerned, of good power'; 'To us with all aids'; 'That one of yours, irresistible'; 'The offspring, the crooked, the enemy'; 'The most watery, the most sinful' — this is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>-meter <s>prauga</s> (opening litany). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The first [verses are] one-footed. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

'You we worship with sacrifices'; 'This, O <s>Vasu</s>, is the pressed drink' — these are the opening verse and subsequent verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
'Hear the call, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'O <s>Indra</s> accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
One should insert the <s>nivid</s> (laudatory formula) in the last [hymn], when there are multiple hymns. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

If the <s>Vairāja</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant): 'Drink the <s>soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; may it intoxicate you' — [these are] the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

'Where was it heard, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'Fight on' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [recitation]. But of [the hymn beginning] 'Hear the call,' the <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulation) [is performed] at the first half-verses of the opening <s>tṛca</s> (set of three). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Likewise for the 'Where was it heard' [hymn]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Of the <s>Virāj</s> (verses), in the middle feet. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The <s>pratigara</s> (response) here is always preceded by the <s>nyūṅkha</s> (modulation). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
The <s>praṇava</s> (om) at the end; [and] the <s>praṇava</s> [also belongs to] the 'Where was it heard' [hymns]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
And [reciting] by half-verses, except the last. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
'Your songs [do] not disregard [me], O swift one'; 'Forth for you, the great, the mightily-growing one, bring' — four and three <s>Virāj</s> [verses]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
Above those, after the introductory [verses], they should insert <s>tṛcas</s> (sets of three). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

The first [set belongs to] the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; the <s>tṛca</s> beginning from the last [verse] of those recited, [belongs to] the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
And [the last set belongs to] the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
'Let us worship <s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt-wielder, the giving one' — from the second [set], in the same manner. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
On the fifth day: 'Even if, O true <s>soma</s>-drinker' — one [verse] from each, in the same manner. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)
On the sixth day: 'For <s>Indra</s> indeed, heaven, the <s>Asura</s>, bowed down' — in the same manner. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fourth day)

When the <s>stoma</s> (chant) is increasing, 'Who today, the manly, with wealth'; 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come hither' — eight-versed [hymns] they should insert, the unharmed ones from <s>Parucchepa</s>'s [hymns]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
Even with those, if not sufficient, they should insert <s>Triṣṭubh</s>-meter [hymns] addressed to <s>Indra</s>, without the word '<s>Marut</s>.' — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
But one should not recite excessively by adding these. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
With one or two [additional hymns] at the morning pressing. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
With unlimited [additional hymns] at the latter two pressings. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
On the fifth [day]: 'This indeed, your guest, awakened at dawn' — nine [verses as] the ghee [hymn]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)

'May our sacrifice reach heaven' — two [verses]. 'Grant us vigor' — one [verse]. 'With the chariot, broad-powerful'; 'Many are the sun-eyed ones'; 'These indeed for you, the heaven-seeking'; 'Drink of the pressed, savory [soma]'; 'God for the god, to each his help'; 'God for the god, sing greatly the voice' — this is the <s>Bārhatī</s> (Bṛhatī-meter) <s>prauga</s> (opening litany). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
Some [say] the <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns) [should be recited] excluding the second and last. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)

'When the five peoples,' '<s>Indra</s> is the sole <s>soma</s>-drinker' — these are the opening verse and subsequent verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]. 'You are the helper'; 'Thus indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, drink for you' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation]. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)

If the <s>Śākvara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> [verses are] the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse). With one-and-a-half <s>kāras</s>, nine by the basic form become three. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
With those, one should continue the <s>purīṣa-padas</s> (earth-verses, filler passages). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
The first five [are recited] in groups of five syllables. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
Or all, as [they are] concluded. — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)
But at the source-position, as concluded, the continuation [is done] with the last [verse] together with the <s>purīṣa-padas</s> (filler passages). — (soma: <s>Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s>: fifth day)

'Sweet thus from the diverse one; bring us the pressed [soma] with the bay horses; <s>Indra</s> was increased by all' — three <s>tṛcas</s> (three-verse groups) [constitute] the <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: fifth day)
'Forth [goes] this prayer; <s>Indra</s> for intoxication; altogether intoxicated' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> (independent recitation). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: fifth day)
In the <s>Paṅkti</s> (five-line) [meter] in the first hymns; in the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation] in <s>Paṅkti</s>; in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> in <s>Paṅkti</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: fifth day)
But the first [is] in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and the last [is in Triṣṭubh]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: fifth day)
At the conclusion of those two: 'O <s>Śatakratu</s> (hundred-powered one), complete victory' — in the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: fifth day)
'O lord of <s>Śacī</s>, the blameless one' — in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: fifth day)

At the morning pressing of the sixth [day], having made other [verses] precede the <s>prasthita-yājyās</s> (processional offering verses), they sacrifice with both without the <s>anavāna</s> (concluding formula). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'O bull <s>Indra</s>'; 'O bull-drinking ones, the <s>soma</s> drops'; 'Well-pressed with the stones, come'; 'For the presser wins the dwelling of the generous one'; 'Do not, from us, [take away] those heroic deeds'; 'Come, O <s>Agni</s>, hear — you who are praised'; '<s>Agni</s> the <s>hotṛ</s>, I consider'; 'The giver'; '<s>Dadhyañc</s>, the first of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, [proclaimed] my birth.' — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Likewise at the midday [pressing]; but there, the <s>anavāna</s> (concluding formula) is one and a half [verses]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'Drink the <s>soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, the well-pressed'; 'By <s>Indras</s>'; 'For <s>Indra</s>, indeed, heaven, the <s>Asura</s>, bowed down' — six [verses]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
But above the verses of the <s>ṛtu-yājas</s> (seasonal offerings). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Thus indeed they sacrifice. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'For you impelling, O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the cows [and] the waters.' — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'This one was born in the holding-place of men' — this is the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) [portion]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The separation [is] by one and by two [verses]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

The conclusion [is] by three; the <s>praṇava</s> (sacred syllable) [is] by four. Where [the recitation is] by half-verses, [it follows] the <s>Pārucchepa</s> [arrangement]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'The sacred grass is spread' — two <s>tṛcas</s>. 'Well-pressed with the stones, come'; 'You two, by hymns of praise, devoted to the gods, the <s>Aśvins</s>'; 'We seek, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'O bull <s>Indra</s>'; 'Let there be the <s>śrauṣaṭ</s> [call]'; 'Come, O <s>Agni</s>, hear — you who are praised'; 'You gods who are eleven in heaven'; 'This one gave the impetuous, debt-releasing one' — this is the <s>prauga</s> (prow-shaped opening). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Two and one [verses] in the fifth; single-cup [portions] in the penultimate; in the last, verse-by-verse repetitions of eight syllables. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Or not. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'That ancient one of the great ones'; 'Three of <s>Indra</s>'; '<s>Soma</s>' — these are the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 'What chariot of yours, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'That bull, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'O companion of the <s>Maruts</s>' — three — thus [is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

Having concluded with one at the beginning, one should extend with two; having concluded with two, one should extend with two — where the <s>Pārucchepa</s> [arrangement applies to] the backward recitation. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

If the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) is <s>Raivata</s>: 'O <s>Revatīs</s> (wealthy ones), in our assembly'; 'Wealthy indeed, the praiser of the wealthy one' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>, near us'; 'Forth indeed of this'; 'He became the one' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'That god <s>Savitṛ</s>, from both [regions]' — one [verse]. 'That choicest [brilliance] of <s>Savitṛ</s>' — two. 'Darkness has come'; 'Sing greatly'; 'Brilliantly, brilliantly come, O <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>'; 'Praise the god <s>Savitṛ</s>'; 'Praise that one'; 'Within the river, the son'; 'The youth.' — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'Of non-deceitful speech, gracious'; 'That god <s>Savitṛ</s> has impelled — the lord of wealth'; 'Both well-established worlds, the good creator' — these are the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (All-Gods recitation). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
And having extracted the last hymn — three [hymns remain]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'This thus, belonging to <s>Rudra</s>.' — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Before the penultimate [verse]: 'Those who by sacrifice' — one should insert. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Of that, by half-verses, before the last [verse], after the fourth. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Having recited the remainder: 'May the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, grant us welfare' — a <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse group). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Thus [ends] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [recitation]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
For the assistant priests' [portions], in the two-footed [verses], here in the <s>Ukthya</s> [sacrifice], they chant. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
After the <s>anurūpas</s> (response-verses), they should recite the modified technical arrangements. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

For the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>: 'O <s>Agni</s>, you are our nearest'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, be [present]; well-kindled with the kindling' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. Then one should distribute the <s>Vālakhilya</s> [hymns]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
That has been stated in [the section on] the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The first and second of the hymns [are recited] in backward verse-order. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The third and fourth by half-verse and verse; the fifth and sixth by interweaving — or one should distribute [them thus]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The first [verse] of the former [hymn is combined] with the second of the latter. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The first [verse] of the latter [hymn is combined] with the second of the former. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Of those two, [the recitation is] by separate verses. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

One should conclude with the first and second feet; one should extend with the first and second [feet]; one should conclude with the third and last [feet]; one should extend with the third and last [feet]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Thus the interweaving [is done] by half-verse in the next [pair]; thus the interweaving by verse in the following [pair]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
One should interchange indeed in the last hymns — in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [portion], everywhere. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'These are your shares' — before the last [verse], having invoked, one should mount the <s>dūrohaṇa</s> (ascent recitation). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'The swan dwelling in purity' — that [is recited] in backward verse-order, by half-verses; with the three-footed [verse], having recited the fourth as <s>anavāna</s> (without pause), having extended, one should conclude. Again with the three-footed [verse], by half-verses, in backward verse-order — the seventh. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
This is the <s>dūrohaṇa</s> (ascent recitation). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'We two are kings' — this is always [used] for the single-day [sacrifice]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Thus [say] the <s>Hauṇḍinas</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Now the <s>Mahāvālabhid</s> (great piercing [recitation]). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
These same six hymns should be distributed in interweaving — in backward verse-order; in interweaving — by half-verses; in interweaving — by verses. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
And at the ends of the <s>pragāthas</s> (chant-pairs), one should recite one-footed [verses] with continuous verse-response. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'<s>Indra</s> is the lord of all cattle; <s>Indra</s> is the lord of all earth; <s>Indra</s> perceives all; <s>Indra</s> rules over all' — four [verses]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
One should bring one [verse] from the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Twenty-three eight-syllable feet from the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (great names) with their <s>purīṣa</s> (interludes). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The response has been stated in [the section on] the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, except for the one-footed [verses]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Having drawn back the one-footed [verse], without distributing, one should recite the fourth. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The rest is the same. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

For the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>: 'These worlds we shall indeed establish' — five [verses]. 'May we attain the invincible [offering]' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'<s>Indra</s> turned away' — this is the <s>sukīrti</s> (praise). — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Of that, by half-verses, the fourth. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Then one should recite the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> [hymn] — just as the <s>hotṛ</s> [recites] the ghee [portion] beginning in the fourth [position]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
But here [it is] in <s>Paṅkti</s> (five-line) recitation manner. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
And the response without <s>praṇava</s> ending, at the second <s>Paṅkti</s> conclusion. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
From that onward, the <s>Kuntāpa</s> [hymns]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

In the third feet, the <s>udātta</s> (raised accent) that is followed by an <s>anudātta</s> (unraised accent) and is the first [such occurrence] — that one should nasalize. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

We shall also illustrate this by example: '<s>Idam</s> (this), O people, listen closely. <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> (praise of men) shall be lauded. Sixty thousand and ninety of the <s>Kaurama</s>s — at <s>Āruśama</s>, we have given — <s>hom</s>!' — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'We exult in the divine' — this is the response. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
In the fourteenth [verse], the separation [is] by one and by two [cola]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
The remainder [is recited] by half-verses. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'These horses plunged in' — seventy feet. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Or eighteen. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
Nine [are] today's. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'A gourd is buried' — seven. 'If one should strike him, how should one strike? Around and around, again and again' — and these. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'Two rays stretched out' — six <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [verses]. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'The drum with the two beaters' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'In the opening of the container' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'At the knot of the night of grain' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'The foot in the shoe' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'The second wife' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'The second woman on the path' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine' — these are the responses at the conclusions. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'Here, thus, eastward, westward, northward' — four [verses], in two-part manner, continuing with the <s>praṇava</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'Gourds' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'Spotted deer' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' '<s>Aśvattha</s> (fig tree) and <s>palāśa</s> (butea) leaves' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'The ants' nest' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine' — these are the responses at the <s>praṇavas</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'<s>Bhuk</s>' — 'It has been approached' — three feet; all as [prescribed] to the end. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)

'A dog' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'Sitting on a leaf' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine.' 'A cow's hoof' — 'O singer, we exult in the divine' — these are the responses. 'These gods have departed' — an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. — (soma: pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha: sixth day)
'The wife will be adorned' — 'O singer, we praise the divine one.' 'The <s>hotṛ</s> with the offering' — 'O singer, we praise the divine one' — these are the responses.

'The <s>Ādityas</s>, O singer, indeed led the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) to the <s>Aṅgirases</s>' — seventeen feet. 'Oṃ indeed, O singer, we praise the divine one.' 'Thus indeed, O singer, we praise the divine one' — these are the responses, alternating in the middle.
Ending with the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ).
'O <s>Indra</s>, with <s>Śarmaṛṇa</s>' — [this is the hymn] for those desiring beings.
The <s>ājya</s> (ghee-verse) and the first [verses] are joined at the fourth [day].
'When the men, the valiant, went forth' — and these [verses].
[Omitted.]
'I have praised <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>' — an <s>anuṣṭubh</s> (8-syllable meter verse). 'The pressed [juices], most honeyed' — four [verses].
'The drop settled upon the <s>Aṃśumatī</s> (stalk-bearing one)' — three [verses].
'We approach <s>Indra</s>' — [this is] the permanent one-day [hymn].
Now for the <s>acchāvāka</s>: 'Forth to <s>Indra</s>, the foremost slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse).
Now the <s>Evayāmarut</s> (hymn with the refrain 'thus, O <s>Maruts</s>'), with the <s>Vṛṣākapin</s> [hymn].
[Omitted.]
Thus the <s>ukthya</s> [hymns are recited] wherever they chant in the <s>dvipadā</s> (two-footed) [meters].
But this day has a fixed pattern.

If both [days] are <s>agniṣṭomas</s>, or if they chant <s>ukthya</s>s in non-<s>dvipadā</s> [meters], they should recite the patterns according to the standard procedure, upward from the introductory [verses], [following] the midday [pattern only].
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [recites] the <s>Bārhatā</s> (Bṛhatī-meter) hymns of the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>.
The <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> [recites] the 'good-fame' [hymn] and the <s>Vṛṣākapin</s>, reciting in the <s>paṅkti</s> (five-footed) [style].
'Heaven, lead, O <s>Indra</s>' — [this is for] the <s>acchāvāka</s>.
'The counter-<s>Evayāmarut</s>' — thus they call [this arrangement].
The <s>hotṛ</s> [recites] the <s>Evayāmarut</s> in the <s>Āgnimaruta</s> (Agni-Marut hymn), before the <s>Māruta</s> (Marut hymn), with a conjunction in the last foot.
But on the sixth day, the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back) days — having recited day by day, one more each day, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> should ascend the <s>dūrohaṇa</s> (high platform).
The <s>sampāta-sūkta</s> (confluence hymn) [is used] when they become one-day [rites].
For when they become one-day [rites], there are no day-by-day recitation pieces, no introductory [verses], no <s>kadvat</s> (containing 'kad') [verses].

In place of the <s>kadvat</s> [verses], having recited the permanent <s>pragāthas</s> (linked verses), in those [days] with <s>sampāta</s> (confluence), the <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) hymns [are used]; in the others, the final one-day [hymns].
But in those with <s>sampāta</s>, in all <s>stomas</s> (chant-forms), or on the standard one-day [rite], the <s>ahīna</s> hymns [are used] as every third one from the beginning.
The <s>sāma-sūktas</s> (chant-hymns), the <s>sāma-pragāthas</s> (chant-linked verses) — in all <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants), [these are] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [pieces].
The concluding forms [are determined] by the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
<s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [is] the first [day]; <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> the fourth; <s>Ukthya</s> the others.
Thus [ends] the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [six-day rite].
[This is] the <s>pratyakṣa-pṛṣṭha</s> (direct back-chant).
With others, [it is] the <s>parokṣa-pṛṣṭha</s> (indirect back-chant).
Or with these [chants] mixed in.
In the absence of the <s>Vairūpa</s> and other [sāmans], the <s>pṛṣṭhya-stoma</s> (back-chant form) [is used].
The <s>āparkya-pṛṣṭhya</s> [is used] when the <s>pavamāna</s> (purifying chant) character [is present].
The <s>tanū-pṛṣṭhya</s> (self-back-chant) [applies] if the <s>hotṛ</s> [follows] the <s>Śyaita</s> or <s>Naudhasa</s> [arrangement].
The <s>Abhijit</s> [day] has the <s>Bṛhat</s> (great) as its <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
It uses both <s>sāmans</s> — even though the <s>Rathantara</s> [is used] in place of the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s>.
But the <s>sāma-pragātha</s> (chant-linked verse) here [begins with] '<s>pivavān</s>' (having drunk).
'Drink the <s>soma</s>; praise him' — [this is] for the midday [pressing].
Of those two, in the one-day [rite], others may recite before [them].
'These very ones' — so [says] <s>Gautama</s>, because the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [rite] has seventeen [stomas].

However many, however many [verses of] <s>Kuśa</s>s [there are], nine or ten in the <s>niṣkevalya</s> (independent recitation), that many hymns should be for the midday [pressing] — this is the proportional rule.
In the <s>Marutvatīya</s> (Marut-possessing recitation), the last two [are] reversed.
The third pressing [uses] the twenty-four [stoma].
The first three-day period of the <s>Abhiplava</s> [has] the <s>Svarasāman</s> (tone-chants).
But here the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants) are <s>svara</s> (tone) [chants].
Their <s>stotriyas</s> (chant-verses) [are]: 'When you were born, O unprecedented one'; 'Fish-like'; 'Of you'; 'This very one'; 'Come back to this one.'
Or the first [set applies] to all.

'We indeed, having pressed, to you' — three <s>Bṛhatī</s> (great meter) [verses]. 'He who is your most helpful for protection' — six <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> (8-syllable meter) [verses] — these are the <s>anurūpas</s> (response-verses).
As the <s>Bṛhatī</s> is fitted in the <s>stotriya</s>, so [it is] in the <s>anurūpa</s>.
These are fixed, like the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> [sāmans].
The <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice day) is to be celebrated during the day.
The morning litany [is recited] after sunrise.
'Broad-shining, immortal' — six <s>dhāyyā</s> (introductory verses) in place of the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses).
A solar [animal] should be offered as the <s>savanīya</s> (pressing-day animal).
Or [animals] for <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>.
'From the ocean, the wave' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee hymn). 'That well-armed one'; 'By what beauty' — and [these form] the <s>Marutvatīya</s> (Marut-possessing recitation).
The great [chant] to be celebrated during the day [is] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).

'The shining <s>Bṛhat</s> — may he drink the <s>soma</s>-honey'; 'Homage, homage to the eye of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. If they use the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> in the <s>pavamānas</s> (purifying chants), one should recite their <s>yoni</s> (source-verses).
The earlier [source-verse is] of the <s>Rathantara</s>.
They become the first [verses]; even with others, at the confluence.
But here, the <s>sāma-pragātha</s> (chant-linked verse) is the last [verse beginning with] '<s>Indra</s> alone for divine worship.'
'Of men, you the most manly, with hymns and praises' — three [verses]. 'He who [has] sharp horns'; 'Upon that ram'; '<s>Indra</s>'s heroic deeds indeed.'

In this [recitation], having recited the <s>Aindrī</s> (Indra-laudation) <s>nivid</s>, one should recite the following six: 'Of heaven even'; 'His pressed [soma]'; 'You'; 'This one, from of old'; 'The bull, the ecstasy'; 'Forth to the most bountiful one'; 'That one indeed.'
Here the <s>Tārkṣya</s> [verse comes] at the end.
Having recited one of those, having called out, one should ascend the <s>dūrohaṇa</s> (high platform).

Thus [ends] the <s>niṣkevalya</s> (independent recitation). If the <s>Vikarṇa</s> [is used as] the <s>brahmasāman</s> (Brahmā's chant), above the <s>anurūpa</s>: 'That wondrous one of yours, overcoming hostility'; 'Forth to your generous one' — the <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> should recite the source-verses of the <s>Śyaita</s> and <s>Naudhasa</s>.
The earlier [source-verse is] of <s>Naudhasa</s>; the latter of <s>Śyaita</s>.
This is the source-verse position for the <s>hotraka</s> (minor hotṛ) [priests]. And the <s>pragātha</s> invocation — that is limited to five invocations for these.
The third pressing has been described with the last <s>Ābhiplavika</s> (Abhiplava-related) [pattern].
But the <s>pratipad</s> (opening verse) and <s>anucara</s> (following verse) are [those of] the one-day [rite].
And the <s>Bhāsa</s> [sāman is used] in place of the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s>.
'Of the mighty, bull-like, ruddy <s>Pṛkṣa</s>, now with power' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>.
'The head of heaven, the hub of the earth'; 'The head of heaven, the navel — <s>Agni</s> — of the earth' — or [these alternatives].
If [it occurs] in other [verses] with similar characteristics, from that [comes] the <s>anurūpa</s>.
The <s>Svarasāman</s> (tone-chant) [days] are reversed.
For the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering sacrifice): 'O <s>Agni</s>, of the men' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee hymn).
The midday [pressing uses] the twenty-four [stoma].
But the <s>Vairāja</s> (Virāj-meter) is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), with the <s>Sanyūṅkha</s>.
And the source-verse of the <s>Bṛhat</s> [comes] before the source-verse of the <s>Vairūpa</s>.
The <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants) of the <s>hotraka</s> (minor hotṛ priests) are the <s>Śākvara</s>, <s>Vairūpa</s>, and <s>Raivata</s>.
They recite the source-verses [of those].
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [recites] of the <s>Vāmadevya</s>; the <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> [recites] of the <s>Uktha</s>.
The <s>acchāvāka</s> [recites] of the <s>Kāleya</s>.
The one-day [rite's] <s>stotriya</s>s [are these]; the source-verses of these two.
Between those [and] the <s>kadvat</s> (containing 'kad') [verses are] the <s>sāma-pragāthas</s> (chant-linked verses) of these very <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>.

'Completely the ecstasies'; 'He who at birth itself became the one' — these are the <s>sāma-sūktas</s> (chant-hymns) before the hymns. The third pressing has been described with the last <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant day) [pattern]. But the <s>pratipad</s> and <s>anucara</s> are [those of] the one-day [rite]. If the <s>Bṛhat</s> [is used] as the <s>agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, of the sacrifices' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. Thus [ends] the nine-night [rite].
All [days] are <s>agniṣṭomas</s>.
Some [say] the <s>ukthya</s>s [are used] for the <s>svarasāman</s> (tone-chant) [days].
The second <s>Ābhiplavika</s> (Abhiplava-pattern) [uses] '<s>gauḥ</s>' (the cow [sāman]); the latter [uses] '<s>āyuḥ</s>' (the life [sāman]).
When arranged as a three-day [rite], from the first three-day period, pressing by pressing: '<s>gauḥ</s>' in between, '<s>āyuḥ</s>' from the latter [three-day period].
When arranged as a six-day [rite], '<s>gauḥ</s>' for the even-numbered [days], '<s>āyuḥ</s>' for the odd-numbered [days].
In the ten-night [rite] —
The <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) six-day [period]; the first three-day [period] again [uses] the <s>Chandoma</s> [arrangement].
But here there is no fixed <s>Vairūpa</s> on the third [day].
The midday [pressing] of the first <s>Chandoma</s> [day has] a doubled [stoma].
In the <s>Vaiṣuvata</s> (equinoctial) <s>nivid</s>-placing, and in the earlier [days].

The recitation of the second [Chandoma day]: 'great'; 'the great'; 'you indeed, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'drink the <s>soma</s>'; 'upon that one'; 'heaven and earth'; 'the great <s>Indra</s>'; 'manly' — [these form] the <s>Marutvatīya</s> (Marut-possessing recitation).

'Unprecedented, most abundant'; 'That fame at the pressing'; 'You are great, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'He who indeed from heaven'; 'You are great, O <s>Indra</s>'; 'To you' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> of the third [day]. '<s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>'; 'The <s>Gāyat-sāma</s> (Gāyatrī chant) stands'; 'The two exhilarating bay horses'; 'These indeed, you' — [this is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. — (soma: viśvajit)

'And in you they have united' — these hymns. 'May the true one come'; 'I became'; 'There [is] <s>Indra</s>'s power' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. 'Come with the forest one'; 'These indeed'; 'The brown one, the unique one' — the two-footed hymns [are placed] before the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymns. — (soma: viśvajit)
Thus [ends the description of] the compact [arrangement]. — (soma: viśvajit)

If [it is] the extended [arrangement], in the last three days of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycle], at the midday [pressings], having additionally recited <s>Gāyatrī</s> <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three), one should insert <s>nivids</s> (invocation formulas) in them. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)

'Now I invoke this protector'; 'That all-conquering one of yours'; 'O <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, O bountiful one'; 'We urge that <s>Indra</s> on'; 'This indeed by which'; 'Come to our pressed [soma] with bay horses.' — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)
Their third pressings [are in] <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [metre]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)

On the fourth day: 'May the god come'; 'Forth, O Heaven' — [this is] the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> [hymn]. 'Forth for the <s>Ṛbhus</s>'; 'Let the pure-bright one go forth' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 'In the good grace of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>'; 'Who indeed revealed?'; '<s>Agni</s>, O men' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. Eighteen [stanzas] at the end [are in] <s>Virāj</s> [metre]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)
Eleven two-footed [verses]; twenty-one <s>Māruta</s> [verses are placed in] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymns. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)

Of the fifth [day]: 'Rise up, that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the home-dweller' — three [verses]. 'Great heaven and earth'; 'Here the foremost' — four [verses]. '<s>Ṛbhu</s>'; '<s>Vibhvan</s>'; 'I praise'; 'The people' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)

'The visible form indeed'; '<s>Agni</s> the <s>hotṛ</s>, the householder'; 'That king' — three [verses] — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. The last [verse] in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymns is the efficacious one. The last one [is from] the <s>Jātavedas</s> [hymn]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)
Everywhere, having joined the closing [formulas], one should conclude. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)

Of the sixth [day]: 'Rise up, that god' — [this is] the <s>Gārtsāmada</s> [hymn]. 'What is the best?'; 'Come to us, O prize-winners' — thirteen [verses are] the <s>Ārbhava</s> (pertaining to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>) and four [form] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymns. One should extract the last <s>tṛca</s> — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)
'Both day and dark night'; 'Of your sweet names'; 'With rivalry' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. Thus [ends] the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [six-day period]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra)
Now the <s>Chandomas</s> (metre-days). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)

'A wave from the ocean' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee recitation). 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come, O pure-drinker'; 'Come near to us with your gifts'; 'You go toward the generous one'; 'To our sacrifice with your hundred-yoked teams'; 'The swift presser has stood at the offerings'; 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, for <s>Indra</s>'s delight'; 'Your hundred yoke-mates, your thousand' — these are the <s>ekapātinī</s> (one-footed verses). 'When for you, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, vying'; 'With the cow-accompanied chariot, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>'; 'Come to us, O god, with power, O impetuous one'; 'Forth at your sacrifices the godly ones have praised'; 'With surging, sustaining [power], this one has flowed' — [this is] the <s>prauga</s> (prefatory hymn). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)
In the midday hymns, having exchanged [the order], one should insert the <s>nivids</s> (invocation formulas) of the other two. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)
Likewise for the other two, the fourth and fifth [days]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)

'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, to you'; 'Go forth, O auspicious ones of the sacrifice'; 'This to the god at birth' — [these are] <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three). 'With these, O <s>Agni</s>, service' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)
The two-footed hymns are constant. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)

'<s>Vaiśvānara</s> has kindled' — one [verse]. 'He has fashioned everything'; 'He releases the seasons at will. Of the sacrifice, the warp he extends. O mighty one, purifying, shine forth! O <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, brilliant! Offered by the <s>Jamadagnis</s>.' 'Forth, your <s>Triṣṭubh</s> messenger' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: first Chandoma day)

Of the second [Chandoma day]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, your god' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee recitation). 'Will it perhaps?'; 'With homage'; 'Those who have grown'; 'Of rich food, wealth-increasing, wise'; 'The dawns have risen, of fair days, faultless' — these are the <s>ekapātinī</s> (one-footed verses). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: second Chandoma day)

'Willing messengers, protectors of the unfailing one'; 'As far as bodies [extend], as far as strength' — one and two [verses]. 'At the rising of the sun for you two'; 'With hymns'; 'The cow of ancient [days], yielding the desired'; 'Come, <s>Indra</s>, to the prayer, O knower'; '<s>Agni</s> rose high, the well-praised one looked upon the wealth'; 'And may that <s>Sarasvatī</s>, delighting, [come] to us' — [this is] the <s>prauga</s> (prefatory hymn). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: second Chandoma day)

'For aid, the golden-handed one' — four [verses]. 'Great heaven and earth for us'; 'The young parents again' — two <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three). 'From the gods indeed, [come] down' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: second Chandoma day)

'The <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, possessing <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the lord of the light of <s>ṛta</s> — we seek the unfailing heat. Established on the ridge of heaven, <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, the great — with his light he drives away the darkness. <s>Agni</s> in the ancient seats; Desire of what has been and what will be — the sole sovereign rules supreme.' 'Your playful troop'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, be gracious' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: second Chandoma day)

Of the third [Chandoma day]: 'We have attained the great' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee recitation). 'Forth, the heroes'; 'The bright ones have borne themselves forth'; 'Those meditating with the true mind'; 'They who dwell in heaven, of the earth'; 'Come, O all-desirable <s>Aśvins</s>, come to us'; 'This <s>soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, is pressed for you'; 'Forth the prayers of the <s>Aṅgirases</s> have gone'; 'The god-seekers invoke <s>Sarasvatī</s>'; 'Come to us from the great sky, from the mountain'; 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, lead us to better [fortune]' — [this is] the <s>prauga</s> (prefatory hymn). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: third Chandoma day)
The <s>ekapātinī</s> (one-footed verses) [come] last. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: third Chandoma day)

'Evening has come'; 'Praise, O great one'; 'Of heaven' — two <s>tṛcas</s>. '<s>Indra</s>, grant sustenance to us'; 'Bestow upon us treasures' — one and two [verses]. 'Those who are thirty' — [this is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: third Chandoma day)

'May <s>Vaiśvānara</s> come for our aid from afar — <s>Agni</s>, [come] near to our well-chanted [praises]. <s>Vaiśvānara</s> has come together to this sacrifice — <s>Agni</s> with <s>uktha</s> (praise) and conveyance. <s>Vaiśvānara</s> delighted in the <s>Aṅgirases</s> — the <s>stoma</s> (chant) and <s>uktha</s> (praise); in these [he placed] heaven-reaching splendour.' 'O <s>Maruts</s>, of whom indeed'; 'Forth for <s>Agni</s> the speech' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: third Chandoma day)

In place of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [verses]: '<s>Agni</s>, O men, with meditations, in the fire-sticks' — [this] <s>tṛca</s> (group of three) [is used] in the <s>Āgneya</s> (pertaining to <s>Agni</s>) ritual. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

'<s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), from her sister's darkness' — [this is] the <s>paccha</s> (response verse) of the two-footed [verses], [recited] thrice, for the <s>Uṣasya</s> (dawn) ritual. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
'Come, O bright <s>Aśvins</s>, with good horses' — [this] <s>tṛca</s> [is used] in the <s>Āśvina</s> ritual. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

In place of the second and third [verses] of the <s>Stoka</s> hymn: 'In the joints'; 'Of ghee, with meditations'; 'Both of the beautiful-shining'; 'Of clarified butter' — these [are substituted]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

'O Waters, carry forth this' — in place of this: 'O Waters, our mothers, purify us.' 'To you, O <s>Agni</s>, for protection' — in place of [this] and the <s>tṛca</s>s: 'To us, the sharp-flaming one'; 'May the answered one be bold' — these <s>tṛcas</s> are for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

'Around you, O <s>Agni</s>, the city, we' — in place of this: 'O <s>Agni</s>, you strike down the foe.' 'Rise up, look upon' — in place of this: 'Rising with power.' 'Stride wide, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — in place of the ghee offering verse: 'Be like <s>Mitra</s>, benevolent, with ghee-offerings.' — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
And day by day, in the day-groups where this day would occur. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
Some [say] one should add [the verse] with <s>Sinīvālī</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
On this day, one should not dispute with anyone about anything — 'non-disputable,' they call this. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
In case of doubt, [one should recite] the self-study outside the <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
Some [say] within the <s>vedi</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
There is no purpose [served by one] with a consonant or [one that is] added. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
In opposition, they should offer an expiatory [oblation]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
'O <s>Agni</s>, [praise] him today like a horse with chants' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee recitation). — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

The division [is] by five syllables, or by ten syllables. 'To you as if to a chariot for aid' — in place of this: 'At the <s>Trikadrukas</s>, the buffalo [drinks] barley-mixed [soma].' — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
'Let us friends wish for blessings' — three <s>Uṣṇih</s> [metre verses]. 'O <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>' — [this is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

'By what wonderful [aid] has he come to us?' — in these [verses] the <s>Rathantara</s> [sāman is] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant); one should recite its source [verse]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
And [the source verse] of the <s>Bṛhat</s> — [says] <s>Gāṇagāri</s>, because of the connection with even [days] in the ten-day [rite]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

Having additionally recited the <s>Tārkṣya</s> one-footed [verse], one should recite the one-footed <s>ṛc</s>-verses: '<s>Indra</s> is the lord of all cattle' — four [verses]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
The continuation [is] with the last [verse]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
'O <s>Indra</s>, greatest <s>soma</s>-drinker' — six <s>Uṣṇih</s> [verses]. 'Of the warrior, that' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
'That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose' — in place of this: 'That god <s>Savitṛ</s> I [praise] with hymns.' — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

'O <s>Ṛbhukṣan</s>' — [this is] the <s>Ārbhava</s> (pertaining to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>). 'Like a cow to the herdsman' — [this is] the two-footed [section]. 'O kindled <s>Agni</s>, with kindling, with song, praise' — these <s>tṛcas</s> and the two-initial <s>Jātavedas</s> [hymn]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
With the fourth [pressing arrangement], the remaining hymns of the extended [rite]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

The <s>Vāmadevya</s> [sāman is] the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> chant. '<s>Agni</s>, O men, with meditations, in the fire-sticks' — [these are] the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse). This day [has the form of] an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
After the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s>s (offerings with the wife): — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

In the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire) they offer [reciting]: 'Delight here; delight here; here is firmness; here is self-support. O <s>Agni</s>, <s>vāṭ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>vāṭ</s>!' — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)

In the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-tender's hearth): 'Let loose the sustaining [stream], the mother; the sustaining one suckled. May [<s>Agni</s>] bestow upon us prosperity of wealth, nourishment, and vigour, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
Having performed the solemn entry into the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall), they chant the <s>Mānasa</s> (mental) [stotra]. — (soma: vyūḷha daśarātra: tenth day)
When he considers [the chant] to have been praised, he should summon [saying] 'O <s>adhvaryu</s>.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
'Ho, O <s>hotṛ</s>' — [says] the other. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'This mottled cow has stepped forth' — having recited three [verses] in a whisper, directed away, with explanatory accent he should announce the <s>caturhotṛs</s> (four-<s>hotṛ</s> formulas). — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day) (Thought was the ladle.)
'The gods, O <s>adhvaryu</s>, with <s>Prajāpati</s> as householder, sat in a communal session (<s>sattra</s>).' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
'<s>Om</s>, O <s>hotṛ</s>; so be it, O <s>hotṛ</s>' — the <s>adhvaryu</s> responds at each pause, at [each of the] ten statements. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'Thought was their ladle; consciousness was their ghee; speech was their <s>vedi</s> (altar); study was their sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>); intention was their fire; discernment was their fire-tender (<s>āgnīdhra</s>); breath was their oblation; <s>sāman</s> (chant) was their <s>adhvaryu</s>; <s>Vācaspati</s> (lord of speech) was their <s>hotṛ</s>; mind was their instructor.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'They indeed took this cup: O <s>Vācaspati</s>, O <s>Vidha</s>, [we worship] your name. May we worship your name. May you, O <s>Vidha</s>, by our name go to heaven. Whatever success the gods with <s>Prajāpati</s> as householder attained — that success we shall attain.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
The <s>adhvaryu</s> withdraws. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
Then the other [<s>hotṛ</s>] runs after [him] in a whisper [reciting] 'the body of <s>Prajāpati</s>.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

[He recites] '<s>Brahman</s>' and 'ascending'; 'the food-eater and the food-wife'; 'the auspicious and the beautiful'; 'the unshaking and the fearless'; 'the unobtained and the unobtainable'; 'the unconquerable and the irresistible'; 'the unprecedented and the brotherless' — [these are] the bodies [of <s>Prajāpati</s>]. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'<s>Agni</s> is the householder' — so say some — 'he is the householder of this world. <s>Vāyu</s> is the householder' — so say some — 'he is the householder of the atmospheric world. That one indeed is the householder who shines yonder [the sun]; he is the lord, the seasons are the house.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'One who, knowing the divine householder, becomes a householder of those [sacrificers] — he succeeds as a householder, those sacrificers succeed. One who, knowing the god whose evil has been struck away, becomes a householder of those [sacrificers] — he as a householder strikes away evil, those sacrificers strike away evil.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, we have succeeded!' — [this is said] aloud. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
This is the offering verse (<s>yājyā</s>). — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
This is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation). — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
He does not give the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response exclamation). The mantra following the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> has been stated. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
'We have succeeded, O <s>hotṛ</s>' — the <s>adhvaryu</s> responds. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
The <s>adhvaryu</s>, having mentally taken the cup, mentally brings the portion (<s>bhakṣa</s>). — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
In the mental partakings, the invitation and the partaking [are done] mentally. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

Having mentally invigorated themselves, grasping the <s>audumbarī</s> (udumbara post), they restrain their speech until the stars are visible. There they should wish to keep their hands downward. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

When [the stars] are visible, facing the <s>adhvaryu</s>, grasping [the post], they proceed to the bathing-place, murmuring: 'You two, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Parvata</s>, fighting in front.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
By the <s>adhvaryu</s>'s path — [according to] some. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
Under the axle of the southern <s>havirdhāna</s> (soma-cart shed) — [according to] some. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

Having reached the waters, having chosen [boons], they release their speech [saying]: 'Whatever we did deficiently here, whatever we did in excess — may that go to <s>Prajāpati</s> the father.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
Then they conceal their speech [saying]: 'May speech come, may speech come, may speech, the comparison, come, speech!' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
At the refuse-heap site, having called the <s>subrahmaṇyā</s> (invocation) three times, they release their speech. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
But the release of speech here is fixed [i.e., obligatory]. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
This is the extent of the <s>hotṛ</s>'s duty in a <s>sattra</s> (communal session), apart from the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

On this, this sacrificial song (<s>gāthā</s>) is sung: 'The <s>atirātra</s> (overnight), the <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth), the two <s>ṣaḍahas</s> (six-day cycles), the <s>abhijit</s> and <s>svaras</s> (accent days), the <s>viṣuvān</s> (solstice day) and the <s>viśvajit</s> (all-conquering), the <s>chandomas</s> (meter-days) and the tenth [day's] observance.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'The <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening offering), the <s>caturviṃśa</s>, the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant day) and the <s>abhiplava</s> (overflowing) indeed, the <s>abhijit</s>, the <s>svara-sāmans</s> (accent chants), the <s>viṣuvān</s> and the <s>viśvajit</s> likewise.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

'The <s>chandomas</s> (meter-days) and the tenth day, and the last is the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. The <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day), <s>ekāha</s> (single-day), [and] <s>sattras</s> — the model is declared. If another [arrangement] is taught, the days accept [it] as formerly taught. Twenty-five [days] by which the year is measured — of these very [days] the origins [are] three hundred and sixty.' — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

Therefore, whatever contacts with the <s>hotṛ</s>'s duties are taught in the <s>Chāndogya</s> (Sāma-related) or <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (Yajur-related) [traditions], one should not perform them, because the <s>hautra</s> (hotṛ's liturgy) is not complete [in those traditions]. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

Dependent on the <s>chandoga</s> (Sāma-chanter) [are]: the <s>stoma</s> (chant-form), <s>stotriya</s> (praise-verse), <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), and <s>saṃsthā</s> (concluding form). — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
