Dependent on the <s>adhvaryu</s> [are]: the explanation of purpose, time, place, and sacrificial fees; the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), <s>upasad</s> (approach offerings), initiation, concluding form and completion; the extent of the oblations; [the rules for] loud and whispered [recitation]; and the sequence of oblations. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)
From these very days, we shall explain the <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) and <s>ekāha</s> (single-day) [rites] that are subsequent [modifications]. — (soma: vyūḍha daśarātra: tenth day)

Having instructed a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>) of this [knowledge], one who is not rejected, for a minimum of one year, having examined [him] regarding the vow, one should teach the next day to one who is compassionate. — (soma: mahāvrata)
The <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (great names) [are taught] first. — (soma: mahāvrata)
In the bright fortnight of the northern course [of the sun], the student, [going] outside the village, having cooked a pot-meal mixed with sesame, should inform the teacher. — (soma: mahāvrata)

When [the teacher] has been informed, having asked about uncertainties regarding the vow, if [the student] has completed [the vows] from the short syllable onward, having taken hold [of the fire], he should offer [into] the fire [saying]: '<s>Agni</s>, the entered one, moves about; this son of the seers is the sovereign.' — (soma: mahāvrata)

'To him I offer with the oblation of ghee. May the share of the gods not be confused. He who would confuse our share — <s>svāhā</s>. She who falls sideways — I am the supporter' — [thus he recites]. — (soma: mahāvrata)

'With the stream of ghee I worship you, the gratifying one, <s>svāhā</s>. For whatever desire of ours, O all-ruling one, we worship, having granted that desire to us, then drink this ghee, <s>svāhā</s>.' — (soma: mahāvrata)

'May this <s>Agni</s> of ours create wide space; may he go before us, breaking through hostilities. May he conquer enemies, exulting; may he win the prize in the prize-contest. <s>Svāhā</s>. To the non-grudging one and to <s>Anumati</s> (approval), <s>svāhā</s>. To the bestower, <s>svāhā</s>.' And separately with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances). — (soma: mahāvrata)
Having offered, he says: 'Eat all of this pot-meal.' — (soma: mahāvrata)

When [the student] has eaten, one should make him venerate the sun with a handful of water [saying]: 'You are the lord of vows, the vow-master. I shall observe the vow; may I be able [to do so]; by that may I be capable; by that may I succeed.' — (soma: mahāvrata)
Having concluded [the ritual], having closed [the eyes], one should restrain speech, observing the [proper] time, when one would come to agreement with the teacher. — (soma: mahāvrata)
For one night, because of the supplementary study. — (soma: mahāvrata)
Or for three nights, with the regular study. — (soma: mahāvrata)
Observing that same time, the teacher, having wound a new garment three times clockwise around the head so as to cover the face, says: 'Remain thus for this period; be sleepless.' — (soma: mahāvrata)
For that period he should sit sleepless. — (soma: mahāvrata)

When [the teaching] is about to be transmitted, having established the fire in the unconquered direction [i.e., the northeast], placing a sword, a water-vessel, and a stone to the north of the fire, having tied a young heifer [facing] west and north, out of hearing. — (soma: mahāvrata)
The teacher should sit on grass behind the fire, facing the unconquered direction. — (soma: mahāvrata)

The celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>), having wiped the remnants [of the offering], having circumambulated the fire and the teacher to the right, having respectfully approached, should sit behind the teacher, on grass, facing the western-southern direction. — (soma: mahāvrata)
Pressing back to back, he should say mentally: 'Teach me the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (great names).' — (soma: mahāvrata)
Having asked again, to [a student who is] compassionate, with eyes closed, one should recite [them] with the <s>purīṣa</s> (interlude) syllables, three times. — (soma: mahāvrata)

Having recited [them], having removed the turban (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>), he should look at the sun [saying]: 'With <s>Mitra</s>'s eye I look upon you; with <s>Mitra</s>'s eye I perceive you.' — (soma: mahāvrata)

'With <s>Mitra</s>'s eye I behold you' — [looking at] the directions, the miscellaneous [items]. Again [looking at] the sun: 'With <s>Mitra</s>'s eye I see you. He who hates us and he whom we hate — may the cause [of evil] from the eyes reach him.' — (soma: mahāvrata)

He should touch the earth [saying]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, homage to <s>Iḍā</s>, homage to <s>Iḍā</s>, homage to the seers, the mantra-makers, the mantra-lords. Homage to you, O gods. Be auspicious and most peaceful for us, O <s>Sarasvatī</s> of gentle grace.' — (soma: mahāvrata)

'May your sky not be visible [i.e., may it not be seen by the unworthy].' 'May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods. May <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s> be [propitious] for us with [their] protections. I praise the well-observing people with the newest [hymns]. Who [shall be] our wondrous one with beauty?' — three [verses]. 'Be gentle, O Earth' — [thus reciting]. Having concluded, the same [procedure follows] except for the miscellaneous [items]. — (soma: mahāvrata)
This is the rule of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) for the two [teacher and student]. — (soma: mahāvrata)
One [person acting] as both teacher [and student] — [this is also possible]. — (soma: mahāvrata)
From [the month of] <s>Phālguna</s> up to [the month of] <s>Śravaṇā</s>, [there is] study for those who have not previously studied. — (soma: mahāvrata)
From [the month of] <s>Taiṣa</s> (Pauṣa) onward, for those who have previously studied, for those who have previously studied. — (soma: mahāvrata)
The <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) and <s>ekāha</s> (single-day) [rites] have their models stated. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for satra)
By the established days, the extension (<s>atideśa</s>) of [other] days [is made]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for satra)

When there is no [specific] extension, a single-day <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> with twelve hundred [cows] as sacrificial fee — with that the recitations of single-day [rites] should be performed. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for satra)
The <s>Go</s> and <s>Āyuṣī</s> [rites], reversed, [are the model] for two-day [rites]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for satra)
For three-day [rites], the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) day is the first; or the <s>abhiplava</s> (overflowing) day. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for satra)
And likewise the sacrificial fees are proportional, up to [but not including] the <s>atirātra</s> (overnight) rites. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for satra)
But the <s>Atirātras</s> (overnight sacrifices) [have] a thousand [as sacrificial fee]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
And the two-day and three-day [sacrifices as well]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)

Those <s>ahīnas</s> (multi-day sacrifices) that are longer than three days — having counted a thousand for the three-day [portion], from that [onward] thousands [are given] daily. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
But they should distribute the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) evenly, as in [the basic rule]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
The surplus, however, [is added] to the last [day] as extra. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)

For those that have been specially prescribed, since the <s>stoma</s> (chant), <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), and <s>saṃsthā</s> (concluding form) are different, there is no [substitution with] something else. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
The modifications [are either] obligatory or occasional. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)

But at the midday [pressing], in the <s>hotṛ</s>'s <s>Niṣkevalya</s> (independent recitation), one should recite what is required by the <s>stoma</s>. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
There, the supplementary [verses are inserted] at the beginning of the hymns, except for the <s>Tārkṣya</s> [hymn]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
When there is omission, the extraction [is done] from that very [source]. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
When <s>stomas</s> (chants) are below the nine-fold, <s>tṛcas</s> (three-verse groups) alone [are used] there in the positions of hymns. — (soma: modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
One should insert the <s>nivids</s> (laudatory formulas) as in the obligatory [procedure]. — (modification of ahīna and ekāhas for sattra)
The <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites have been stated. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
We shall describe the <s>soma</s> [sacrifices] in place of the seasonal rites. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
Some [say they are performed] without a <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post). — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
They yoke the animal to the enclosing [stick]. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)

In place of the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (All-Gods rite), [there is] the first <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) day. 'The mightiest, fierce, the fierce one was born' — [these are] the midday [hymns]. The <s>hotrā</s> (invocatory formulas) are from the single-day [sacrifice] everywhere, on the first days of the <s>sāmpātika</s> (coincidence) [rites], which are single-day [sacrifices]. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)

The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> and <s>Pārjanya</s> oblations, and the animal-cake of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], should be carried along [with the soma offerings]. In the <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes) of the morning pressing, the oblations of the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> should be carried along. The <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (All-Gods) animal [is offered]. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary [cow]) is [dedicated] to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
In place of the <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s>, [there is] a two-day [sacrifice]. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
In the <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes) of the morning pressing of the latter day, the oblations of the <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s> should be carried along. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The animals [dedicated] to the <s>Maruts</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary [cow]) is [dedicated] to <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
In place of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>-<s>Aindra</s>-<s>Agna</s> [rite]. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
In place of the <s>Sākamedha</s>, [there is] a three-day [sacrifice] ending with an <s>Atirātra</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
In the <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes) of the second day, at each pressing, [are placed] the oblations of the previous day. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)

On the third day, having offered the <s>upāṃśu</s> (silent cup) and <s>antaryāma</s> (inner cup), [one offers] the <s>paurṇadarvī</s> (full-ladle offering). In the [cakes] of the morning pressing, the <s>kraiḷina</s> (offerings to the playful <s>Maruts</s>). — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
At the midday [pressing], the <s>Māhendrāṇi</s> (offerings to <s>Mahendra</s>). — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
Between the ghee offering-verses, at the southern <s>mārjālīya</s> (purification fire), the <s>pitryā</s> (ancestral rites). — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
There, the attendance [is] as for those who perform without carrying [the fire] forward. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
They should carry along the <s>Āditya</s> (solar) [oblation] with the animal-cake of the <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary cow). — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The animals [are]: [one dedicated] to <s>Agni</s>, [one] to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, [and] the elevenfold [animals]. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary [cow]) is [dedicated] to <s>Sūrya</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)

An <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [is performed] in place of the <s>Śunāsīrīyā</s>. In the <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes) of the morning pressing, the oblations of the <s>Śunāsīrīyā</s> should be carried along. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The animal [is dedicated] to <s>Vāyu</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary [cow]) is [dedicated] to the <s>Aśvins</s>. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
The <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) are fifty [cows] per day. — (pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha)
Now the <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration) [rites]. — (rājasūya)
Before the full-moon day of <s>Phālgunī</s>, one should sacrifice with a purificatory <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> as the <s>abhyārohaṇīya</s> (ascending offering). — (rājasūya)
On the full-moon day, one commences the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) rites. — (rājasūya)
The regular seasonal rites [are performed]. — (rājasūya)
But with the two [sacrificial] wheels, they perform [rites] in the intervals between the seasons. — (rājasūya)
[The order is] day-reversal or fortnight-reversal. — (rājasūya)
At the end of the year, in the same fortnight, [are performed] the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> (consecration) and the <s>Daśapeya</s> (ten-cup offering). — (rājasūya)
The <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> is an <s>Ukthya</s> [sacrifice] with the <s>Bṛhat</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) and both <s>sāmans</s>. — (rājasūya)

When the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation] has concluded, seated to the south of the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) on a golden cushion, one should narrate the <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> [legend] to the king who has been consecrated and is surrounded by his sons and ministers. — (rājasūya)
He narrates seated on a golden cushion; he who receives [the narration] accepts seated on a golden cushion. For gold is glory; thus he endows him with glory. — (rājasūya)
'Om' is the response to a <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse group); 'Tathā' (so be it) [is the response] to a narrative song (<s>gāthā</s>). — (rājasūya)
'Om' is indeed divine; 'Tathā' is human. Thus by both the divine and the human, one releases him from evil sin. — (rājasūya)
Therefore, whatever king would be victorious — even without performing the sacrifice — should have this <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> narrative narrated. For not even a small sin remains in him. — (rājasūya)
One should give a thousand [cows] to the narrator. — (rājasūya)
A hundred to the respondent. — (rājasūya)
Each at their respective seat. — (rājasūya)
Having performed the <s>saṃsṛpa-iṣṭis</s> (creeping offerings), one should sacrifice with the <s>Daśapeya</s> (ten-cup offering). — (rājasūya)
There, ten [priests] at a time should partake of one cup each. — (rājasūya)
Having counted the regular [priests], one should cause the others to participate. — (rājasūya)

Those who, on both the mother's and father's side, have maintained [purity] for ten generations through learning and austerity, and through meritorious deeds — those in whom there is no non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> [ancestry] on both sides — them they should lead [to participate]. — (rājasūya)
Some [say] only on the father's side. — (rājasūya)

'The <s>Navagvas</s>, having pressed the <s>soma</s>, [called] <s>Indra</s>'; 'Where, as a friend, with the nine <s>Navagva</s> friends' — at the first of the two [hymns] with the <s>nivid</s> (laudatory formula) inserted. — (rājasūya)
'In the <s>sūktamukhīya</s>' — as stated, one should understand these. — (rājasūya)
In the bright fortnight, the <s>keśavapanīya</s> (hair-cutting [ceremony]) — an <s>Atirātra</s> with the <s>Bṛhat</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>. — (rājasūya)
After two months, the <s>vyuṣṭi-dvyaha</s> (dawn two-day [sacrifice]). — (rājasūya)
An <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> on the first day. An <s>Atirātra</s> with all <s>stomas</s> on the second. — (rājasūya)
In the bright fortnight, the <s>Kṣatrasya-dhṛti</s> (sustaining of sovereignty) — an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. — (rājasūya)
Thus [end] the <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration) [rites]. — (rājasūya)
And the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) are determined by rule, except for the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> and <s>Daśapeya</s>. — (rājasūya)
But at the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>, thirty-two thousand [cows] each, separately, to the chief [priests]. — (rājasūya)
Sixteen [thousand] each to the second[-rank priests]. — (rājasūya)
Eight [thousand] each to the third[-rank priests]. Four [thousand] each to the fourth[-rank priests]. — (rājasūya)

For the <s>saṃsṛpa-iṣṭis</s> (creeping offerings): gold for the <s>Āgneyī</s>; a heifer for the <s>Sārasvatī</s>; a black [bull] for the <s>Sāvitrī</s>; a white-backed [one] for the <s>Pauṣṇī</s>; a bull for the <s>Bārhaspatyā</s>; a great hornless [bull] for the <s>Aindrī</s>; [one dedicated] to <s>Varuṇa</s> for the <s>Vāruṇī</s>. — (rājasūya)
The <s>Daśapeya</s> [has] a thousand [as fee]. — (rājasūya)
And these are the prescribed <s>dakṣiṇās</s>. — (rājasūya)
A golden garland [is given] to the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter). — (rājasūya)
A horse to the <s>Prastotṛ</s> (precentor). A milch cow to the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> (respondent). — (rājasūya)
A goat to the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> (assistant). — (rājasūya)
Two golden earrings to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. — (rājasūya)
Two silver [earrings] to the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> (counter-officiant). — (rājasūya)
Twelve and sixty pregnant [cows] to the <s>Brahmā</s> (presiding priest). — (rājasūya)
A barren cow to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. — (rājasūya)
A gold ornament to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. — (rājasūya)
A bull to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. A cotton garment to the <s>Potṛ</s>. A linen and a fur [garment] to the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>. — (rājasūya)
A single-yoked [cart] loaded with barley to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (rājasūya)
A heifer to the <s>Unnetṛ</s>. A three-year-old uncastrated [bull] to the <s>Grāvastut</s>. — (rājasūya)
One who considers himself as if he has swallowed poison should perform the <s>Uśanas Stoma</s> (praise of <s>Uśanas</s>) to conquer [the affliction]. — (uśanas stoma etc.)

'<s>Uśanas</s>, [coming] with the powerful ones, has arrived'; 'You [are like] waters, when the wise one traveled for the desiring one' — these are the <s>sūktamukhīyas</s> (hymn-openings). [For the] <s>go-stoma</s> (cow-praise), <s>bhūmi-stoma</s> (earth-praise), and <s>vanaspati-sava</s> (plant pressing): 'The swift horse does not reach them, nor the pebble-cutter, nor does the thief destroy or seize them'; 'Verily thus, the firm [ones] of the mountains'; 'O lord of the forest, with the oblations'; 'O lord of the forest, having tied with the rope' — these are the <s>sūktamukhīyas</s>. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
One desiring sovereignty or desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s> should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s> (pressing for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>). — (uśanas stoma etc.)
Its <s>tṛcas</s> (three-verse groups) [are placed] in the positions of hymns. — (uśanas stoma etc.)

'<s>Agni</s> rules among the gods' — this is the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) [portion]. 'He who supported, shaking' — these are the <s>sūktamukhīyas</s>. '<s>Indra</s>, with the <s>Maruts</s>, here'; 'Of men, you' — the midday. 'Up, that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the golden'; 'Ghee-rich, the splendor of the worlds'; '<s>Indra</s>, with the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, prize-bearing, sprinkled'; 'May the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, grant us welfare' — the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. '<s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>Agni</s>, perceived by the mind'; 'May the vigorous <s>Agnis</s> come forth with might'; '<s>Agni</s>, kindled, with the kindling praise' — the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. The assistant priests, after the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>, should recite the first and last <s>tṛcas</s>. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
But from the <s>pragāthas</s> at the midday [pressing]. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
Eleven <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) each at each pressing. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
Or eleven thousand each. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
Or hundreds. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
A horse [is given] additionally at the midday [pressing]. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
One who has a rival and wishes to overcome [him] should sacrifice [with this]. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
One desiring heaven [should perform] the <s>sadyaskriyā</s> (same-day rite), <s>anukriyā</s> (repeat rite), or <s>parikriyā</s> (surrounding rite). — (uśanas stoma etc.)
One desiring food should [sacrifice with] the <s>ekatrika</s> (one-three) or <s>tryeka</s> (three-one) [arrangement]. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
With the <s>Gotama Stoma</s>, one who desires 'May my offspring be generous' [should sacrifice]. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
The recitation of these seven has been stated in [the section on] the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s>. — (uśanas stoma etc.)

'You are the counterpart of the earth'; 'You became great, O <s>Indra</s>, through prayer'; 'The bull born immediately, the youngest'; 'You, <s>Indra</s>, immediately born'; 'Indeed, the gods follow you, O slayer'; 'To your great <s>Indriya</s> (might) has been given.' — (uśanas stoma etc.)

'How shall I serve you, knowing?' — two [verses]. 'Of even one, my power surpasses'; 'The one true lord of the five peoples'; 'Three — <s>Aryaman</s>, of men, the divinity'; 'Forth indeed of this great one, the great things'; 'Thus indeed, O <s>Soma</s>, in intoxication'; '<s>Indra</s> has grown for intoxication' — these are the <s>sūktamukhīyas</s>. — (uśanas stoma etc.)
They make the <s>Gotama Stoma</s> an inner <s>Ukthya</s> [sacrifice]. — (gotama stoma)

If it is an <s>Ukthya</s> within the cups: 'O <s>Agni</s>, with the <s>Ṛkvā Maruts</s>'; 'Rejoice, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>'; 'For <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'; 'For <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, together' — these one should insert in the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation] before the encircling verse. — (gotama stoma)
The invocation [is made] for both. — (gotama stoma)
In either one — some [say]. If among the <s>ukthya stotriya</s> (chant-verses), [one chants] with the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [sāman]. — (<s>Gotama stoma</s>)
Or with their own [sāmans]. — (<s>Gotama stoma</s>)
Having invoked the <s>stotriyas</s> (chant-verses) once; likewise the <s>anurūpas</s> (corresponding verses). — (<s>Gotama stoma</s>)
Similarly elsewhere too, when there is a coincidence of <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>. — (<s>Gotama stoma</s>)
But if in the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> source-position, it would be with all the <s>ukthya sāmans</s> in the basic form — when that is the case. — (<s>Gotama stoma</s>)
One desiring to perform sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s> (hawk) and <s>Ajira</s> (swift) [rites]. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'I am <s>Manu</s>'; 'Even in the womb'; 'With you, O <s>Manyu</s> (wrath)'; 'Whatever of yours, O <s>Manyu</s>' — these are the midday [hymns]. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
The remainder [follows] the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s> (pressing for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
The <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) [is made] of reeds. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
The enclosing sticks [are made] of pestles. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
The fuel [is made] of <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica) [wood]. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
Or of <s>vāghātaka</s> [wood]. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
Having murmured, one should call out 'Hear ye!' — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
And one should give the response-call. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
One should utter the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> [exclamation] as if cutting. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
One should pour [the oblation] as if crushing. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
A prepared hide [serves as] the <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
A threshing floor [serves as] the <s>uttaravedi</s> (high altar). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
A winnowing basket [serves as] the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
A stake-point [serves as] the <s>yūpa</s>. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
[It is] without the <s>caṣāla</s> (top-piece of the post). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
A bundle [serves as] the <s>caṣāla</s> (top-piece). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
These are the accessory modifications. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
And the <s>adhvaryus</s> know other [modifications]. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
But when the harvest is ripe, the <s>hotṛ</s> should follow the joint directive. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
One who is overwhelmed by evil reputation or great illness, or one who is capable of begetting but does not obtain offspring — he should sacrifice with the <s>Agniṣṭuta</s>. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)

'Stand firm, O bay horses'; 'He who just born' — these are the midday [hymns]. If entirely dedicated to <s>Agni</s>, the <s>stotriya-anurūpa</s> pairs should be addressed to <s>Agni</s>. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
Or in all deity-designations, one should direct [them] to <s>Agni</s> alone. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
That being the case, immediately after, one should sacrifice with the <s>Indrastuta</s> (praise of <s>Indra</s>). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'<s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>'; '<s>Indra</s>, praise' — these are the midday [hymns]. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
One desiring prosperity, or desiring a village, or desiring offspring should sacrifice with the <s>Upahavya</s>. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'These indeed for you'; 'He who alone' — the midday [pressing uses] the <s>kulāya</s> (nest) of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> for one desiring progeny. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'Stand firm, O bay horses'; 'Praise him indeed' — the midday [pressing uses] the <s>ṛṣabha</s> (bull [sāman]) for one who is about to conquer. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'O <s>Indra</s> accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>'; 'Fight for him' — these are the midday [hymns]. With strong <s>soma</s>, for one desiring food-eating. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'Where is this hero?'; 'Of the strong one, the overpowering' — these are the midday [hymns]. With the <s>vighana</s> (striking [rite]), for one practicing sorcery. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
Its recitation [uses] the <s>Ajira</s> (swift [arrangement]). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
With [the hymns to] <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>Utkrānti</s> (ascent [rite]) — for one desiring heaven. — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)

'These indeed for you'; 'O heaven, lead, O <s>Indra</s>' — the midday [hymns]. One who desires: 'Let me go away from evil, from sin' — he should sacrifice with the <s>Ṛtapeya</s> (truth-drinking). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'For abundant are the streams of <s>ṛta</s> (truth)' — at the hymn-facing [recitation], they partake of the cups with truth [saying]: — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
'True is this earth; true is this <s>Agni</s>; true is this <s>Vāyu</s>; true is that <s>Āditya</s> (sun).' — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)
<s>Soma</s> cups [are given as] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). — (<s>Śyena</s> etc.)

One about to sacrifice with the <s>Atimūrti</s> (surpassing form) should sacrifice for a month with the <s>Saurya</s> (solar) and <s>Cāndramasī</s> (lunar) <s>iṣṭis</s> (offerings). — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
[On the] bright [fortnight, one performs] the <s>Cāndramasī</s> (lunar); with the <s>Saurya</s> (solar), the other [fortnight]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)

Here [are] the offering and invitatory verses: 'Of the cow they have discovered'; 'New and new he becomes when born, the crossing one, visible to all'; 'The wondrous face of the gods has risen.' — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
'He indeed settled this great, resounding one'; 'Having overcome with sleep <s>Cumuri</s> and <s>Dhuni</s>' — at the hymn-facing [recitation]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
With the <s>Sūryastuta</s> (praise of the sun), for one desiring fame. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
'Drink the <s>soma</s>'; 'Praise <s>Indra</s>' — the midday [hymns]. With the <s>Vyoman</s> (sky [rite]), for one desiring food-eating. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
With the <s>Viśvadeva-stuta</s> (praise of all gods), for one desiring fame. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
With the five-fold <s>Śāradīya</s> (autumnal [rite]), for one desiring cattle. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
For these three [rites]: 'By what splendor'; 'That indeed was [his]' — these are the midday [hymns]. The first two [share] both <s>sāmans</s>. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
The five-fold <s>Śāradīya</s> is an <s>Ukthya</s> [sacrifice]. 'For every clan, your guest' — this is the ghee [hymn]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
The <s>Kaṇva Rathantara</s> [is] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant). — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
With the <s>Gosava</s> (cow-pressing) and <s>Vivadha</s> (carrying [rite]), for one desiring cattle. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
'<s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>'; 'Let us go with this' — the midday [hymns]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
Ten thousands [are the] <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees). — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
Sixteen single-day [sacrifices]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
'Long life'; 'cow' — in exchange. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
With the <s>Udbhid</s> (sprouting) and <s>Balabhid</s> (strength-splitting [rites]), for one desiring heaven. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
'<s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>'; '<s>Indra</s> the fortress-breaker' — the midday [hymns]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
The <s>Vinuti</s> (removal) and <s>Abhibhūti</s> (overpowering) [rites use] the arrow and thunderbolt [hymns] and the <s>Manyu</s> (wrath) hymns. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
One performing sorcery should sacrifice [with them]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)

The <s>Tviṣi</s> (splendor) and <s>Apaciti</s> (reverence) [use] '<s>Saṃrāṭ</s>' (supreme ruler) and '<s>Svarāj</s>' (self-ruling), '<s>Rāṭ</s>' (ruler) and '<s>Virāj</s>' (shining forth), and the <s>śadas</s> (shed) [formula] in the single-day [rite]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
The <s>Upaśada</s> and <s>Rāśimarā</s> [rites use] the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> and <s>Tadidāsīya</s> [hymns]. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
[These are] for those desiring prosperity, sovereignty, food-eating, vital power, and brilliance. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
These desires [are fulfilled] two by two. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
The <s>Ṛṣi-stomas</s> (seer-chants) and <s>Vrātya-stomas</s> (vagrant-chants) [constitute] the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) days. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
The <s>Nākasada</s> (heaven-seated), <s>Ṛtu-stomas</s> (season-chants), and <s>Dik-stomas</s> (direction-chants) [constitute] the <s>Abhiplava</s> days. — (<s>Ṛtu yāja</s>)
With the <s>Vājapeya</s> (drink of victory), for one desiring sovereignty. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
Seventeen consecrations. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
Or seventeen [is] the limit. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
The priests wearing golden garlands should officiate. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
[The garland] for the <s>Hotṛ</s> [has] thunderbolt-filaments and a hundred lotuses. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)

The <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering) [is] the ghee [hymn]. 'By what splendor'; 'That indeed was [his]' — the midday [hymns]. When the <s>Marutvatīya</s> is concluded, the <s>Bārhaspatya iṣṭi</s> (offering to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) [is performed]. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)

From the ghee-portions to the end of the <s>Iḷā</s>. '<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, being born first'; '<s>Bṛhaspati</s> conquered wealth.' 'We invoke you as swift messenger'; 'Praising <s>Agni</s> of good kindling, of good kindling, of good appearance' — these are the joint offering verses. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)

But if the <s>adhvaryus</s> should cause the chariot-race to be run, then the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], at the proper place, having mounted a wheel attached to a beam, while it is being turned clockwise, should sing the <s>Vājina sāman</s> (prize-song): 'The heroes have appeared, the prizes — the prize-winners have come. By the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, may the horses win heaven; the horses win heaven.' Or [reciting]: — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)

If one has not studied the <s>sāman</s> (chant), one should recite this <s>ṛc</s> (verse) three times. The third pressing has been described by the third <s>Abhiplava</s> [day]. If, while chanting in the <s>Citravatī</s> [verses]: 'You, O wondrous-aided <s>Agni</s>'; '<s>Agni</s>, born with <s>Vivasvat</s> and the dawns' — these are the <s>stotriya-anurūpa</s> of the <s>Agniṣṭoma sāman</s>. But the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [is performed] here. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
Above that, the supplementary <s>uktha</s> (recitation). — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
'Forth that today, O <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, your name'; 'Forth that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is praised for [his] heroic power' — these are the <s>stotriya-anurūpa</s>. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
'<s>Brahman</s> was born first in the east'; 'Whatever you wish to give'; 'You indeed, O lord of strength.' — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
'Him in the ancient way' — of the thirteen [verses], having left one, having invoked, one should mount the <s>dūrohaṇa</s> (ascent recitation). — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)

'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you two and <s>Indra</s>, of wealth' — this is the <s>paridhānīyā</s> (enclosing verse). 'The resplendent <s>Bṛhat</s> — may he drink the sweet <s>soma</s>' — this is the offering verse. For that [sacrifice], the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) [are]: of cows — hundreds; of horse-chariots, of riding horses, of draft horses; of cooking vessels; of female servants wearing gold necklaces; of elephants with golden girths — seventeen groups of seventeen [each]. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
The other ten groups of <s>dakṣiṇās</s> [consist of] wealth, each at least a hundred, in decreasing halves. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
Or one should double the former ones in groups. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
One should complete [them as] seventeen groups of seventeen. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)
Thus [ends] the <s>Vājapeya</s>. — (<s>Vājapeya</s>)

Having sacrificed with that, a king should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration). A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [should sacrifice] with the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s> (pressing for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>).
For the <s>Anirukta</s> (unexpressed [sacrifice]), by the twenty-four-fold [stoma are performed] the morning pressing and the third pressing. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
'Him in the ancient way' — but thirteen [verses constitute] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods [recitation]). — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
'By what splendor'; 'That indeed was [his]' — the midday [hymns]. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
The assistant priests, after the <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns), should recite the first <s>sampātas</s> (coincidences). — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
Or the <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) hymns. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
Similarly at the first pressing, when the <s>Bṛhat pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants) are not in the collected tradition. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
The arrangement of the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering [sacrifice is]) according to desire. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
Of that, what is common with the <s>Viśvajit</s> [is taken] from the <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns). — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
In the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s>, [this is] the ghee [hymn]. And the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s> [each have] a <s>tṛca</s> (set of three). — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
But with those two, the former ones [are used] in the single-day [sacrifice]. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
The assistant priests, after the <s>pragāthas</s>, should recite the unmodified technical arrangements. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
And the <s>Sāma</s>-hymns. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
The first <s>tṛcas</s> (sets of three) of the <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) hymns. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
Of the final single-day [hymns], the last [tṛcas]. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
The third pressing is the same as in the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s>. But here <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> [comes] before the <s>Vaiśvadeva tṛca</s> (all-gods set of three). — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
But the <s>Evayāmarut</s> [comes] in the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> (Agni-Marut [recitation]), after the <s>Māruta</s> (Marut [portion]). — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
The method of recitation for those two has been stated. — (<s>Anirukta</s>)
One whose cattle do not thrive, or who wishes to lead away other clans — he should sacrifice with the <s>Aptoryāma</s> (completing the sacrificial circuit). — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
At the midday [pressing], what has been described by the <s>Viśvajit</s>, except for the technical arrangement's source. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
By a single-day [sacrifice]. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
If chanting in the <s>garbhakāra</s> (womb-making [mode]), then the <s>stotriya-anurūpas</s> are just the same. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
First with the <s>Rathantara</s>, then with the <s>Vairāja</s>, then with the <s>Rathantara</s>. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
Or with the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Vairāja</s>, in the same manner. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
Or the <s>Śyaita</s> and <s>Vairūpa</s>. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
The <s>Kāleya</s> and <s>Raivata</s> [belong] to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
In the sequence of <s>sāmans</s>, two <s>pragāthas</s> (responsorial hymns) each, without the <s>garbhakāra</s> (womb-making [mode]). — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
But the <s>Atirātra</s> [is performed] here. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
If an <s>Ukthya</s> without the <s>Dvaipada</s> (two-footed), the <s>Vaiṣuvata</s> [is] the third pressing. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
After the <s>Āśvina</s> [recitation], supplementary <s>ukthya</s> [recitations]. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)

'Awake to old age'; 'Learn that'; 'Aging, you are kindled'; 'By <s>Agni</s>, by <s>Indra</s>'; '<s>Agni</s> shines forth'; 'With the lord of the field, we' — this is the <s>paridhānīyā</s> (enclosing verse). 'You two gods, by ancient wisdom' — this is the offering verse. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)

'Whatever today, O <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer'; 'Rise up indeed'; 'Heard [is] the generous one'; 'With all [aids]'; 'Early-coming'; 'O lord of the field, a honey-sweet wave' — this is the <s>paridhānīyā</s>. 'You two gods, three times eleven' — this is the offering verse. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)

'That <s>Indra</s> we impel'; 'Great <s>Indra</s> who with power'; 'Now <s>Aśvins</s>'; 'That chariot of yours'; 'Honey-sweet herbs'; 'Heaven and earth'; 'The waters' — this is the <s>paridhānīyā</s>. 'That praiseworthy [deed] of the <s>Aśvins</s>, done by you' — this is the offering verse. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
'May the gods help us from there' — or the last [verse] of the <s>anurūpa</s>. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)

'I invoke heaven and earth'; 'Both now'; 'The divine <s>hotṛs</s>, the first, the placed-before' — this is the <s>paridhānīyā</s>. 'This is your portion deposited, O worship-worthy ones' — this is the offering verse. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
If one has not studied, 'The ancient seat, the auspicious friendship of yours' — four [verses serve as] offering verses. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)

'That [hymn] sing for you at the pressing, together'; 'Sing a hymn to <s>Indra</s>'; 'That constant one of yours, the always-conquering'; 'Constantly your [devotees] follow' — or [these are] the <s>stotriya-anurūpas</s>. — (<s>Aptoryāma</s>)
The <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) are unlimited, exceeding a thousand.
And white she-mules — for each <s>hotṛ</s>, for each <s>hotṛ</s>.
[The <s>Atirātra</s>] for one desiring brilliance.
The nine-seventeen [stoma is] for one desiring offspring.
The <s>Viṣuvat</s>-stoma [is] for one who has a rival.
And the '<s>Gauḥ</s>' (cow) and <s>Abhijit</s> [patterns].
The '<s>Gauḥ</s>' with both <s>sāmans</s> and all <s>stomas</s> [is] for one desiring to prosper.
The '<s>Āyuḥ</s>' (life) [pattern is] for one afflicted with long illness.

The <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering sacrifice) [is] for one desiring cattle. The <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) days, from the beginning, [are] for those desiring celibacy, strength, offspring, and stability, respectively, each with separate desires.
Thus [end] the <s>Atirātras</s> (overnight sacrifices).
Of those, the first three have the recitation patterns of one-day [rites].
Thus [end] the one-day sacrifices (<s>ekāhas</s>).
Now the <s>ahīnas</s> (multi-day sacrifices).
Beginning with two days, having twelve nights as the maximum, beginning with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, ending with <s>Atirātra</s>, concluding at [each] month, with unlimited consecrations.
Therein, the numbers of days are counted, ending with six-day [periods] from the <s>Abhiplava</s>.
But the <s>Atirātra</s> is the last among the counted ones, for completing the count.
When there is a deficiency, an additional <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [day is inserted].
The <s>Āṅgirasa</s> (rite of the Aṅgirases) [is] for one desiring heaven.
Or for one who is meritorious but diminished and not desiring to retrieve [his merit].
The <s>Caitra-ratha</s> [is] for one desiring food. The <s>Kāpivana</s> [is] for one desiring heaven — these are the two-day [rites].
But the third pressing of the first [rite's] latter day [follows] the pattern of the third [pressing].
'You indeed, O <s>Kṣaitavat</s>' — and [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee hymn).
The <s>Garva</s> three-night [rite is] for one desiring heaven.
Its middle day has the <s>Vāmadevya</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant); the <s>Viśo-viśīya</s> [is] the <s>agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>.
The <s>Vāravantīya</s> [is used] on the last [day].
'You, O <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>' — and [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee hymn).
The <s>Vaida</s> three-night [rite is] for one desiring royal power.
All [days] are <s>trivṛt</s> (threefold) <s>Atirātras</s>.
The <s>Chandoma-Pavamāna-Antarvasū</s> [rite is] for one desiring cattle.
The <s>Parāka-Chandoma-Parāka</s> [rite is] for one desiring heaven.
Thus [end] the three-day [rites].
[These] have the recitation patterns of the <s>Garga</s> three-night [rite].
The <s>Atri</s> four-hero [rite is] for one desiring heroes.
Its <s>ājya</s> (ghee) [hymns contain the word] 'hero-possessing'.
'O <s>Agni</s>, you who are best at winning prizes' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> on the second day. 'O <s>Agni</s>, whoever is mortal' — on the third. 'O <s>Agni</s>, of men' — on the fourth.
The fourth [day] has a <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> [concluding form].
Its [pṛṣṭha is]: 'To you, O bull, the pressed [soma]' — in <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meters], the <s>Rathantara</s> [is] the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
In <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> and <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meters], the <s>Bṛhat</s> [is the pṛṣṭha].
On the fourth: 'You, O [slayer] of <s>Bala</s>, possessing cows'; 'When you were born, unprecedented' — or [these].
The <s>Jāmadagna</s> [rite is] for one desiring nourishment.
Its <s>upasads</s> (preparatory offerings) have <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes).
The <s>Vaiśvāmitra</s> [is] for one who has a rival and desires offspring; the <s>Vasiṣṭha-Saṃsarpa</s> [likewise].
Thus [end] the four-day [rites].

The <s>Sārvasena</s> [is] for one desiring cattle. The <s>Daiva</s> [is] for one who has a rival. The <s>Pañcaśāradīya</s> (five-autumns rite) [is] for one desiring cattle. The <s>Vratavat</s> (vow-possessing rite) [is] for one desiring long life. The <s>Vāvara</s> [is] for one wishing to speak eloquently.
Thus [there are] five five-night [rites].

But in the <s>Pañcaśāradīya</s>, seventeen bullocks dedicated to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Maruts</s>, together with seventeen heifers accompanied by <s>Mārutī</s> [verses], five years old, consecrated by circumambulation around the fire, [are] the pressing-day [animals].
Of those, they should offer three [each] on [each of the] four days; the remaining five on the fifth.
But in the <s>Vratavat</s>, in place of the third day, [there is] the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance).
The last is a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> five-day [rite].
The six-day [rite] of the seasons [is] for one desiring stability.
The <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> — compact or extended.
The <s>pṛṣṭhya-avalamba</s> (pṛṣṭhya pendant) [is] for one desiring cattle.
The <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> five-day [rite] attached [to a Viśvajit], and the <s>Viśvajit</s> also.
The <s>Sambhārya</s> (assemblage rite) [is] for one desiring long life — the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> three-day [period] first, and the <s>Abhiplava</s> three-day [period] also.

The <s>Ṛṣi</s> seven-night [rite is] for one desiring prosperity. The <s>Prājāpatya</s> [is] for one desiring offspring. The <s>Chandoma-Pavamāna-Vrata</s> [is] for one desiring cattle. The <s>Jāmadagna</s> [is] for one desiring food. These four [have] a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [period] and a <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
[They have] a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [period] and a <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
But the <s>vrata</s> (observance) has its own <s>stoma</s> on the first [day].
Seventeen[-fold stoma] on the second.
<s>Chandoma-Pavamāna</s> on the third.
Twenty-four[-fold] <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> (outer purifying chant), seventeen[-fold] remainder — the fourth.
The <s>Aindramati</s> and the others [are] for one desiring offspring to prosper.
<s>Trikadruka</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Viśvajit</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s> — with all <s>stomas</s>.
The <s>Janaka</s> seven-night [rite is] for one desiring prosperity — <s>Abhiplava</s> four-day [period], <s>Viśvajit</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s>, <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
The seventh [day with] <s>pṛṣṭhya-stoma</s> and <s>Viśvajit</s> [is] for one desiring cattle.
The eight-night [rite is] for one desiring divinity.
[It has] a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [period], <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
The nine-night [rite is] for one desiring long life — [it has] a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [period] and <s>Trikadruka</s>s.
The <s>Trikadruka</s>s [as] a <s>pṛṣṭhya-avalamba</s> (pṛṣṭhya pendant) — [this is] for one desiring cattle.
Thus [end] the nine-night [rites].
The <s>Trikakub</s> (triple-kakubh) one-and-a-half [is] a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>. The <s>Mahā-Trikakub</s> extended [is] a nine-night [rite]. The <s>Samūḷha-Trikakub</s> (compact Trikakub) [is] compact.
The four-stoma <s>Trikakub</s> one-and-a-half [is] an <s>Abhiplava</s>. With these four, one desiring preeminence among one's own [people] should sacrifice.
The <s>Kusurubindu</s> [rite is] for one desiring prosperity — [taking] each of the three <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> days, one by one, thrice.
The <s>Chandomavat</s> (meter-possessing rite) [is] for one desiring cattle — before the <s>Viśvajit</s> of the <s>pṛṣṭhya-avalamba</s>, a <s>Chandoma</s> [day], and the tenth day also.
Formerly [used for] performing hostile rites.
'<s>Jyotiḥ</s>' (light), '<s>Gauḥ</s>' (cow) surrounding, '<s>Gauḥ</s> Abhijit</s>, <s>Viśvajit</s>, '<s>Āyuḥ</s>' (life).
The <s>Śalalī-piśaṅga</s> [rite is] for one desiring glory.
The <s>Abhiplava</s> three-day [period] first, three times.
Thus [end] the ten-night [rites].

The <s>Pauṇḍarīka</s> (lotus sacrifice) [is] for one desiring prosperity — [it has] a <s>pṛṣṭhya-stoma</s>, <s>Chandoma</s>, <s>Gotama-stoma</s>, <s>Viśvajit</s>; or the extended nine-night [rite], <s>Mahāvrata</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
Now the two <s>Sambhāryas</s> (assemblage rites).
<s>Atirātra</s>, twenty-four[-fold] one-and-a-half, <s>Abhiplava</s> or <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>.
The <s>Indra-vajra</s> [rite is] for one who has a rival.
After that, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
Now there should be twelve-day [rites].
They may be <s>sattras</s> (communal sessions) or <s>ahīnas</s> (multi-day rites).
The ten-night [rite] has been described.
Compact or extended.
Flanked on both sides by <s>Atirātras</s>.
Or at the two <s>Sambhāryas</s>, one should add a <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [day].
The year-extending [rite is] for one desiring glory — <s>Atirātra</s>, twenty-four[-fold], nine-night [rite] excluding the <s>Viṣuvat</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
Now the <s>Bharata</s> twelve-day [rite].
They should approach this very one-day [rite] with different concluding forms.
<s>Atirātra</s> first, then <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, then eight <s>Ukthyas</s>, then <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, then <s>Atirātra</s>.
Thus [ends] the twelve-day [rite].

Those desiring to prosper by themselves, by offspring, and by cattle, those about to procreate, those who will attain the world of creation, those who desired preeminence among their own [people] — they should approach [the sattra] or sacrifice [the ahīna].
Thus [the distinction] of separateness.
Now the common [rules].
Since <s>dharma</s> (ritual law) is unlimited, we shall state [only] portions of it.
For just as limited phonemes attain the unlimited course of speech, even so [there are] unlimited combinations of limited days.
But the days are established; whatever combination of them [is made], the recitation pattern is also established.
But when there is doubt about the days, some [resolve it] by the <s>stoma</s>, <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, and concluding forms.
That is incomplete, because deviations are observed.

Having made an agreement only with the <s>Sāmaveda</s> chanters regarding the <s>Bṛhat</s>- or <s>Rathantara</s>-character of the day, the <s>Rathantara</s> [hymns] should not be recited with a one-day [recitation pattern].
With the second <s>Ābhiplavika</s> [pattern for] the <s>Bṛhat</s> [hymns].
Or perhaps the <s>Kayā-śubhīya</s> and <s>Tad-id-āsīya</s> [hymns] should be in the <s>nivid</s> positions; the rest [follows] the one-day [pattern].
One who will attain all desires, who wishes to conquer all victories, who will enjoy all dawns — should sacrifice with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
One about to release the horse should sacrifice with two <s>iṣṭis</s> (offerings).
<s>Agni</s> [is] the head-possessing one [as deity].
The concluding offerings [are] in <s>Virāj</s> [meter].
The second [offering] is for <s>Pūṣan</s>.
'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are widely extending'; 'O <s>Soma</s>, those life-giving [powers] of yours' — with [verses] containing [the word] '<s>sad</s>' (seat).

'You, of most brilliant fame'; 'Whatever is the best, that [is offered] to <s>Agni</s>' — [these are] the concluding offerings. Having released the horse and appointed guards, the three <s>Sāvitrī</s> (Savitṛ-related) offerings [are performed] day after day, following the <s>Vairāja</s> pattern.
<s>Savitṛ</s> the true impeller, the impeller, the stimulator.
'He who [created] all these beings'; 'May the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, of good treasure, come'; 'May that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the helper' — two [verses].

When each [recitation] is completed, sitting to the south of the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) on a golden cushion, one should narrate the <s>pāriplava</s> (cycle of legends) to the king who has been anointed, surrounded by his sons and ministers. — (aśvamedha)
The <s>adhvaryu</s> (priest), sitting on a golden bundle of grass, responds. — (aśvamedha)
When about to narrate, one should call out: 'O <s>adhvaryu</s>!' — (aśvamedha)
'Ho, <s>hotṛ</s>!' [responds] the other. — (aśvamedha)

On the first day: '<s>Manu Vaivasvata</s>; his subjects are human beings; they are seated here' — householders should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should recite a hymn. — (aśvamedha)

On the second day: '<s>Yama Vaivasvata</s>; his subjects are the ancestors; they are seated here' — elderly persons should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Yajurveda</s> is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should recite an <s>anuvāka</s> (prose passage). — (aśvamedha)

On the third day: '<s>Varuṇa Āditya</s>; his subjects are the <s>Gandharvas</s>; they are seated here' — handsome young men should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Atharvaveda</s> is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — whatever remedy is approved, that one should recite. — (aśvamedha)

On the fourth day: '<s>Soma Vaiṣṇava</s>; his subjects are the <s>Apsarases</s>; they are seated here' — beautiful young women should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Āṅgirasaveda</s> is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — whatever terrifying [text] is approved, that one should recite. — (aśvamedha)

On the fifth day: '<s>Arbuda Kādraveya</s>; his subjects are the serpents; they are seated here' — serpents, or those who know serpents, should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'Poison-lore is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should recite the poison-lore. — (aśvamedha)

On the sixth day: '<s>Kubera Vaiśravaṇa</s>; his subjects are the <s>Rākṣasas</s>; they are seated here' — wanderers and evil-doers should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Piśāca</s>-lore is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — whatever <s>piśāca</s>-related [text] is approved, that one should recite. — (aśvamedha)

On the seventh day: '<s>Asita Dhānva</s>; his subjects are the <s>Asuras</s>; they are seated here' — money-lenders should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Asura</s>-lore is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should perform some magic. — (aśvamedha)

On the eighth day: '<s>Matsya Sāmmada</s>; his subjects are the aquatic creatures; they are seated here' — fishes, heaped up, should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Purāṇa</s>-lore is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should narrate a <s>Purāṇa</s>. — (aśvamedha)

On the ninth day: '<s>Tārkṣya Vaipaścita</s>; his subjects are the birds; they are seated here' — birds, or <s>brahmacārins</s> (students), should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Itihāsa</s> (epic) is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should narrate an <s>itihāsa</s>. — (aśvamedha)

On the tenth day: '<s>Dharma Indra</s>; his subjects are the gods; they are seated here' — young, learned [brāhmaṇas] who do not accept gifts should be brought in; them one should point out [saying]: 'The <s>Sāmaveda</s> is the <s>Veda</s>; this is it' — one should sing a <s>sāman</s> (chant). Thus one should narrate in this cycle throughout the year. — (aśvamedha)
Completing each tenth [day cycle]. — (aśvamedha)
At the end of the year, one is consecrated (<s>dīkṣā</s>). — (aśvamedha)
There are three pressing days (<s>sutyā</s>). — (aśvamedha)

The <s>Gotama Stoma</s> (praise) [is performed] first. On the second day, at the time of presenting the animal, having brought the horse, they should station both [animals] outside the <s>vedi</s> (altar). — (aśvamedha)
If [the horse] should sniff or turn toward [the other animal], one should know [it is a sign of] the sacrifice's success. — (aśvamedha)
If not, one should make the sacrificer say: 'The stallion [brings] good cattle for us; the stallion, good horses.' — (aśvamedha)
That [horse], standing [still], is chanted over with eleven [verses] beginning with 'When you neighed' for the <s>upākaraṇa</s> (presentation), without concluding the <s>praṇava</s>. — (aśvamedha)
Some [say] with the self-study [recitation]. — (aśvamedha)

Having recited 'O unyielding one, may they kindled' — with 'Twenty-six are its ribs' or 'Let not, O <s>Mitra</s>' — one should insert [the verses]; and also [the verse]: 'The winning steed has come near to the praise-post' — these two. — (aśvamedha)
The queens shake the slaughtered horse, having unbraided the right hair-tresses and let loose the others, having smelled the left thighs. — (aśvamedha)
Then they lay the chief queen (<s>mahiṣī</s>) down beside it. — (aśvamedha)
The <s>hotṛ</s> (priest) addresses her with ridicule: 'Your mother and your father play at the top of the tree; your father inserts his fist into the womb in pregnancy.' — (aśvamedha)

She responds to the <s>hotṛ</s> with ridicule, together with a hundred royal daughters as attendants: 'Your mother and your father play at the top of the tree. Your mouth is like that of one about to lick; O <s>hotṛ</s>, do not you speak too much.' — (aśvamedha)

The <s>brahmā</s> (priest) [says of] the one lying with [the horse]: 'He should raise her upward, like one carrying a load up a mountain. Then let her middle tremble, as in a cool wind again.' — (aśvamedha)

She responds to the <s>brahmā</s> with ridicule, together with a hundred royal daughters as attendants: 'She raises him upward, like one carrying a load up a mountain. Then let his middle tremble, as in a cool wind again.' — (aśvamedha)
Having performed the solemn entry into the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall), having proceeded with the <s>svāhā</s>-oblations. — (aśvamedha)
They conduct the <s>brahmodya</s> (theological riddle contest). — (aśvamedha)
'Who walks alone? Who is born again? What is the remedy for cold? What is the great sowing-ground?' — the <s>hotṛ</s> asks the <s>adhvaryu</s>. — (aśvamedha)
'The sun walks alone; the moon is born again; fire is the remedy for cold; the earth is the great sowing-ground' — he replies. — (aśvamedha)
'What light is equal to the sun? What lake is equal to the ocean? Who is greater than the earth? Of what is no measure found?' — the <s>adhvaryu</s> asks the <s>hotṛ</s>. — (aśvamedha)
'Truth is the light equal to the sun; heaven is the lake equal to the ocean; <s>Indra</s> is greater than the earth; of the cow no measure is found' — he replies. — (aśvamedha)

'I ask you, O friend of the gods, for discernment — if with your mind you have gone there: in which three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s> do you stand? In which has the entire world entered?' — the <s>brahmā</s> asks the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanter). — (aśvamedha)

'I am indeed in those three steps in which the entire world has entered. Immediately I traverse the earth and the sky; with one limb [I encompass] the directions and his back' — he replies. — (aśvamedha)

'Into which has a person entered within? What things are fixed within a person? We question you about this, O <s>brahmā</s> — what will you answer us here?' — the <s>udgātṛ</s> asks the <s>brahmā</s>. — (aśvamedha)
'Into five [elements] has a person entered within; those are fixed within a person. Answering you in this, I become superior to you here, without deceit' — he replies. — (aśvamedha)
Having gone forth eastward, they ask the sacrificer one by one: 'I ask you about the farthest end of the earth.' — (aśvamedha)
'This <s>vedi</s> (altar) is the farthest end of the earth' — he replies. — (aśvamedha)
With greatness, before and above, they proceed with the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) [offerings]. — (aśvamedha)

'The self-born one, the first-born within the great ocean — he conceived the seasonally-born embryo, from which <s>Prajāpati</s> was born.' 'May the <s>hotṛ</s> offer to <s>Prajāpati</s>; may [he who is] most delighted by greatness come; may he drink the <s>soma</s>. O <s>hotṛ</s>, conquer!' — this is the <s>praiṣa</s> (direction). — (aśvamedha)

'Yours are these worlds, directions, and quarters' — this is the offering verse. 'The horse, the goat, the wild horse, the cow, the deer' — these are the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (pertaining to <s>Prajāpati</s>) [victims]. — (aśvamedha)
They proceed with the [rites for] the remaining animals. — (aśvamedha)
The <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (pertaining to all gods) arrangement [is used]. — (aśvamedha)
The recitation [follows] the fifth day of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycle] of the extended [rite]. — (aśvamedha)
We shall describe its special features. — (aśvamedha)
'That <s>Agni</s> I consider' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee recitation); its single-day [portion comes] after [the main part]. — (aśvamedha)
In the <s>prauga</s> (prefatory hymn) <s>tṛcas</s>, the single-day <s>tṛcas</s> [are inserted]. — (aśvamedha)

'At the <s>Trikadrukas</s>, the buffalo [drinks] barley-mixed [soma]' — this is the opening [verse] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>, one [verse] in place of the <s>tṛca</s>; the single-day [verse serves as] the following [verse]. And having additionally recited the single-day [portion] after extracting the last [verse] in the hymns, one should insert the <s>nivid</s> (invocation formula) in that. — (aśvamedha)
Likewise for the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. — (aśvamedha)

'That god <s>Savitṛ</s> I [praise] with hymns' — this is the opening [verse] of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, one [verse] in place of the <s>tṛca</s>; the single-day [verse serves as] the following [verse]. And having additionally recited the single-day [portions] in the hymns, one should insert the <s>nivids</s> (invocation formulas) in them. — (aśvamedha)
Likewise indeed for the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [section]. — (aśvamedha)
The fourth day of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycle is] the last [day]. — (aśvamedha)

<s>Jyotis</s> (light), <s>Gaus</s> (cow), <s>Āyus</s> (life), <s>Abhijit</s> (victory), <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering), <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance), <s>Sarvastoma</s> (all-chants), and <s>Aptoryāma</s> (completion) — [these are the forms of the sacrifice]. — (aśvamedha)

Excluding land, persons, and the possessions of non-<s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he gives the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fees) in each direction to the priests: the eastern direction [is] the <s>hotṛ</s>'s fee; the southern [is] the <s>brahmā</s>'s; the western [is] the <s>adhvaryu</s>'s; the northern [is] the <s>udgātṛ</s>'s. The assistant priests (<s>hotrakās</s>) are correspondingly dependent [on their respective chief priests]. — (aśvamedha)
Now we shall describe the special conjunctions of these days — how each is applied for each particular purpose. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
This very single-day <s>Atirātra</s> [serves as] the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening day) at the beginning. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
This same [serves as] the <s>udayanīya</s> (concluding day) at the end. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
The undifferentiated [day is] in the middle. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
In <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) rites, this same [day] has the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [form]. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
Between those two [opening and closing days] is the extended <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite). — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
This is the standard model (<s>prakṛti</s>) for <s>sattras</s> (communal sessions). — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
Therein [is] the place for insertions (<s>āvāpa</s>). — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
After the <s>Daśarātra</s>, in place of a single day, the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance) [is performed]. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
Before the <s>Daśarātra</s>, the other days [are inserted]. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)

For a two-day requirement: the <s>Go-Āyus</s> [days]. For a three-day requirement: the <s>Trikadrukas</s>. 'The <s>Abhiplava</s> three-day [period comes] first, then the <s>Trikadrukas</s>' — thus they declare. For a four-day requirement: the <s>Trikadrukas</s> and the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
For a five-day requirement: the <s>Abhiplava</s> five-day [period]. But the third pressing of the last [day follows] that of the sixth [day]. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
For a six-day requirement: the <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day [period]. Thus the regular insertions [are made]. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
[The insertions] end with six-day [periods], again and again. — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
Each complete six-day [period] follows the standard pattern (<s>tantra</s>). — (sattra: dvādaśa as the model)
Two [types of] thirteen-night [sattras exist]. — (sattra: 13–20 days)
The first [is] for those desiring prosperity: the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycle] and the <s>Chandomas</s> [are] in between; [on the last day] an <s>Atirātra</s> with all <s>stomas</s>. — (sattra: 13–20 days)
Those desiring a firm foundation [perform] the second, arranged according to rule with an observance. — (sattra: 13–20 days)
Two <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycles], the latter reversed. — (sattra: 13–20 days)
Those deliberating on matters concerning a couch, or water, or a marriage [perform] the second. — (sattra: 13–20 days)
The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [cycle] with <s>Trikadrukas</s> on both sides. — (sattra: 13–20 days)
Those desiring a firm foundation [perform] the third, arranged according to rule with a two-day supplementary [rite]. — (sattra: 13–20 days)

The first of four fifteen-night [sessions is] for those desiring divinity. Of the first fourteen-night [session], in the middle of the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant cycle), the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance) [is inserted]. — (sattra: 13-20 days)

The second [is] for those desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>. Of the second fourteen-night [session], the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> [day comes] immediately after the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening offering). — (sattra: 13-20 days)
The third [is] for those of a <s>sattra</s>-<s>ahīna</s> [nature] who wish to attain both worlds. — (sattra: 13-20 days)

Of the third fourteen-night [session], a regularly arranged three-day addition (<s>tryaha-upajana</s>) in the place of the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> <s>prāyaṇīya</s> [completes] the remainder. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
The fourth, [with] a regularly arranged three-day addition, [is] for those desiring firm establishment. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
A sixteen-night [session with] a four-night addition [is] for those desiring food. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
A seventeen-night [session with] a five-night addition [is] for those desiring cattle. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
An eighteen-night [session is] for those desiring long life. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
And here the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> (six-day cycle) is completed. We shall describe the addition for the continuous [rite]. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
A nineteen-night [session with] a one-night addition [is for] those wishing to secure domestic and wild animals. — (sattra: 13-20 days)
A twenty-night [session is] for those desiring firm establishment. The <s>abhijit</s> and <s>viśvajit</s> [days come] after the <s>abhiplava</s> (overflowing cycle). — (sattra: 13-20 days)

The first of two twenty-one-night [sessions is] for those desiring firm establishment. Of the three <s>abhiplavas</s>, between the first two, an <s>atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice) [is inserted]. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

The second [is] for those desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>. Of the nine-night [section], in place of <s>abhijit</s> and <s>viśvajit</s>, two <s>pṛṣṭhyas</s> (back-chant days), the latter being reversed. — (sattra: 21-32 days)
They call [this] 'equivalent to the year.' — (sattra: 21-32 days)
A twenty-two-night [session with] a four-night addition [is] for those desiring food. — (sattra: 21-32 days)
A twenty-three-night [session with] a five-night addition [is] for those desiring cattle. — (sattra: 21-32 days)
The first of two twenty-four-night [sessions is] for those desiring offspring, or for those desiring cattle. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

And here the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> (six-day cycle) is completed. We shall describe the addition for the continuous [rite]. Those who are about to dwell in the heavenly world, about to ascend to the seat of the Radiant One — [perform] the second. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

The <s>pṛṣṭhya-stoma</s> (back-chant praise) is thirty-three-fold (<s>trayastriṃśa</s>), described [in detail], expansive. The <s>pṛṣṭhya-stomas</s> are twenty-one-fold, twenty-seven-fold, and thirty-three-fold — in reverse order in the first three-day [period], in direct order in the latter [three-day period]. With the expansive [form], even the latter three-day [period] is in reverse and direct order. The undescribed day is the reversed <s>pṛṣṭhya-stoma</s>. — (sattra: 21-32 days)
The <s>tṛvṛt</s> (nine-fold) [stoma] is the undescribed one. — (sattra: 21-32 days)
<s>Jyotis</s> (light) [is the sāman] for both [days]. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

They call this the 'session of assemblies.' A twenty-five-night [session with] a one-night addition [is] for those desiring food. A twenty-six-night [session with] a two-night addition [is] for those desiring firm establishment. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

A twenty-seven-night [session with] a three-night addition [is] for those desiring prosperity. A twenty-eight-night [session with] a four-night addition [is] for those desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>. — (sattra: 21-32 days)
A twenty-nine-night [session with] a five-night addition [is for] those wishing to win the supreme victory. A thirty-night [session is] for those desiring food. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

And here the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> (six-day cycle) is completed. We shall describe the addition for the continuous [rite]. A thirty-one-night [session with] a one-night addition [is] for those desiring food. A thirty-two-night [session with] a two-night addition [is] for those desiring firm establishment. — (sattra: 21-32 days)

The first of three thirty-three-night [sessions is] for those desiring firm establishment. Of the three <s>abhiplavas</s>, after each, an <s>atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice) [is inserted]. — (sattra: 33+ days)

The second [is] for those desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>. Of the four five-night [periods], the last is reversed, and between the two last ones, an <s>atirātra</s> with all <s>stomas</s>. — (sattra: 33+ days)
The third [is for] those who wish to attain both worlds. Of the six five-night [periods], in the middle [is] a <s>viśvajit</s> <s>atirātra</s>. — (sattra: 33+ days)
But the latter three [five-night periods] are reversed. — (sattra: 33+ days)
A thirty-four-night [session with] a four-night addition [is] for those desiring food. — (sattra: 33+ days)
The latter four [are] for those desiring cattle. A thirty-five-night [session has] a five-night addition. — (sattra: 33+ days)

In a thirty-six-night [session], a <s>ṣaḍaha</s> (six-day cycle) is added. We shall describe the addition for the continuous [rite]. A thirty-seven-night [session has] a one-night addition. — (sattra: 33+ days)

A thirty-eight-night [session has] a two-night addition. A thirty-nine-night [session with] a three-night addition [is for] those desiring endless prosperity. A forty-night [session with] a four-night addition [is for] those establishing themselves in the supreme <s>Virāj</s> (sovereign power). — (sattra: 33+ days)

From the forty-one-night onward, the subsequent [sessions follow] the pattern up to the forty-eight-night. And from the fifty-night onward up to the sixty-night. And from the sixty-two-night onward up to the ninety-nine-night. — (sattra: 33+ days)
Among those, the one-night and four-night additions include [special] observances. — (sattra: 33+ days)
The first of seven forty-nine-night [sessions is for] those who wish to dwell free from evil. — (sattra: 49 days)

An <s>atirātra</s>, three nine-fold (<s>trivṛt</s>) days, an <s>atirātra</s>, ten fifteen-fold days, an <s>atirātra</s>, twelve days, an <s>atirātra</s>, a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [day], an <s>atirātra</s>, twelve twenty-one-fold days, an <s>atirātra</s>. — (sattra: 49 days)

Of the nine-fold [days], the first is an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, the last is a <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>. Of the fifteen-fold [days], the rest are <s>Ukthyas</s>. They call [these] the <s>vidhṛtis</s> (separations). — (sattra: 49 days)
The <s>Yama-atirātra</s> (twin overnight sacrifice) [is for] those desiring twofold prosperity, as it were. — (sattra: 49 days)

Two <s>abhiplavas</s>, <s>Go</s> [and] <s>Āyuṣī</s>, two <s>atirātras</s>, two <s>abhiplavas</s>, <s>abhijit</s> and <s>viśvajit</s>, two <s>atirātras</s>, one <s>abhiplava</s>, an all-<s>stoma</s> [day] with nineteen and seventeen [fold stomas], <s>atirātras</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s>. — (sattra: 49 days)
The third [is for] those desiring preeminence among their own [people]. Of the four <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) days, each one [is repeated] nine times. — (sattra: 49 days)
Of the nine groups, the first, sixth, seventh, and last days are <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>. — (sattra: 49 days)
The other [days are] <s>Ukthyas</s>; the fifth [is] the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. — (sattra: 49 days)
They call [this] the '<s>Savitṛ</s>'s peak' (<s>Savituḥ Kakubh</s>). — (sattra: 49 days)
For the latter three, the <s>abhiplavas</s> are regularly arranged. — (sattra: 49 days)
But in the first [session], after the fourth [day], an <s>atirātra</s> with all <s>stomas</s>. — (sattra: 49 days)

During the <s>upasads</s> (approach offerings), at the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire), having separately cooked ghee with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>sugandhi</s> (fragrant substance), <s>tejana</s> (sharp grass), and <s>paitudāru</s> (pine), at each pressing, when the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [cups] are set down, they should anoint and oil [themselves]. — (sattra: 49 days)
Those who are not afraid of [their own] radiance, or those who do not even know themselves — they should undertake these [rites]. — (sattra: 49 days)
They call [them] the 'anointing and oiling' [sessions]. — (sattra: 49 days)
These same [sessions are used] for those desiring firm establishment, without the anointing and oiling. — (sattra: 49 days)
In these same [sessions], the <s>Mahāvrata</s> [takes] the place of the all-<s>stoma</s> [day]. — (sattra: 49 days)
The last [sessions are dedicated to] <s>Indra</s>-<s>Mati</s> (Indra's thought), [for] those wishing to have offspring. — (sattra: 49 days)
In these same [sessions], having extracted the all-<s>stoma</s> [day], the <s>Mahāvrata</s> [is placed] in its proper position. — (sattra: 49 days)
The last [is for] those wishing to attain a full year's [benefits]. — (sattra: 49 days)

An <s>atirātra</s>, the <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth day), three <s>abhiplavas</s>, the nine-night [session], two <s>abhiplavas</s>, <s>Go</s> [and] <s>Āyuṣī</s>, the <s>daśarātra</s> (ten-day) observance, [and] <s>atirātra</s>. — (sattra: 49 days)
They call [this] 'equivalent to the year.' — (sattra: 49 days)
A sixty-one-night [session is] for those desiring firm establishment. In these same [sessions], two <s>pṛṣṭhyas</s> surround the nine-night [session]. — (sattra: 49 days)
Of those two, the latter is reversed. — (sattra: 49 days)
A hundred-night [session is] for those desiring long life. Fourteen <s>abhiplavas</s> with four-day additions. — (sattra: 49 days)
Thus [end] the night-<s>sattras</s> (communal sessions reckoned by nights). — (sattra: 49 days)
Now the <s>Gavāmayana</s> (course of cows) [session is for] those desiring all [wishes]. — (sattra: gavāmayana)

Having commenced with the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> (opening offering) and <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth day), they undergo four <s>abhiplavas</s> with a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> as the fifth, for five months. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Then they assemble the sixth [month]. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Three <s>abhiplavas</s>, a <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>, the <s>abhijit</s>, and the <s>svara-sāman</s> (accent chants). — (sattra: gavāmayana)
It is completed with the first two days. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Thus indeed the first half. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Then the <s>viṣuvān</s> (solstice day), [with] a twenty-one-fold [stoma]. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
[It belongs] neither to the first half nor to the latter half. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
The <s>svara-sāmans</s> and <s>ṣaḍahas</s> of the latter half are reversed. — (sattra: gavāmayana)

After the <s>svara-sāman</s>, the <s>viśvajit</s>, the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>, three <s>abhiplavas</s> — making the seventh [month] short by a two-night [period]. Then with <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>-headed four <s>abhiplavas</s>, they undergo four months. — (sattra: gavāmayana)

Then they assemble the last [month]. Three <s>abhiplavas</s>, <s>Go</s> [and] <s>Āyuṣī</s>, the <s>daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite) — the seventh [month] is completed with the observance and <s>udayanīya</s> (concluding offering). — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Thus indeed the latter half with a single assemblage. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Now [the version] with double assemblage. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
The observance and <s>udayanīya</s> [belong] to the last [month]. The <s>Go</s> [and] <s>Āyuṣī</s> [belong] to the seventh [month]. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Or they may separate the <s>Go</s> and <s>Āyuṣī</s>. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
The <s>Go</s> [day comes] immediately after the <s>viśvajit</s>. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
The <s>Āyuṣa</s> [day comes] just before the <s>daśarātra</s>. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Or alternatively, after the <s>viśvajit</s>, making the seventh a pressing-month, they may extract the <s>Go</s> [and] <s>Āyuṣī</s> and the <s>daśarātra</s>. — (sattra: gavāmayana)

Or alternatively, the days of the latter half would simply be reversed — the <s>ṣaḍahas</s> would be in direct order; or the <s>ṣaḍahas</s> would be reversed, and the days in direct order. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Thus [ends] the <s>Gavāmayana</s>. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
Or all the <s>ṣaḍahas</s> may be <s>abhiplavas</s>, they may be <s>abhiplavas</s>. — (sattra: gavāmayana)
By [the description of] the <s>Gavāmayana</s>, the <s>Ādityānām Ayana</s> (course of the <s>Ādityas</s>) is explained. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)
But all the <s>abhiplavas</s> are nine-fold and fifteen-fold. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)
And of the middle nine months, [the days are in] <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> [arrangement], excluding the sixth, seventh, and last [months]. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)
And the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s> (pressing for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) and <s>Indra-stuti</s> (praise of <s>Indra</s>) [take] the place of <s>abhijit</s> and <s>viśvajit</s>. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)

And in the place of the last two <s>abhiplavas</s> of the seventh month, a nine-fold extended <s>daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite), and <s>udbhid</s> (bursting) and <s>balabhid</s> (strength-breaking) [days]. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)
And of the last month, at the beginning, having extracted three <s>abhiplavas</s>, the middle of those would then be <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>-middle [arrangement]. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)
The <s>daśarātra</s> is contracted. — (sattra: ādityānām ayana)
By [the description of] the <s>Ādityānām Ayana</s>, the <s>Aṅgirasām Ayana</s> (course of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>) is explained. — (sattra: aṅgirasām ayana)
But the <s>abhiplava</s> (repeated six-day) [rites have] nine-fold <s>stomas</s> (chants). — (sattra: Aṅgirasām Ayana)
The <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) and following [rites constitute] the first five months of the first half. — (sattra: Aṅgirasām Ayana)
But four [months] of the second [half], ending with the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>, beginning from the eighth. — (sattra: Aṅgirasām Ayana)
And the three six-day [rites] at the beginning of the last month — they too should end with the <s>pṛṣṭhya</s>. — (sattra: Aṅgirasām Ayana)
The first two should be <s>abhiplavas</s>. — (sattra: Aṅgirasām Ayana)
The <s>Ayana</s> (year-long session) of <s>Dṛtivātavat</s>. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
The opening is an <s>Atirātra</s>. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)

With the nine-fold [stoma] for a month; with the fifteen-fold for a month; with the seventeen-fold for a month; with the twenty-one-fold for a month; with the twenty-seven-fold for a month; with the thirty-three-fold for a month. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
An observance [day is performed] in place of the <s>viṣuvat</s> (solstice day). — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
With these same months in reverse order, the second half. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
The closing is an <s>Atirātra</s>. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
The two <s>Atirātras</s> belong to these same days. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
Furthermore, even in other [sattras], when there is a time-filling [requirement] with prescribed [days], the concluding form is fixed. — (sattra: Dṛtivātavat Ayana)
The <s>Ayana</s> of the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s> (cup-drinkers). — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
They remain consecrated for a month. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
In that month, they purchase the <s>soma</s>. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
Their <s>upasads</s> (approach offerings) are twelve. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
Having bound the <s>soma</s>, having removed the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk rite) vessels — or having bound [them] — they offer the <s>agnihotra</s> for a month. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
They sacrifice with the <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon offerings) for a month. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
With the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (All-Gods offering) for a month. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
With the <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s> for a month. With the <s>Sākamedhas</s> for a month. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
With the <s>Śunāsīrīya</s> for a month. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)

On the day when the month is complete, on that day, having concluded the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering), having performed the preliminary rites beginning with the fire-carrying-forward, or the concluding rites beginning with the fire-removal, and the preparatory rites of the overnight [vigil], on the next day they should press [the soma]. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)

Some indeed perform [the pressing] immediately after the <s>upasads</s> alone, since it is observed that they call the pressing months beginning with the <s>agnihotra</s> the soma-months. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
That is not proper. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
For the fire-carrying-forward is for the sake of the animal [sacrifice], and that [animal sacrifice] is the occasion for the pressing on the next day. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)

And there would be a defect in the procedure of carrying [the fire] beyond, for the <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon offerings); likewise for the <s>agnihotra</s>. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)

The <s>sadas</s> (seat of priests), <s>havirdhāna</s> (soma-cart shed), <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-kindler's hearth), <s>Agnīṣoma-praṇayana</s> (carrying forward of the <s>Agni-Soma</s> fire), and the taking of the <s>vasatīvarī</s> (overnight waters) — these are for the sake of the animal [sacrifice]; some [say] for the sake of the pressing. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
Both the time and the attributes [belong to that purpose]. — (sattra: Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana)
